rows.original: [var0 |As you make time across the frozen waste, your exploration's cut short by the sound of a bird screaming out over the valley of the rift, the dissonant sound carrying swiftly through the shrill air. This is swiftly followed by the sight of a gigantic bird taking off from one of the nearby cliffs — a creature about twice to thrice your height and proportions to match, snowy white in color save for the crystalline clear nature of its beak, talons and guard feathers. It dives towards [party.combatNames] at breakneck speed, its intentions clear as it pulls into a stoop and clears what might be an hour's worth of walking for you in the blink of an eye. Drawing your [pc.weapon], you [party.hasCompanions |shout to [party.compNames] to be ready and ]prepare to fend off the predator — if it's but a wild beast, perhaps you can convince it that as much of a morsel as you might be, you're not worth the effort. That hope dries up like thin spit on a hot stove as the bird draws closer and you spy someone seated atop its back on a saddle: a haughty-looking, fine featured bird-man, his feathers blue and white to complement the bone and gold jewelry that adorns his body and the crystal-tipped spear clenched in one hand. As the snow roc makes a circling pass above you, he spreads his wings and vaults off his mount's back elegantly, the business end of his spear hurtling towards you[party.has Etheryn | and Ryn ]. "[party.has etheryn |[pc.ra elf |Elves |Elf ] |Elf ]!" he screeches in broken Belharan, his voice shattering the frigid air and your eardrums alike. "You have overstayed your welcome here! Run back and hide in your city where you belong!" There's no time to lose. [party.has etheryn |Catching Ryn by the shoulder and pulling her down as well, y |Y ]ou throw yourself to the ground face-first into a snowbank as both roc and rider swoop over you, talons extended. The icy beat of their wings passes over your back as they narrowly miss you by a hair's breadth, pull away, and circle around for another pass at you — and they don't intend to let you dodge out of the way this time. [party.has etheryn |"Surely this must be some sort of mistake!" Ryn calls out as she pulls herself to her feet and readies her [etheryn.weapon], coughing and spluttering. "Can't we talk this through?" |Now this has to be some kind of mistake! Can't you just calm down a bit, talk this out and maybe — ] "We have talked for two centuries, and each time you elves have reneged on your previous promises. Blame your queens for being perfidious liars — if you are as innocent as you purport yourself to be, then the blame rests squarely on their shoulders! If you will not leave, then I will send you out, and teach you to stay out!" So much for diplomacy, this one's implacable. Seeing the bird-man and his mount dive for you another time, lightning crackling on the tip of the former's crystal spear, you ready your [pc.weapon] and prepare to give battle.[party.has etheryn | Ryn seems less sure about all of this, swallowing hard, but alas, conflict is inevitable. ] It's a fight! |As you make time across the frozen waste, your exploration's cut short by the sound of a bird screaming out over the valley of the rift, the dissonant sound carrying swiftly through the shrill air. This is swiftly followed by the sight of a gigantic bird taking off from one of the nearby cliffs — a creature about twice to thrice your height and proportions to match, snowy white in color save for the crystalline clear nature of its beak, talons and guard feathers. It dives towards [party.combatNames] at breakneck speed, its intentions clear as it pulls into a stoop and clears what might be an hour's worth of walking for you in the blink of an eye. Drawing your [pc.weapon], you [party.hasCompanions |shout to [party.compNames] to be ready ] and await to fend off the predator — if it's but a wild beast, perhaps you can convince it that as much of a morsel as you might be, you're not worth the effort. Then, the unexpected happens. As the snow roc closes the distance, you spy a rider atop its back on a saddle — an elegant, fine featured bird-man, his feathers blue and white to complement the bone and gold jewelry that adorns his lithe body and the crystal-tipped spear clenched in one hand. The gigantic bird slows as it approaches you, pulling into a circle as it passes above your heads, and the bird-man leaps from its back, spreading his wings as he cartwheels through the air to land on his feet in the snow next to you. The jewelry aside, he's wearing nothing save for what looks to be a cloak of his own feathers, pulled tightly about his own body, and he holds the tip of his spear downwards non-threateningly as he approaches you. Moments later, the roc lands a little distance away, looking nonplussed and starting to preen itself. "Hail, [pc.race]," he says, his Belharan broken and halting. "What brings you here to this place? Are you lost?[pc.ra frostmander arcticfox | | You do not seem to be very suited to the cold, nor prepared for such. ] If you are, I can guide you out — the rift is a harsh mistress, and unforgiving to those not born of her embrace." [pc.isDK |It's not any business of his. You're not in his way, so he has no reason to be hassling you like this. You know where you're going, will be perfectly fine by yourself and have business to attend to, so if he doesn't mind getting out of your way you can part peacefully |While you appreciate his concern of guidance back out of the rift, you're not lost. In fact, you're here with a purpose, and you're going to see it through — so far, you've managed to handle the hazards of the rift just fine, so there's no need for him to worry. Now, if he would please step aside so that you can continue peacefully on your way, that would be very kind of him ]. The bird-man doesn't budge. "These lands are safe, or as safe for your kind as they will ever be... for now. How long will your business take you here?" To be honest, you don't know. Taking care of the demon cult and tying up all the loose ends you find might take a good long while depending on how quickly these things go. "I say this because there will be war within the rift soon, perhaps within the week, perhaps a little later, but it is inevitable at this point. Regardless, it is not a safe place for outsiders to be, regardless of what business they may have here. You would do well to not overstay the welcome the rift extends to you, [pc.race] — she quickly tires of carrying the same person on her back overlong." All right, you get the point. Seriously, you wouldn't be up here if you didn't at least know some of the risks, and given that you're the Champion of Winter, you think you can handle yourself well enough even in this bleak landscape. Those last words give the bird-man pause. His talon-fingers tighten about the bone haft of his spear, his stance widens in a barely perceptible manner as muscles tense under the feathers. Even the roc appears more agitated now, perhaps sensing its master's discomfort as it claws at the snow and ice with a foot. In the blink of an eye, the atmosphere has soured significantly, dark clouds gathering on the horizon just out of sight. "What did you say you were?" The bird-man's tone of voice leaves no doubt that he knows very well what you said, and the question is less a request for clarification and more... something else. The Champion of Winter. "More than two and a half centuries ago, a Champion of Winter came from the elf-city to the south. Now, another one emerges from that place... nothing good ever follows the likes of you." He levels his spear at you. "No friend of the elves is a friend to the avanai, or any of the rift's peoples. Get gone!" With that, the bird-man — the avanai, you suppose — vaults into the air with wings spread, the crystal tip of the spear crackling with lightning and aimed at you. You have barely enough time to [party.hasCompanions |rally [party.compNames] and ]draw your [pc.weapon] before you're fighting a flurry of icy fury and feathers, the snow roc charging into battle alongside its master. It's a fight! ]
rows.translation: [var0 |当你艰难地穿越这片冰封的荒原时，突然，一只鸟在裂谷上空发出尖锐的叫声，这刺耳的声音迅速在空气中传播开来，打断了你的探索。紧接着，你看到一只巨大的鸟从附近的悬崖上飞了起来——这只鸟的体型大约是你的两到三倍，体型与比例也与之相称，它的身体呈雪白色，唯有喙、爪子和防护羽毛呈现出晶莹剔透的颜色。它朝着你的方向俯冲了过来…… [party.combatNames] 它以惊人的速度前进，目的十分明确——它迅速弯下身子，瞬间就跨越了原本可能需要你步行一小时才能走完的距离。 拉着你…… [pc.weapon]你 [party.hasCompanions |向……致敬 [party.compNames] 做好准备，随时待命。 ]准备好抵御这个捕食者吧——如果它只是一只野兽，或许你可以让它相信：尽管你只是个小不点，但根本不值得它费这个劲。然而，当那只鸟逐渐靠近时，这种希望就像热炉子上冒出的薄薄一层水汽一样瞬间消失了。因为你看到，有人坐在它的背上，骑在它的背上：一个神情傲慢、相貌出众的鸟人，他的羽毛呈蓝白色，与身上佩戴的骨制和金制饰品相得益彰，而他手中紧握着一把尖端镶有水晶的长矛。 当雪岩鸟在你头顶盘旋时，它展开双翼，优雅地从坐骑背上跃下，其长矛的尖端直刺向你。[party.has Etheryn | 还有瑞恩 ]. "[party.has etheryn |[pc.ra elf |精灵们 |精灵 ] |精灵 ]啊！”他用断断续续的贝尔哈兰语尖叫道，声音震破了寒冷的空气，也震得你的耳膜发疼。“你们在这里已经待得太久了！快跑回去，回到属于你们的城市里去躲起来吧！” 没有时间可以浪费了。 [party.has etheryn |抓住瑞恩的肩膀，也将她拉了下来。 |Y ]当你看到岩鸟和它的骑手俯冲下来，利爪伸向你的时候，你只能面朝下扑进雪堆里。它们冰冷的翅膀划过你的背部，却仅仅差那么一点点就击中你了。它们随即拉开距离，开始盘旋，准备再次攻击——这一次，它们绝对不会让你有逃脱的机会。 [party.has etheryn |肯定这是某种误会吧！”莱恩边说边站起身来，准备采取行动。 [etheryn.weapon]我们能不能好好谈谈这件事？”他边说边咳嗽着，声音断断续续的。 |这肯定是什么误会吧！你能不能先冷静下来，把事情好好谈一谈，或许…… ] 我们已经进行了两个世纪的谈判，而每次你们精灵族都会违背之前的承诺。把责任归咎于你们的女王们吧——她们就是些背信弃义的骗子！如果你们真如自己所声称的那样无辜，那么所有的责任都应该由她们来承担！如果你们不肯离开，那么我就亲自把你们赶出去，让你们明白什么叫做…… 留下 出去！” 外交手段已经失败了，这个人根本不会让步。看到那个鸟人和他的坐骑再次朝你冲过来，看到鸟人手中的水晶长矛尖端闪烁着闪电，你立刻做好了准备…… [pc.weapon] 准备投入战斗吧。[party.has etheryn | 瑞恩对此似乎不太确定，他艰难地咽了口唾沫，但可惜，冲突是不可避免的。 ] 这是一场激烈的战斗！ |当你艰难地穿越这片冰封的荒原时，突然，一只鸟在裂谷上空发出尖锐的叫声，这刺耳的声音迅速在空气中传播开来，打断了你的探索。紧接着，你看到一只巨大的鸟从附近的悬崖上飞了起来——这只鸟的体型大约是你的两到三倍，体型与比例也与之相称，它的身体呈雪白色，唯有喙、爪子和防护羽毛呈现出晶莹剔透的颜色。它朝着你的方向俯冲了下来…… [party.combatNames] 它以惊人的速度前进，目的十分明确——它迅速弯下身子，瞬间就跨越了原本可能需要你步行一小时才能走完的距离。把你…… [pc.weapon]你 [party.hasCompanions |向……致敬 [party.compNames] 做好充分准备 ] 然后，意想不到的事情发生了。当雪 roc逐渐靠近时，你看到它的背上坐着一个骑手——一个身材优雅、容貌俊美的鸟人，他的羽毛呈蓝白色，与佩戴在他结实身体上的骨制和金色饰品相得益彰，而他手中紧握着一把水晶尖端的长矛。 那只巨大的鸟在接近你的时候逐渐减速，然后在你的头顶上方划出一个圆圈飞过，紧接着，那个骑在鸟背上的男子跳了下来，他展开双翼，在空中翻滚着，最终稳稳地落在你身旁的雪地上。 除了那些珠宝之外，他身上什么也没穿，只披着一件似乎由自己的羽毛制成的斗篷，紧紧地裹在身上。当他向你走来时，他将长矛的矛尖向下握住，显得并不具有威胁性。片刻之后，那只巨鸟在稍远的地方降落下来，看起来有些不知所措，然后开始整理自己的羽毛。 致敬， [pc.race]他说，他的贝尔哈兰语说得断断续续、结结巴巴。“你为什么会来到这个地方？是迷路了吗？[pc.ra frostmander arcticfox | | 你似乎并不适合寒冷的环境，也没有为这样的环境做好准备。 ] 如果你是的话，我可以引导你离开——那裂隙是个残酷的存在，对于那些不是她所接纳的人，它绝不会宽恕他们。 [pc.isDK |这与他无关。你并没有妨碍到他，所以他没有理由这样纠缠你。你知道自己要去哪里，独自一人也会一切顺利，而且你还有自己的事情要处理。所以，如果他不介意别妨碍你的话，你们就可以和平地分开。 |虽然你很感激他关心你能否顺利走出那个裂隙，但实际上你并没有迷路。相反，你来到这里是有目的的，而且你一定会完成自己的目标——到目前为止，你已经成功应对了裂隙中的种种危险，所以他完全没有必要担心。现在，如果他能够让开道路，让你能够安心地继续前行，那将真是太好了。 ]那个鸟人一动不动。“这些地方很安全，至少对你们这类生物来说是目前最安全的了……不过你们要在这里待多久呢？” 说实话，你也说不准。处理那些恶魔崇拜组织以及解决所有遗留问题，可能需要相当长的时间，具体取决于这些事情进展的速度。 我这么说是因为，裂隙之中很快就会爆发战争——也许就在这一周内，也可能稍晚一些，但无论如何，这场战争已经不可避免了。对那些外来者来说，这里绝对不是一个安全的地方，无论他们来这里究竟有什么目的。 你最好不要过度占用别人给予你的好意。 [pc.race] ——长时间背同一个人在背上，她很快就会感到疲惫不堪。” 好吧，你明白我的意思了。说真的，如果你连这些风险都不了解，的话，你根本就不会站在这里。而既然你已经是冬季的冠军，你应该觉得自己有足够的能力应对这个严酷的环境吧。 最后那几句话让那个鸟人停下了动作。他的利爪紧紧抓住长矛的骨柄，站姿微微改变，羽毛下的肌肉开始紧绷。就连那只巨鸟也显得更加焦躁不安，它用一只足部在冰雪上抓挠，似乎察觉到了主人的不安。转眼间，气氛变得紧张起来，地平线上隐约出现了乌云。 你刚才说什么来着？”那个鸟人说话的肌肉度明显表明他非常清楚你说了什么，而这个问题与其说是在请求你澄清，不如说……是别的什么意思。 冬之冠军。 两个半世纪多年前，一位冬季勇士从南方的精灵之城而来。如今，又有一位这样的勇士从那里出现了……像你们这样的人，从来不会带来任何好事。”他将长矛对准了你。“凡是精灵的朋友，也就一定是avanai以及裂隙地带所有民族的朋友。 滚开！ 说着，那个鸟人——你大概应该称他为“阿瓦奈”——便张开双翼跃向空中，那支长矛的水晶尖端闪烁着闪电般的光芒，直直地指向你。你几乎没有任何时间可以反应…… [party.hasCompanions |集结 [party.compNames] 以及 ]拿出你的…… [pc.weapon] 在你面对一连串冰冷而猛烈的攻击之前，雪岩鸟就会与它的主人一起冲入战场。 这是一场激烈的战斗！ ]

rows.original: [rand |You have an ominous feeling in the pit of your stomach, the back of your neck tingles; your instincts scream danger at you and you waste no time in throwing yourself to the ground[party.hasCompanions |, pulling [party.compNames] along with you ]. Barely have you landed in the snow and ice before a massive presence darts in from behind you, talons closing about empty air; if not for your prescience, you might've very well been snatched up and off the ground by the roc diving at you. rows.original:
Defeated, the roc-rider sinks to one knee, using the haft of his spear to support himself. You're not having any of that, and step up to kick it out of his grasp and away from him. A quick glance at the avanai's bestial mount confirms that it's just as winded as its master is, the fight thoroughly beaten out of it. You cast a quick glance at your surroundings, but it looks like you're safe for now — the fight hasn't let anything else creep up upon you while you were occupied, so... 
    
    ...What now? One supposes you could just leave, or if you were so minded, do something else with this fine-figured bird-man while he's at your mercy...
rows.translation:
被击败后，那个骑着巨鸟的战士单膝跪地，用长矛的柄支撑着自己的身体。但你没有这样的机会——你迅速上前，一脚将长矛从他手中踢开，使其远离自己。你匆匆瞥了一眼那个骑鸟战士的坐骑，发现它和它的主人一样筋疲力尽，这场战斗已经让它们彻底耗尽了体力。你环顾四周，发现目前看来你是安全的——在你忙于应对战斗的时候，没有其他东西悄悄接近你……所以……
    
    ……现在该怎么办呢？或许你可以直接离开，或者如果你愿意的话，也可以利用这个身材优美的鸟人做点别的事情……

"
    Defeated, the roc-rider sinks to one knee, using the haft of his spear to support himself. You're not having any of that, and step up to kick it out of his grasp and away from him. A quick glance at the avanai's bestial mount confirms that it's just as winded as its master is, the fight thoroughly beaten out of it. You cast a quick glance at your surroundings, but it looks like you're safe for now — the fight hasn't let anything else creep up upon you while you were occupied, so... 
    
    ...What now? One supposes you could just leave, or if you were so minded, do something else with this fine-figured bird-man while he's at your mercy... 
    "

rows.original: The roc-rider scowls as you approach — or at least, given that he has a beak, you get the impression that he's doing the equivalent of such. His eyes dart to your [pc.weapon], perhaps expecting you to finish him and his mount off, but you put that away and crouch down beside him so that your gaze is level with his. The snow roc flutters with indignation and weakly tries to rise from the ice, but seeing that you're not being threatening, the avanai holds up a taloned hand and it stops in its tracks, chirping. Now then, you have some questions you want answered. "That fully depends on what you intend to ask." Even in defeat, the bird-man's voice is cold, melodious, haughty. You don't think it's intentional, though — it's just how he speaks Belharan, broken as it is. That's what happens when beaks speak words meant for lips... Well then, he doesn't need to worry. You're sure he'll be more than willing to answer your questions — starting off with exactly why he chose to attack you. "Should that not be obvious?" Maybe, maybe not. But with such situations, you really aren't inclined to play the guessing game and make assumptions. Now then, out with it. This isn't something he has any reason to keep to himself, is it? [party.has etheryn |The roc-rider turns his gaze towards Etheryn and bobs his chin at her. "There is your answer. She is a boer'alvar. We have had enough of her and her kind within the rift. They are to leave, or the Grand Alliance will chase them out; you travel with her, and any friend to an elf is no friend to the peoples of the rift |[pc.ra elf |The roc-rider holds your gaze with clear, glassy eyes. "There you have your answer. You are an elf. If you are genuinely asking this question in ignorance, perhaps you have not personally committed any crimes against the peoples of the rift, but that does not change anything. Elves have overstayed their welcome within the rift, and must leave or the Grand Alliance will drive them out. Perhaps it is some kind of injustice to you, but then if there were any good elves they were content to sit back and not impede their brethren while they reaped the fruits of the latter ravaging the land and ice of the rift |The roc-rider holds your gaze and glowers at you with clear, glassy eyes. "Word spreads fast — you are some Champion of Winter in that elf city to the south. That makes you a friend to the elves, and no friend to the elves is a friend to us, or any other peoples of the Grand Alliance. So long as you have pledged allegiance to the elves, it is our duty to drive you as their agent from our lands." ...Cute. You don't think that Ryn declaring you Champion of Winter is something that could be rescinded even if you wanted to, though. "That is not any particular concern of ours." Well, if that isn't just unpleasant. "It is the truth; one should not ask questions and then balk if they are unprepared for the answers that may be given ] ]. It is only by our mercy that we have decided to grant all elves a short grace period to leave peacefully before we forcibly expel them from the rift." Forcibly expel, huh. From what you've seen of the glacial rift's native peoples, they aren't as advanced as the elves in terms of technology and civilisation — most of their energies must be spent on survival. That, and the pale elves openly have Lumia on their side. Maybe that's what this Grand Alliance thing is all about... "Are you satisfied?" No, you still have more questions. What grievance do they have against the pale elves? You may have heard something of it yourself, but again, you want to get it from his point of view. "Two centuries ago, the elves came to save us from a great darkness from the south, led by a goddess of light at their head. And they did, after a fashion. But after the darkness was defeated, they did not return to their city as they had promised, instead choosing to establish a keep towards the east of the rift. "Even if it was the first promise that they broke, that in itself would not have been enough to anger us — perhaps they would have been good neighbors. But they were not. Time and again they have taken more and more of the mountain glaciers for their own, melting the ice with heat from the earth and collapsing the cliffs that our rocs nest on. They quell the storms that used to scream across the rift to make travel safe for them, but we need the blessing of the sky to live. As they dredge the glacial streams for metals, the resultant waters become fouled and impossible to drink — and what else is available, they claim for themselves. Time and again we have negotiated, they have promised, and those promises are broken because we are little more than tribal savages to the likes of them. "Enough is enough. The jotuns, selkies and siorcanna have their own problems with these elves, but these are the injustices that we avanai have suffered at the hands of the elves. They have outstayed their welcome, and the time for talking is over. A Grand Alliance of these peoples, the peoples of the ice and storms, has been formed to send [pc.ra elf |you back where you belong, elf. You |the elves back where they belong. They ] are no longer wanted nor needed here." [party.has etheryn |"There's been a change of command in the Winter City," Ryn begins, sounding like she's going to cry at any moment. "The queen has been ousted for consorting with demons and has fled the city. Maybe with a change in leadership, new negotiations — " "Twice the queen of the elves has changed, and yet nothing here has. Why would this be any different?" You place a hand on Ryn's shoulder and squeeze her gently. It's not as if this was anything she could have known or done anything about while Alissa was in power. It's not her fault. ] One way or another, this looks like a sticky situation. From the avanai's point of view, they have a legitimate case against Lumia and the pale elves — of course, assuming that this roc-rider isn't lying out of his beak. On the other hand, everything you went through in the Winter City has gone to show that the pale elves aren't bad people as a whole. This is something for Ryn to handle... and it might take a long, long time if it weren't for the fact that it's already been a long time and things are coming to a head now — Ryn's rule is getting off to a rocky start, that's for sure. Well, there's nothing else you can do about this for the moment, save perhaps hear out the other parties involved in this mess, both from the other members of this Grand Alliance and the Lumian pale elves. Perhaps if you even get a better picture of what's going on, you'll be able to help Ryn sort this mess out. For now, it'll be just fending off the infuriated denizens of the rift... The avanai sniffs and clicks his beak. "So. What else do you want to know, [pc.race]?" That's it... for now. You have your own business in the rift to attend to, and even if you wanted to get involved in all this you'd need to know more about the situation before you'd be able to act. So yes, that's all — he ought to get lost before you change your mind. The roc-rider doesn't need telling twice. He looks like he's still fuming — or maybe not, bird visages are really inscrutable when they want to be — and hobbles first for his spear, then for his mount. Both of them are too winded to fly, so they settle for limping away across the ice and snow in disgrace, side by side. That should be enough humiliation for him to not try another go at you anytime soon, although you can't say the same for the remaining bird-brains in the rift... ...Oh, whatever. The more you learn of this mess, the less you like it. You just wanted to deal with Tollus and his little cult, plus any of your private business within the rift without getting mixed up in all this — why does everything have to be so complicated?

rows.raw: " The roc-rider scowls as you approach — or at least, given that he has a beak, you get the impression that he's doing the equivalent of such. His eyes dart to your [pc.weapon], perhaps expecting you to finish him and his mount off, but you put that away and crouch down beside him so that your gaze is level with his. The snow roc flutters with indignation and weakly tries to rise from the ice, but seeing that you're not being threatening, the avanai holds up a taloned hand and it stops in its tracks, chirping. Now then, you have some questions you want answered. "That fully depends on what you intend to ask." Even in defeat, the bird-man's voice is cold, melodious, haughty. You don't think it's intentional, though — it's just how he speaks Belharan, broken as it is. That's what happens when beaks speak words meant for lips... Well then, he doesn't need to worry. You're sure he'll be more than willing to answer your questions — starting off with exactly why he chose to attack you. "Should that not be obvious?" Maybe, maybe not. But with such situations, you really aren't inclined to play the guessing game and make assumptions. Now then, out with it. This isn't something he has any reason to keep to himself, is it? [party.has etheryn |The roc-rider turns his gaze towards Etheryn and bobs his chin at her. "There is your answer. She is a boer'alvar. We have had enough of her and her kind within the rift. They are to leave, or the Grand Alliance will chase them out; you travel with her, and any friend to an elf is no friend to the peoples of the rift |[pc.ra elf |The roc-rider holds your gaze with clear, glassy eyes. "There you have your answer. You are an elf. If you are genuinely asking this question in ignorance, perhaps you have not personally committed any crimes against the peoples of the rift, but that does not change anything. Elves have overstayed their welcome within the rift, and must leave or the Grand Alliance will drive them out. Perhaps it is some kind of injustice to you, but then if there were any good elves they were content to sit back and not impede their brethren while they reaped the fruits of the latter ravaging the land and ice of the rift |The roc-rider holds your gaze and glowers at you with clear, glassy eyes. "Word spreads fast — you are some Champion of Winter in that elf city to the south. That makes you a friend to the elves, and no friend to the elves is a friend to us, or any other peoples of the Grand Alliance. So long as you have pledged allegiance to the elves, it is our duty to drive you as their agent from our lands." ...Cute. You don't think that Ryn declaring you Champion of Winter is something that could be rescinded even if you wanted to, though. "That is not any particular concern of ours." Well, if that isn't just unpleasant. "It is the truth; one should not ask questions and then balk if they are unprepared for the answers that may be given ] ]. It is only by our mercy that we have decided to grant all elves a short grace period to leave peacefully before we forcibly expel them from the rift." Forcibly expel, huh. From what you've seen of the glacial rift's native peoples, they aren't as advanced as the elves in terms of technology and civilisation — most of their energies must be spent on survival. That, and the pale elves openly have Lumia on their side. Maybe that's what this Grand Alliance thing is all about... "Are you satisfied?" No, you still have more questions. What grievance do they have against the pale elves? You may have heard something of it yourself, but again, you want to get it from his point of view. "Two centuries ago, the elves came to save us from a great darkness from the south, led by a goddess of light at their head. And they did, after a fashion. But after the darkness was defeated, they did not return to their city as they had promised, instead choosing to establish a keep towards the east of the rift. "Even if it was the first promise that they broke, that in itself would not have been enough to anger us — perhaps they would have been good neighbors. But they were not. Time and again they have taken more and more of the mountain glaciers for their own, melting the ice with heat from the earth and collapsing the cliffs that our rocs nest on. They quell the storms that used to scream across the rift to make travel safe for them, but we need the blessing of the sky to live. As they dredge the glacial streams for metals, the resultant waters become fouled and impossible to drink — and what else is available, they claim for themselves. Time and again we have negotiated, they have promised, and those promises are broken because we are little more than tribal savages to the likes of them. "Enough is enough. The jotuns, selkies and siorcanna have their own problems with these elves, but these are the injustices that we avanai have suffered at the hands of the elves. They have outstayed their welcome, and the time for talking is over. A Grand Alliance of these peoples, the peoples of the ice and storms, has been formed to send [pc.ra elf |you back where you belong, elf. You |the elves back where they belong. They ] are no longer wanted nor needed here." [party.has etheryn |"There's been a change of command in the Winter City," Ryn begins, sounding like she's going to cry at any moment. "The queen has been ousted for consorting with demons and has fled the city. Maybe with a change in leadership, new negotiations — " "Twice the queen of the elves has changed, and yet nothing here has. Why would this be any different?" You place a hand on Ryn's shoulder and squeeze her gently. It's not as if this was anything she could have known or done anything about while Alissa was in power. It's not her fault. ] One way or another, this looks like a sticky situation. From the avanai's point of view, they have a legitimate case against Lumia and the pale elves — of course, assuming that this roc-rider isn't lying out of his beak. On the other hand, everything you went through in the Winter City has gone to show that the pale elves aren't bad people as a whole. This is something for Ryn to handle... and it might take a long, long time if it weren't for the fact that it's already been a long time and things are coming to a head now — Ryn's rule is getting off to a rocky start, that's for sure. Well, there's nothing else you can do about this for the moment, save perhaps hear out the other parties involved in this mess, both from the other members of this Grand Alliance and the Lumian pale elves. Perhaps if you even get a better picture of what's going on, you'll be able to help Ryn sort this mess out. For now, it'll be just fending off the infuriated denizens of the rift... The avanai sniffs and clicks his beak. "So. What else do you want to know, [pc.race]?" That's it... for now. You have your own business in the rift to attend to, and even if you wanted to get involved in all this you'd need to know more about the situation before you'd be able to act. So yes, that's all — he ought to get lost before you change your mind. The roc-rider doesn't need telling twice. He looks like he's still fuming — or maybe not, bird visages are really inscrutable when they want to be — and hobbles first for his spear, then for his mount. Both of them are too winded to fly, so they settle for limping away across the ice and snow in disgrace, side by side. That should be enough humiliation for him to not try another go at you anytime soon, although you can't say the same for the remaining bird-brains in the rift... ...Oh, whatever. The more you learn of this mess, the less you like it. You just wanted to deal with Tollus and his little cult, plus any of your private business within the rift without getting mixed up in all this — why does everything have to be so complicated? "

rows.original: Gweyr is good to her word, leading you southwest along rocky paths and around snowdrifts — though she's clearly [a] [silly|absolute unit|beast of woman], the snowshoes she's wearing prevent her from sinking into the snow too deeply. The gray-furred wolfess is clearly used to traveling across and through snow with little problem, and the path she leaves in her wake eases your passage as well. Eventually, the air begins to warm — if marginally — as you approach the rift's southwest corner and the thermal vents; she leads you up a ridge and into a hole in the mountainside. Here, it's significantly warmer, and you soon see why; a crack further into the cave is filled with steaming water, heating the air as it slowly rises out of the cave mouth. It's good to get out of the cold, if only for a bit. "Make yoursel[party.hasCompanions |ves |f ] comfortable," the wolfess grunts. "Not many people ever drop by save for the avanai and jotuns for feathers and whalebone. Never saw a better whaler than a jotun." What about the elves? They live pretty close by with their sluicing operations. "I've got nothing they'd want to trade for," Gweyr replies. "Everything they need is hoisted up the glacier by those lifts of theirs." Huh. The wolfess leads you to a low table carved of bone, pulling up rolled-up pelts for [party.yall] she takes a stool for herself. "Now, [party.has quintillus |I'm being nice and giving the both of you a chance to explain yourselves. What has the lot of you tied up with this Tollus man?" On his part, Quin's drawn a cup of hot water from the spring and is soaking his fingers in it, still looking positively grumpy about the whole affair. "Go on, [pc.name]. Tell the nice lady that we aren't in Tollus's little gang." |if you don't mind me asking, what has [party.hasCompanions |the lot of ]you up here that you nearly caught your leg in one of my snares?" ] With little to lose and some time to burn — perhaps in the hope of turning this wolfess to your side as an ally — you launch into a brief explanation as to what happened that fateful night. Cait's arrival in the Frost Hound, the old temple, the cult, Tollus. You keep your story focused on the cult's activities, since this is what she's most interested in, and indeed Gweyr listens intently as you explain the corruption that went on in Harvest Valley through Tollus's control of the centaurs and what you did to resolve the situation.[party.has quintillus | When you're done, Quin briefly explains that you found him running from the cult in Harvest Valley, trying to desert from their fold, and how Garth and you eventually took him in. ] "Hm." [party.has cait |"It's true, I swear!" Cait pipes up from beside you. "Those creeps, they took Calla and... and we still haven't found her yet. But we're going to!" "Hmph. There, dear — I know full well what it's like to lose someone close to you." "She's not dead! If there's no body, I'm not going to accept that Calla's dead, so don't speak about her as if she is!!" ] Now, if she doesn't mind, it's time for her to introduce herself in this little give-and-take. What's the cult to her, and why does merely mentioning it raise her hackles that much? "They're the reason I'm up here. I thought I dealt with them more than a decade ago... broke most of their leadership and scattered them to the winds. Guess I was wrong." [party.has cait |"They may not have been broken, but they were certainly laying low," Cait pipes up. "While [pc.name] was out, I went around asking about the creeps and although no one really knew anything, they did note that people had been disappearing around the village and its environs every year." |She was, you guess, although they've been laying low. You remember that when Cait went around asking the people of Hawkethorne about the cult, no one really knew anything, but they did know that people had been disappearing around the village and its environs every year. ] "...My only regret is that I didn't get the chance to kill Tollus back then." You shake your head. Just who is she? "You've been putting up at the Frost Hound, haven't you?" To begin with, yes... Garth offered to let you stay free of charge indefinitely. You already have some idea of how all this is coming together, but you still have to say the words once more: just who is Gweyr? "Garth's my husband, silly."
rows.translation: 格温尔确实遵守了自己的承诺，她带领你们沿着崎岖的小路向西南方向前进，穿过积雪堆……不过很明显，她其实…… [a] [silly|绝对单位|女人中的猛兽]她脚上穿的雪鞋让她的身体不会陷入雪中太深。这只灰毛母狼显然已经习惯了在雪地中行走，而且她留下的足迹也为其他人提供了方便的通行路径。 当你逐渐接近裂隙的西南角以及那些热泉时，空气开始变暖——虽然只是略微升温而已。她带你沿着一条山脊前行，最终来到山坡上的一个洞穴中。在这里，温度明显更高了，你很快就能明白原因：洞穴深处有一条裂缝，里面充满了冒着热气的泉水，这些热水不断从洞口流出，从而使周围的空气逐渐变暖。 走出寒冷的环境，哪怕只是短暂的时间，也是件好事。 “好好享受吧……[party.hasCompanions |自己|f ] 很舒服，”母狼低声说道，“除了那些为了羽毛和鲸骨而来的阿瓦奈人和乔顿人之外，几乎没人会来这里。我从来没见过比乔顿人更出色的捕鲸者。” 那么精灵们呢？他们就住在附近，从事着他们的渔业活动。 我没有什么他们想要用来交换的东西，”格韦尔回答道，“他们所需要的所有东西都被那些升降设备运到了冰川上。” “嗯。” 那只女狼带你来到一张用骨头制成的低矮桌子旁，然后拉开了那些卷起来的毛皮…… [party.yall] 她拿了一把凳子坐下来。“现在， [party.has quintillus |我出于好意，给了你们两个人解释的机会。你们这些人到底和这个叫托卢斯的男人有什么关系？ 至于奎因，他则从泉水中取来一杯热水，正在把手指浸在里面，整个人看起来还是对这件事非常不满。“说吧，”他说道。 [pc.name]告诉那位好心的女士，我们并不属于托卢斯的小团队。 |如果你不介意我问的话，那么……是什么让事情变成了这样呢？ [party.hasCompanions |很多 ]就是你啊，差点被我的陷阱缠住腿吧？ ] 既然没什么可失去的，而且也有一些时间可以消耗——或许还抱着让这个女狼成为自己盟友的希望——你便简要解释了那个决定命运的夜晚发生了什么。凯特来到了霜猎犬号，那座古老的寺庙，还有那个邪教组织，以及托卢斯。 你将故事的重点放在那个邪教的组织活动上，因为这正是她最感兴趣的内容。事实上，当你讲述托卢斯如何控制半人马，从而导致收获谷发生了种种腐败行为，以及你是如何解决这些问题的时候，格韦尔也听得非常认真。[party.has quintillus | 当你完成这些事情后，奎因简要解释了你是如何在收获谷发现他正在逃离那个邪教组织，试图摆脱他们的控制，以及后来加斯和你是如何收留他的。 ] 嗯。 [party.has cait |真的，我发誓！”凯特在你身旁说道，“那些混蛋把卡拉带走了……我们至今还没有找到她，但我们一定会找到的！” “哼。亲爱的，我非常清楚失去身边亲近的人是什么感觉。” “她还没有…… 死了！ 如果没有尸体，我就不会承认卡拉已经死了，所以不要把她当作已经去世的人来谈论！！ ] 现在，如果她不介意的话，是时候让她在这个小小的互动中介绍一下自己了。对于她来说，这个“邪教”究竟意味着什么？为什么仅仅提到它就会让她如此恼火呢？ “他们就是我来到这里的原因。我原以为在十多年前就已经解决了他们的问题……摧毁了他们的大部分领导力，把他们分散得无处可寻。看来我错了。 [party.has cait |它们可能并没有被损坏，但肯定是被藏了起来，”凯特插话说，“在那个时候…… [pc.name] 当时外面下着雨，我就去周围打听那些奇怪的事情。虽然没人真正知道什么，但他们确实提到，每年都有人在这个村庄及其周边地区失踪。 |你可以猜到，她其实一直在暗中活动。你还记得当时凯特在鹰棘镇村里询问人们关于那个邪教组织的事情吧？其实没人真正知道什么，但他们确实知道，每年都有很多人在村子及其周边地区失踪。 ] ……我唯一后悔的是，当时没有机会杀死托卢斯。” 你摇了摇头。她到底是谁呢？ “你一直住在霜猎犬那里，对吧？” 嗯，确实如此……加斯提出让你免费住在那里，永远都不用离开。你大概已经猜到这一切背后的原因了，但还是得再问一次：格温尔到底是谁？ “加斯是我的丈夫，傻瓜。
rows.raw: " Gweyr is good to her word, leading you southwest along rocky paths and around snowdrifts — though she's clearly [a] [silly|absolute unit|beast of woman], the snowshoes she's wearing prevent her from sinking into the snow too deeply. The gray-furred wolfess is clearly used to traveling across and through snow with little problem, and the path she leaves in her wake eases your passage as well. Eventually, the air begins to warm — if marginally — as you approach the rift's southwest corner and the thermal vents; she leads you up a ridge and into a hole in the mountainside. Here, it's significantly warmer, and you soon see why; a crack further into the cave is filled with steaming water, heating the air as it slowly rises out of the cave mouth. It's good to get out of the cold, if only for a bit. "Make yoursel[party.hasCompanions |ves |f ] comfortable," the wolfess grunts. "Not many people ever drop by save for the avanai and jotuns for feathers and whalebone. Never saw a better whaler than a jotun." What about the elves? They live pretty close by with their sluicing operations. "I've got nothing they'd want to trade for," Gweyr replies. "Everything they need is hoisted up the glacier by those lifts of theirs." Huh. The wolfess leads you to a low table carved of bone, pulling up rolled-up pelts for [party.yall] she takes a stool for herself. "Now, [party.has quintillus |I'm being nice and giving the both of you a chance to explain yourselves. What has the lot of you tied up with this Tollus man?" On his part, Quin's drawn a cup of hot water from the spring and is soaking his fingers in it, still looking positively grumpy about the whole affair. "Go on, [pc.name]. Tell the nice lady that we aren't in Tollus's little gang." |if you don't mind me asking, what has [party.hasCompanions |the lot of ]you up here that you nearly caught your leg in one of my snares?" ] With little to lose and some time to burn — perhaps in the hope of turning this wolfess to your side as an ally — you launch into a brief explanation as to what happened that fateful night. Cait's arrival in the Frost Hound, the old temple, the cult, Tollus. You keep your story focused on the cult's activities, since this is what she's most interested in, and indeed Gweyr listens intently as you explain the corruption that went on in Harvest Valley through Tollus's control of the centaurs and what you did to resolve the situation.[party.has quintillus | When you're done, Quin briefly explains that you found him running from the cult in Harvest Valley, trying to desert from their fold, and how Garth and you eventually took him in. ] "Hm." [party.has cait |"It's true, I swear!" Cait pipes up from beside you. "Those creeps, they took Calla and... and we still haven't found her yet. But we're going to!" "Hmph. There, dear — I know full well what it's like to lose someone close to you." "She's not dead! If there's no body, I'm not going to accept that Calla's dead, so don't speak about her as if she is!!" ] Now, if she doesn't mind, it's time for her to introduce herself in this little give-and-take. What's the cult to her, and why does merely mentioning it raise her hackles that much? "They're the reason I'm up here. I thought I dealt with them more than a decade ago... broke most of their leadership and scattered them to the winds. Guess I was wrong." [party.has cait |"They may not have been broken, but they were certainly laying low," Cait pipes up. "While [pc.name] was out, I went around asking about the creeps and although no one really knew anything, they did note that people had been disappearing around the village and its environs every year." |She was, you guess, although they've been laying low. You remember that when Cait went around asking the people of Hawkethorne about the cult, no one really knew anything, but they did know that people had been disappearing around the village and its environs every year. ] "...My only regret is that I didn't get the chance to kill Tollus back then." You shake your head. Just who is she? "You've been putting up at the Frost Hound, haven't you?" To begin with, yes... Garth offered to let you stay free of charge indefinitely. You already have some idea of how all this is coming together, but you still have to say the words once more: just who is Gweyr? "Garth's my husband, silly." "

rows.original: Time passes slowly. [var0 |Given the trail rations you've brought with you, you break open a portion and share them with Gweyr — she's shown you her hospitality, so it's only proper that you return the favor in some measure. Judging by the smoked and salted strips of seal, whale and fish hanging up on the side of the cave, the sugared pastries and dried fruits within the travelers' food is welcome. |Given the camping supplies you've brought with you, you break open a portion and share them with Gweyr — she's shown you her hospitality, so it's only proper that you return the favor in some measure. Hard bread and biscuits along with reconstituted jerky might be tough on the palate for you, but judging by the smoked and salted strips of seal, whale and fish hanging up on the side of the cave, it's a change from what she usually gets. |Gweyr offers you simple food from what she has on hand — smoked and salted strips of seal, whale and fish hanging up on the side of the cave, all tough and with little in the way of flavor. There's also a simple squid stew bubbling in an old pot, but the sight of it is as unappetising as the smell that exudes with the steam. Most notably is that Gweyr doesn't cook with wood for fuel, but instead feeds the fire with what looks like black rocks with a sheen of fat on them. Not surprising, given that wood's in short supply up here. ] For being such a big wolfess, Gweyr eats surprisingly little; mostly watching you while you apply yourselves to the filling, if bland, food. "It was about fifteen, sixteen years ago," Gweyr says. "Four years since we settled Hawkethorne, three since Garth and I finished building the Frost Hound together. It... it wasn't so bad a retirement from being the captain of a mercenary company, to finally take the money that we'd put together and throw it into something worth building. It was a new village at the time, we were optimistic about how things would shake out in a place where people didn't know us, who we were, where we came from." Gwyn and Garret... "Somewhere between three to four at the time." Gweyr lets the pause stretch out uncomfortably, then clears her throat and continues. "All of us, we weren't more than a handful of families at the time — no more than four or five dozen people at most. People who were willing to brave the wilds and had nothing to lose, or were running away from something like Garth and I were. It wasn't a good life, but it wasn't a bad one either; it was a different kind of hardship than what being in a mercenary company was, but it's not as if we'd thought our lives would be all roses after leaving. It was a living, I guess. "And then the bastard Tollus came." So your encounter with him wasn't the first time he'd had his eye on Hawkethorne. Gweyr gives you a rueful smile and gets a faraway look in her eyes. "Given your description of him, he had fewer wrinkles back then. Looked less like a complete piece of shit, which was why they were able to convince some of the lads and lasses to join them; they were fed up with Sanders and his whole 'self-control' and 'abstinence' thing. Youthful rebellion or sheer contrariness, who knows? Tollus came in with sixty of his goons, demanded we billet them at our places while they fixed up the old temple up on the hill. Tried to take over the town, given how small we were and how half of the youths around wanted to listen to what he was saying. Even wanted to overthrow the baroness and become the ruler, given that she never really showed her face... said she'd be a pushover, given how she was cowering behind her walls while her fledgeling village was being annexed. "The people, they were scared. Neither Sanders nor Garth and I were, but Tollus had half the youths of the village on his side, and a whole bunch of flashy parlour tricks. Garth and Sanders were going to talk about what they were going to do, maybe go up to the castle to see what the baroness could do, rally some kind of resistance while talking around those of our own who were being taken in by the man and his words..." [party.has quin |"Sixteen years," Quin muses. "Didn't know the bastard had been doing this for that long. He may have had more hair then, but he still doesn't look that old; you don't have to be old to be a fugly creep." "Of course you weren't there," Gweyr mutters, "else you'd be dead." "You wolves sure know how to hold a grudge, don't you?" "It's why we invented the weregeld," the wolfess replies gruffly. "But maybe here and now, it's just me. Just be sure to repent, little bunny, and repent good and hard. Because there might be someone like me out there looking for you, for what you did while you were in with that lot." ] You clear your throat in a bid to get the conversation moving again. So what happened after that? Presumably they must've chased Tollus and his posse away, at least for a while. "It was a couple of weeks into this mess... then one of the village girls disappeared. They covered their tracks pretty well, but River said he saw Tollus and his goons taking her up the hill to the old temple. I didn't know what they were about, but my gut told me it wasn't good. Sanders asked me for help, so I took my sword and my staff and went out after them." There was a portal? "I didn't get that far, so I don't know." A bitter chuckle. "They were waiting for me at the foot of the mountain trail, in full view of the gate. The village boys and girls who'd taken up with Tollus, I could tell that they weren't themselves. Controlled, mesmerised, possessed, whatever you want to call it. Tollus was using them as meatshields, forcing Sanders and me to have to get through my own in order to reach him. He thought I wouldn't have the stomach to do it, and I'd turn back home with my tail between my legs. "He didn't know me, of course. Those kids threw themselves at me without caring for themselves, so I butchered them all. They weren't trained and whatever hold Tollus had on them was dulling their senses and reactions, so it was a simple matter to cut them all down two or three at a time. There must've been a dozen of them, then his head crony Leold came at me — a bit less worthless than the rest, but still easy meat. I tore him apart, and that was when Tollus's panic turned to fucking terror. Bastard shat his pants as he took to his heels — I think he was considering using the girl he'd captured as a hostage, but after seeing what I'd done to his meatshields he didn't doubt that I'd kill her too just to get at him." There's a heavy silence that hangs in the air. He got away. Gweyr nods. "He got away. River freed the girl, and when I turned around, everyone had gathered at the gate, cowering behind the palisades and staring at me like they didn't know who to be more afraid of, Tollus or me. I didn't blame them, returned the girl... but even if they'd fallen into bad company, even if they weren't themselves any more, those were the sons and daughters of maybe a third of the village that I'd just chopped into meaty chunks without blinking, and then there was the matter of Tollus's head goon who I'd ripped in two before their eyes. Of course they'd be scared of me, even if I saved them and the girl. "No good deed goes unpunished, [pc.name]. I single-handedly saved them all from being slaves to some madman in a robe, and there and then Sanders tells me to walk the ice, else they'd lynch me. I... don't blame them for what they did, I'd have been afraid of myself too after seeing what I did. I would've been resentful if it were my Gwyn and Garret who'd been killed, even if they weren't themselves anymore; I wouldn't be able to look myself in the eye. But even so, to realize that only my husband, River and even Sanders, in a way, stood by me while the rest of Hawkethorne was willing to throw me to the wolves, I couldn't help but feel a deep disgust for the lot of them. I guess leading my own mercenary company for so long had spoiled me, made me expect things of people that most folk don't have. "The point of sending you to walk the ice is to kill you, [pc.name]; you're meant to keep on walking further and further north until the cold takes you. A way to kill you while maintaining the illusion of keeping one's hands clean. But as you can see, I didn't die. I wasn't about to let myself. I've hunted Tollus for all these years... and now he and his ilk wind up on my doorstep. "You're right, [pc.name]. Those snares weren't meant for rabbits. They're meant for people. You can guess who."
rows.translation: 时间过得很慢。 [var0 |考虑到你带上了这些野战口粮，你应该拆开一部分分给格韦尔——她已经对你表现出了热情好客，因此你理应以同样的方式回报她。从洞穴壁面上悬挂着的那些熏制或腌制的海豹肉、鲸肉和鱼肉，以及旅行者们携带的含糖糕点与干果来看，这些食物确实非常受欢迎。 |考虑到你带了这些露营用品，你不妨拆开一部分分给格韦尔吧——她已经对你表现出了热情好客，因此你也应该以同样的方式回报她。虽然硬面包、饼干以及重新加工制成的肉干可能不太合你的口味，但看看洞穴壁面上悬挂着的那些熏制过的海豹肉、鲸肉和鱼肉，就会知道这些食物与她平时吃的东西截然不同。 |格温尔用她手头现有的食材为你准备了一些简单的食物——那些挂在洞穴壁上的熏制和盐腌的海豹肉、鲸肉和鱼肉，全都质地坚韧，几乎没有什么味道。还有一个用旧锅煮着的简单鱿鱼汤，但它的样子和散发出来的气味一样，让人提不起食欲。 最值得注意的是，格温尔并不会用木材作为燃料来烹饪，而是使用一些表面带有脂肪光泽的黑色岩石来生火。考虑到这里的木材非常稀缺，这一点也就不足为奇了。 ] 作为一只如此庞大的母狼，格温尔吃的东西却出奇地少；它大多时候只是静静地观察你们，而你们却在吃那些虽然味道可能并不鲜美，但却很充饥的食物。 “那是大约十五、十六年前的事了，”格温尔说道，“在我们搬到鹰棘镇定居已经四年了，而加思和我一起完成建造‘霜犬酒馆’也已经是三年前的事了。 作为一支雇佣兵队伍的队长，退出这一角色其实也没那么糟糕。我们把积攒的钱用来建设一些有意义的东西——当时那只是一个新建的村庄，对于在一个人们不认识我们、不知道我们是谁、也不知道我们来自哪里的地方，事情会如何发展，我们其实抱有乐观的态度。" 格温和加勒特…… “当时，人数大概在三到四个人之间。”格温尔让这个停顿持续了一会儿，显得有些尴尬，然后清了清嗓子继续说道：“那时候，我们所有人加起来也不过是几户家庭而已——最多也就四五十个人而已。 那些愿意冒险闯荡、已经没有什么可失去的人，或者像加斯和我那样为了逃避某些事情而离开的人。这样的生活并不美好，但也不算糟糕；它与在雇佣兵队伍中生活的艰辛有所不同，但我们当初离开时，并没有认为自己的未来会一片光明。 我想，那简直就像是一个活生生的生命体。 然后那个混蛋托卢斯出现了。” 所以，你与他的相遇，并不是他第一次盯上鹰棘镇了。 格温尔露出懊悔的笑容，眼神也变得恍惚起来。 根据你对他的描述，那时候他的皱纹还少一些，看起来也不那么像个彻头彻尾的混蛋。正因为如此，他们才能够说服一些年轻人和女孩加入他们；那些人和女孩已经受够了桑德斯以及他那一套“自我控制”和“禁欲”的说辞。 是青春期的叛逆，还是纯粹的故意违抗？谁又能知道呢？托卢斯带着六十个打手部来到了这里，要求我们让他们住在我们的住处，同时让他们去修缮山上的那座旧寺庙。由于我们的人数很少，而且周围有一半的年轻人都愿意听他的话，所以他试图控制整个小镇。 甚至还想推翻女男爵，自己成为统治者——毕竟她从来都没有真正露面过……人们原本以为她会是个容易对付的对象，毕竟当她那刚刚建立起来的村庄被吞并时，她只是躲在城墙后面瑟瑟发抖而已。 那些人们，他们都害怕了。桑德斯、加斯和我都没有害怕，但托卢斯已经拉拢了村里一半的年轻人站在他那一边，而且他还掌握着许多花哨的表演技巧。加斯和桑德斯打算商量接下来该怎么做，也许会去城堡看看女男爵能提供什么帮助，同时努力说服那些已经被那个人和他的言辞影响而加入他们阵营的人，让他们重新站到我们这一边…… [party.has quin |十六年啊，”奎因沉思道，“真没想到那个混蛋竟然干了这种事这么久。那时候他的头发可能还多一些，但现在的样子…… 那个 年纪大并不意味着你就一定会变成一个丑陋可怕的怪物。” “你当然当时不在场，”格温尔低声说道，“否则你早就死了。” “你们这些狼族，确实很会记仇，不是吗？这就是我们发明‘赎罪金’的原因，”女狼粗声粗气地回答道，“但也许现在，只有我在寻找你。小兔子，你一定要好好忏悔，深刻地忏悔。因为可能还有像我这样的人，在外面寻找你——寻找你在那些人中间时所做的一切。" ] 你清了清嗓子，试图让谈话重新继续下去。那么之后发生了什么呢？想必他们一定把托卢斯和他的那些人赶走了，至少是暂时把他们赶走了。 “这件事发生已经有几周了。然后，村里的一个女孩消失了。她们试图很好地隐藏自己的行踪，但里弗说他看到托卢斯和他的手部下把那女孩带上了山，去了那座古老的寺庙。我不知道他们到底想做什么，但我的直觉告诉我，这绝不是什么好事。 桑德斯向我求助，于是我拿上剑和法杖，跟着他们出发了。 有一个传送门？ “我还没走到那里，所以不知道。”他苦涩地笑了笑，“他们在山路的尽头等着我，就在传送门的正下方。那些加入了Tollus的村里的男孩和女孩们，我看得出来，他们已经不再是以前的他们了。 被控制了，着迷了，被附身了——无论你想用什么词来形容。托卢斯把他们当作肉盾，迫使桑德斯和我必须突破这些障碍才能接近他。他以为我没有勇气这么做，会夹着尾巴逃回家去。 他当然不认识我。那些孩子不顾自己的安危冲向我，所以我把他们全都解决了。他们没有受过任何训练，而Tollus对他们的控制让他们的感官和反应能力变得迟钝，所以一次杀死两三个对他们来说根本不是什么难事。 他们大概有十几个人，然后他的心腹莱奥德冲了过来——比起其他那些人，他还算有点用处，但依然是个容易对付的目标。我把他撕成了碎片，就在那时，托卢斯的恐慌彻底变成了恐惧。那个混蛋吓得屁滚尿流，拔腿就跑；我猜他本来想用被他抓来的那个女孩当人质，但看到我对他的手部下们做了什么之后，他肯定不再怀疑：只要能抓住我，我也会杀了那个女孩的。" 空气中弥漫着重型的寂静。 他逃走了。 格韦尔点了点头：“他逃走了。里弗救出了那个女孩，而当我转过身来时，所有人都聚集在门口，躲在栅栏后面，盯着我看，似乎不知道该更害怕托卢斯还是我。 我并没有责怪他们，把那个女孩送了回去……但即便他们陷入了不良的圈子，即便他们已经不再是从前的自己了，可那些人毕竟还是这个村庄中大约三分之一人的子女啊。而我，却毫不犹豫地将他们一个个杀死了。更何况，还有那个为托卢斯效力的暴徒，我也在他们眼前将他撕成了两半。 他们当然会害怕我，即使是我救了他们和那个女孩。 没有善举会不受惩罚， [pc.name]我独自将他们从那个穿着长袍的疯子的手部中解救出来，就在那时，桑德斯却命令我在冰面上行走，否则他们就会把我 lynch。我……并不怪他们的所作所为，因为看到自己所做的事情之后，我也会害怕自己的。 如果被杀的是我的格温和加勒特，即使他们已经不再是原来的他们了，我也会感到愤恨不已，我根本无法面对自己。但即便如此，当我意识到在鹰棘镇的所有人中，只有我的丈夫、里弗，甚至在某种程度上还有桑德斯站在我身边，而其他人却都愿意把我抛弃时，我对他们所有人都感到无比的厌恶。 我想，长期领导自己的雇佣兵团队已经让我养成了某些习惯，让我对别人抱有了一些大多数人都不具备的期望。 “派你去冰原上执行任务，其实就是为了让你死。 [pc.name]你本应该一直向北走，直到寒冷将你吞噬。这是一种既能杀死你，又能让人保持清白的手部段。但你们看到的，我并没有死。我绝不会让自己死。这些年来，我一直在追捕托卢斯……而现在，他和他的同伙们，竟然出现在我的家门口。 “你说得对， [pc.name]那些陷阱并不是用来捉兔子的，而是用来捉人的。你应该能猜到是谁吧。
rows.raw: " Time passes slowly. [var0 |Given the trail rations you've brought with you, you break open a portion and share them with Gweyr — she's shown you her hospitality, so it's only proper that you return the favor in some measure. Judging by the smoked and salted strips of seal, whale and fish hanging up on the side of the cave, the sugared pastries and dried fruits within the travelers' food is welcome. |Given the camping supplies you've brought with you, you break open a portion and share them with Gweyr — she's shown you her hospitality, so it's only proper that you return the favor in some measure. Hard bread and biscuits along with reconstituted jerky might be tough on the palate for you, but judging by the smoked and salted strips of seal, whale and fish hanging up on the side of the cave, it's a change from what she usually gets. |Gweyr offers you simple food from what she has on hand — smoked and salted strips of seal, whale and fish hanging up on the side of the cave, all tough and with little in the way of flavor. There's also a simple squid stew bubbling in an old pot, but the sight of it is as unappetising as the smell that exudes with the steam. Most notably is that Gweyr doesn't cook with wood for fuel, but instead feeds the fire with what looks like black rocks with a sheen of fat on them. Not surprising, given that wood's in short supply up here. ] For being such a big wolfess, Gweyr eats surprisingly little; mostly watching you while you apply yourselves to the filling, if bland, food. "It was about fifteen, sixteen years ago," Gweyr says. "Four years since we settled Hawkethorne, three since Garth and I finished building the Frost Hound together. It... it wasn't so bad a retirement from being the captain of a mercenary company, to finally take the money that we'd put together and throw it into something worth building. It was a new village at the time, we were optimistic about how things would shake out in a place where people didn't know us, who we were, where we came from." Gwyn and Garret... "Somewhere between three to four at the time." Gweyr lets the pause stretch out uncomfortably, then clears her throat and continues. "All of us, we weren't more than a handful of families at the time — no more than four or five dozen people at most. People who were willing to brave the wilds and had nothing to lose, or were running away from something like Garth and I were. It wasn't a good life, but it wasn't a bad one either; it was a different kind of hardship than what being in a mercenary company was, but it's not as if we'd thought our lives would be all roses after leaving. It was a living, I guess. "And then the bastard Tollus came." So your encounter with him wasn't the first time he'd had his eye on Hawkethorne. Gweyr gives you a rueful smile and gets a faraway look in her eyes. "Given your description of him, he had fewer wrinkles back then. Looked less like a complete piece of shit, which was why they were able to convince some of the lads and lasses to join them; they were fed up with Sanders and his whole 'self-control' and 'abstinence' thing. Youthful rebellion or sheer contrariness, who knows? Tollus came in with sixty of his goons, demanded we billet them at our places while they fixed up the old temple up on the hill. Tried to take over the town, given how small we were and how half of the youths around wanted to listen to what he was saying. Even wanted to overthrow the baroness and become the ruler, given that she never really showed her face... said she'd be a pushover, given how she was cowering behind her walls while her fledgeling village was being annexed. "The people, they were scared. Neither Sanders nor Garth and I were, but Tollus had half the youths of the village on his side, and a whole bunch of flashy parlour tricks. Garth and Sanders were going to talk about what they were going to do, maybe go up to the castle to see what the baroness could do, rally some kind of resistance while talking around those of our own who were being taken in by the man and his words..." [party.has quin |"Sixteen years," Quin muses. "Didn't know the bastard had been doing this for that long. He may have had more hair then, but he still doesn't look that old; you don't have to be old to be a fugly creep." "Of course you weren't there," Gweyr mutters, "else you'd be dead." "You wolves sure know how to hold a grudge, don't you?" "It's why we invented the weregeld," the wolfess replies gruffly. "But maybe here and now, it's just me. Just be sure to repent, little bunny, and repent good and hard. Because there might be someone like me out there looking for you, for what you did while you were in with that lot." ] You clear your throat in a bid to get the conversation moving again. So what happened after that? Presumably they must've chased Tollus and his posse away, at least for a while. "It was a couple of weeks into this mess... then one of the village girls disappeared. They covered their tracks pretty well, but River said he saw Tollus and his goons taking her up the hill to the old temple. I didn't know what they were about, but my gut told me it wasn't good. Sanders asked me for help, so I took my sword and my staff and went out after them." There was a portal? "I didn't get that far, so I don't know." A bitter chuckle. "They were waiting for me at the foot of the mountain trail, in full view of the gate. The village boys and girls who'd taken up with Tollus, I could tell that they weren't themselves. Controlled, mesmerised, possessed, whatever you want to call it. Tollus was using them as meatshields, forcing Sanders and me to have to get through my own in order to reach him. He thought I wouldn't have the stomach to do it, and I'd turn back home with my tail between my legs. "He didn't know me, of course. Those kids threw themselves at me without caring for themselves, so I butchered them all. They weren't trained and whatever hold Tollus had on them was dulling their senses and reactions, so it was a simple matter to cut them all down two or three at a time. There must've been a dozen of them, then his head crony Leold came at me — a bit less worthless than the rest, but still easy meat. I tore him apart, and that was when Tollus's panic turned to fucking terror. Bastard shat his pants as he took to his heels — I think he was considering using the girl he'd captured as a hostage, but after seeing what I'd done to his meatshields he didn't doubt that I'd kill her too just to get at him." There's a heavy silence that hangs in the air. He got away. Gweyr nods. "He got away. River freed the girl, and when I turned around, everyone had gathered at the gate, cowering behind the palisades and staring at me like they didn't know who to be more afraid of, Tollus or me. I didn't blame them, returned the girl... but even if they'd fallen into bad company, even if they weren't themselves any more, those were the sons and daughters of maybe a third of the village that I'd just chopped into meaty chunks without blinking, and then there was the matter of Tollus's head goon who I'd ripped in two before their eyes. Of course they'd be scared of me, even if I saved them and the girl. "No good deed goes unpunished, [pc.name]. I single-handedly saved them all from being slaves to some madman in a robe, and there and then Sanders tells me to walk the ice, else they'd lynch me. I... don't blame them for what they did, I'd have been afraid of myself too after seeing what I did. I would've been resentful if it were my Gwyn and Garret who'd been killed, even if they weren't themselves anymore; I wouldn't be able to look myself in the eye. But even so, to realize that only my husband, River and even Sanders, in a way, stood by me while the rest of Hawkethorne was willing to throw me to the wolves, I couldn't help but feel a deep disgust for the lot of them. I guess leading my own mercenary company for so long had spoiled me, made me expect things of people that most folk don't have. "The point of sending you to walk the ice is to kill you, [pc.name]; you're meant to keep on walking further and further north until the cold takes you. A way to kill you while maintaining the illusion of keeping one's hands clean. But as you can see, I didn't die. I wasn't about to let myself. I've hunted Tollus for all these years... and now he and his ilk wind up on my doorstep. "You're right, [pc.name]. Those snares weren't meant for rabbits. They're meant for people. You can guess who." "

rows.original:
[party.has cait
                    |Cait thinks a moment, pursing her lips. "Not saying that I don't believe you, Mrs. Gweyr, it does explain why Garth was so enthusiastic about helping us out that night with Calla and all. But when I went around the town asking about the cult, no one seemed to know anything, which would run counter to common knowledge if Tollus had tried to annex Hawkethorne all those years ago. What gives?"
                    |Which explains why Garth was so enthusiastic about helping Cait and you that night. That leaves but one question: when Cait went around asking about the cult, no one seemed to know anything, which would run counter to common knowledge if Tollus had tried to annex Hawkethorne all those years ago. What gives?
                ]
                
                Gweyr shrugs. "I'd wager most of the families eventually uprooted themselves and left, either down into Harvest Valley or Tychris. We were only a handful back then... while I've only seen it from afar these days, Hawkethorne's grown a lot as the years have passed. It wouldn't be surprising if most of the new settlers didn't know anything..."
                
                And with the oldest residents effectively keeping mum on the subject of Garth's wife, no one would have had the opportunity to learn.
                
                The wolfess folds her ears forward. "Just so."
                
                [party.has cait
                    |"But — but doesn't that mean that if everyone who opposed you is gone, you can go home again? To Gwyn? To Garret?" Cait waves her hands about excitedly. "You don't have to live in a cave up here! Everyone thinks that you died or something, but if — "
                    |But doesn't that mean if everyone who opposed her is more or less gone, she can return to Hawkethorne? To Gwyn? To Garret? She doesn't have to live up in a cave amidst this icy wasteland, she could — 
                ] 
                
                She cuts [party.has cait
                    |Cait
                    |you
                ] off with a sharp slice of her hand. "No. Not before I've dealt with matters here. Not when he's got his lackeys on my doorstep. I won't hear any of it."
                
                And she didn't return in the years beforehand?
                
                "Not while he was out there. And then while River might be forgiving, I doubt old man Sanders has changed any in these two decades."
                
                ... 
                
                "...I didn't have any kind of lead, or anything to go off on. Every trail I turned up went cold, the man clearly had learned to cover his tracks after the whipping I gave him the first time around. But now... now he's staying put here, I want to know why, and have a plan to find out."
                
                Is there any way you can help? It looks like you've got a common enemy here in Tollus.
                
                Gweyr snorts. "We can talk about that in a bit; my mouth is dry and there's been a lot for you to take in, I suppose. But I don't think the gods placed you in my path out of sheer coincidence, [pc.name], nor that of my husband's. When you're ready to start taking action against Tollus's little cult up here in this frozen hellhole, come talk to me again and we can start discussing plans. For now... make yourself comfortable. This has been my home for the last fifteen years, and if it's good enough for me, it's good enough for you."
rows.translation:
[party.has cait
                    |凯特沉思了一会儿，嘴唇微微抿紧。“并不是说我不相信你，格温尔夫人，但这确实可以解释为什么加思在那个晚上会如此热心地帮助我们处理卡拉的事情。但是当我在镇上询问关于那个邪教组织的情况时，似乎没有人知道任何相关信息。如果多年前托卢斯真的试图吞并鹰棘镇的话，这种情况应该是与普遍认知相悖的啊。这是怎么回事呢？
                    |这就解释了为什么加斯在那个晚上会如此热心地帮助凯特和你们。那么就只剩下一个问题了：当凯特四处打听关于那个邪教组织的情况时，似乎没有人知道任何相关信息，而这与常理相悖——因为如果托卢斯在多年前就试图吞并鹰棘镇的话，这种情况根本不可能发生。这是怎么回事呢？
                ]
                
                格温尔耸了耸肩：“我敢打赌，大多数家庭最终都离开了这里，要么搬到了收获谷，要么去了提克里斯。那时候我们只有寥寥几人……而这些年来，虽然我只是远远地看到它，但鹰棘镇确实发展得很大。 如果大多数新来的定居者对此一无所知，那也不足为奇了……

而由于那些年纪最大的居民们刻意回避谈论加思的妻子，所以根本没有人有机会了解到这些事情。
                
                那只母狼将耳朵向前折叠。“就这样。
                
                [party.has cait
                    |但是——但是这意味着，如果所有反对你的人都离开了，你就可以回家了吧？回到格温身边，或者回到加勒特那里？”凯特兴奋地挥舞着手。“你不必再住在这山洞里了！大家都以为你已经死了，或者发生了什么，但是如果……
                    |但这难道不意味着，既然所有反对她的人差不多都离开了，她就可以回到鹰棘镇了吗？回到格温身边，回到加勒特身边？她不必再生活在这片冰冷的荒原中的洞穴里，她完全可以…… 
                ] 
                
                她动手部切割了。 [party.has cait
                    |凯特
                    |你
                ] 她猛地甩了甩手部，说道：“不行。在我解决这里的事情之前，绝对不行。只要他的走狗还出现在我的家门口，我就不会听任何理由。”

那么，在那之后的几年里，她就没有再回来过吗？
                
                在他还在世的时候，绝对不行。而且，虽然里弗可能会原谅他，但我怀疑桑德斯老头在这二十年里根本没有任何改变。”

……

“……我没有任何线索，也没有任何可以依据的东西。 我追踪的每一条线索都毫无结果，很明显，那次我狠狠地教训了他之后，他已经学会了如何掩盖自己的行踪。但现在……他却留在了这里，我想知道原因，并且有一个计划来查明真相。有没有什么办法可以帮助你呢？看来在托卢斯，你们有一个共同的敌人。”

格韦尔哼了一声：“这个我们稍后再谈吧；我现在口渴得很，而且你似乎也有很多事情需要了解。 但我认为，诸神将你安排到我的道路上，绝非偶然。 [pc.name]也不是我丈夫的。当你准备好对这个位于这个冰封地狱中的托卢斯小教派采取行动时，再来找我谈谈，我们可以开始讨论具体的计划。目前来说……请随意休息。过去十五年来，这里一直是我的家，如果它对我来说足够好，那么对你来说也应该足够好。

rows.original: [rand |You shuffle in by the wolfess, sitting down across her from the fire. She lowers her sewing and gives you a nod and grunt, acknowledging your presence but little more. How's she holding up? "Fine as ever. It's colder than a pale elf's pecker up in the Rift, but y'know, welcome." [party.has etheryn |Etheryn shifts her eyes at that comment. |Uh-huh. ] "But you obviously aren't here to waste both our time just staring at each other, so: what's on your mind?" |You find Gweyr by the smoking rack, putting strips of meat and blubber over the fire and listening to them sizzle and pop, dripping juices down onto the coals. She acknowledges you with a grunt and nod as you draw close, not taking her eyes off the cooking. It actually smells good, even halfway appetising, but it most certainly won't by the time she's through with it and packed the lot in snow, you guess... Good day. "Good day." Gweyr sniffs at one of the strips, breaks off a piece, and chews carefully. The fact that the fat's still sizzling slightly on the meat is completely lost to her. "Weather's terrible." It is. A moment of awkward silence, and then she sighs. "Sorry about that. I'm... I'm just not used to receiving guests on a regular basis like you any more, not that I was ever any good at making small talk. Yes, I used to lead a company once, but... that was a long time ago and the cold, it dulls everything that isn't born of it, my wits included. Or maybe I'm just getting old. What can I do for you?" |Drawn by the sound of melancholic music, you find Gweyr sitting cross-legged on her bed, playing on a simple bone flute. For fingers that're as thick as hers, they move with considerable alacrity and precision, beating out a surprisingly complex tune uncharacteristic of such a primitive instrument. You settle down on the stool and wait for her to be done, which she does after a minute or two of playing; the wolfess turns her head to peer at you and eventually acknowledges you with a nod. "Hope I didn't keep you waiting." Oh no, she didn't. "You have to do these things once in a while to stay sane. The constant wind, the presence of these mountains... if you're not born of the Rift, they eventually drive you insane. If you are born of the Rift, they are your strength." Too bad Tollus's goons have already embraced madness. "Hm. Are you here to discuss that matter?" Amongst other things. Perhaps you should begin? ]
rows.translation: [rand |你在狼女旁边坐下，面对着火堆。她放下手中的针线活，向你点了点头，发出一声低哼，算是承认了你的存在，但并没有说太多话。 “她现在怎么样？” “还是一如既往地过得不错。虽然这里比裂谷里那些苍白精灵居住的地方还要冷得多，不过……欢迎你来。 [party.has etheryn |听到这个评论，伊瑟琳微微移开了视线。 |嗯，好的。 ] 但你显然不是来浪费我们双方的时间，只是互相盯着看的，所以……你到底有什么打算？ |你在那个用来烤肉的架子旁找到了格温尔。她把肉片和油脂放在火上，听着它们滋滋作响、噼啪跳跃，肉汁不断地滴落在炭火上。当你靠近时，她只是哼了一声，点了点头，目光始终没有离开正在烹饪的食物。 它实际上闻起来还挺香的，甚至有点开胃，但等到她把它全部处理完，然后把那些东西裹在雪里保存起来之后，味道肯定就完全变了……你懂我的意思吧…… 早上好。 “早上好。”格温尔闻了闻其中一条食物条，撕下一小块，然后仔细地咀嚼起来。 她完全没有注意到肉上的脂肪还在微微冒着热气。“天气真是糟透了。” 确实如此。 一阵尴尬的沉默之后，她叹了口气：“抱歉，我………我只是已经不再习惯像你现在这样经常接待客人了，毕竟我从来就不擅长闲聊。没错，我曾经管理过一家公司，但是……那已经是很久以前的事了。寒冷会让一切非由它引发的事物变得迟钝，包括我的反应能力也是如此。 或者，也许只是我年纪大了吧。我能为您做些什么呢？ |被那忧郁的音乐吸引，你看到格温尔盘腿坐在床上，正在吹奏一支简单的骨笛。对于她那样粗壮的手指来说，她的手指动作却异常敏捷而精准，奏出了令人惊讶的复杂旋律——这对于这样一种原始的乐器来说实在是不可思议的。 你坐在凳子上，等待她玩完。过了一两分钟，她终于停下了动作；那只母狼转过头来看着你，最终点了点头，表示认出了你。 “希望我没有让你等待太久。哦不，她并没有那么做。” “你必须偶尔做这些事情，才能保持理智。持续不断的风声，这些山脉的存在……如果你不是在裂谷地区出生的，最终它们会让你发疯的。 如果你 是 他们诞生于裂隙之中，正是你们的力量源泉。” 可惜，托卢斯的那些手下早已陷入了疯狂。 “嗯，你是来讨论这个问题的吗？” 除此之外，或许你应该先开始谈谈吧？ ]
rows.raw: " [rand |You shuffle in by the wolfess, sitting down across her from the fire. She lowers her sewing and gives you a nod and grunt, acknowledging your presence but little more. How's she holding up? "Fine as ever. It's colder than a pale elf's pecker up in the Rift, but y'know, welcome." [party.has etheryn |Etheryn shifts her eyes at that comment. |Uh-huh. ] "But you obviously aren't here to waste both our time just staring at each other, so: what's on your mind?" |You find Gweyr by the smoking rack, putting strips of meat and blubber over the fire and listening to them sizzle and pop, dripping juices down onto the coals. She acknowledges you with a grunt and nod as you draw close, not taking her eyes off the cooking. It actually smells good, even halfway appetising, but it most certainly won't by the time she's through with it and packed the lot in snow, you guess... Good day. "Good day." Gweyr sniffs at one of the strips, breaks off a piece, and chews carefully. The fact that the fat's still sizzling slightly on the meat is completely lost to her. "Weather's terrible." It is. A moment of awkward silence, and then she sighs. "Sorry about that. I'm... I'm just not used to receiving guests on a regular basis like you any more, not that I was ever any good at making small talk. Yes, I used to lead a company once, but... that was a long time ago and the cold, it dulls everything that isn't born of it, my wits included. Or maybe I'm just getting old. What can I do for you?" |Drawn by the sound of melancholic music, you find Gweyr sitting cross-legged on her bed, playing on a simple bone flute. For fingers that're as thick as hers, they move with considerable alacrity and precision, beating out a surprisingly complex tune uncharacteristic of such a primitive instrument. You settle down on the stool and wait for her to be done, which she does after a minute or two of playing; the wolfess turns her head to peer at you and eventually acknowledges you with a nod. "Hope I didn't keep you waiting." Oh no, she didn't. "You have to do these things once in a while to stay sane. The constant wind, the presence of these mountains... if you're not born of the Rift, they eventually drive you insane. If you are born of the Rift, they are your strength." Too bad Tollus's goons have already embraced madness. "Hm. Are you here to discuss that matter?" Amongst other things. Perhaps you should begin? ] "

rows.original: So, this is Garth's wife, huh. Wonder if you can see what he saw in her...
rows.translation: 所以，这就是加思的妻子，嗯。不知道你能不能看出他在她身上看到了什么……
rows.raw: "So, this is Garth's wife, huh. Wonder if you can see what he saw in her... "

rows.original: See what you can learn about this old wolfess.
rows.translation: 看看你能从这个老雌狼身上了解到些什么吧。
rows.raw: "See what you can learn about this old wolfess."

rows.original: Let's get to crushing Tollus and his goons already. What did she have in mind?
rows.translation: 我们赶紧去打败托卢斯和他的手下吧。她到底在打什么算盘？
rows.raw: "Let's get to crushing Tollus and his goons already. What did she have in mind?"

rows.original: If Garth is towering, Gweyr is massive. She's got at least a full head of height over her husband, and is thick to match; the constant cold of the rift has only encouraged her to grow stouter like everything else here in a bid to stave off the cold. Perhaps in her youth she might've been more stereotypically feminine and curvaceous, but the years and rigors of the Rift have taken their toll on her, turning her more stolid and blocky — or at least, what you can tell of her frame under the thick furs and pelts. Her fur is gray, but has been blotched to grayish-white in several places, especially about her muzzle; not that you can see most of it given how well she's wrapped up in her clothes. And what clothes they are. The thick coat and fur-lined boots of leather and hide — all made by herself — are one thing, but the way she's bound her tail is another. It makes sense to wrap up her extremities like this lest she lose them to frostbite, but seeing the pelt tied about her tail like wrappings is... well. That's not to mention the snowshoes, or the slitted bone coverings she wears over her eyes, propped up upon her muzzle. "You have to wear these when you go out during the day," Gweyr explains. "All the snow and ice constantly reflects the sun into your eyes, and if you don't protect yourself, you'll go blind; that's one of the first things I learned from the pale elves when I arrived in this place. Not all at once, but over weeks and months; the damage adds up and when you realize what's going on it's too late to do anything about it. And the snowshoes, they spread out my weight so I don't sink into drifts when I walk on them. Not that any of the natives have any problems with either... but if you're not born of the Rift, it hates you with a passion you can't even begin to imagine." She certainly looks like a mad hermit, that's for sure. Meaty fingers and hammer hands bear hard, ragged claws, and you notice that several of Gweyr's teeth are misaligned and overgrown, jutting from her jaws like an orc's tusks. [var0|It's clear which side of the family Garret takes after — the resemblance to his mother is striking. This might be Garret if he were a woman and one added twenty-five years or so, along with removing his boisterous sense of humor. In a way, it's an extremely sad loss, especially if Gweyr's temperament was one akin to her son's.|] Given that there's a source of hot water in her home, you don't imagine baths are in short supply, but soap... well, that's another matter. If anything, the wolfess looks like a weather-beaten boulder, if nothing else. Her arms and thews are thick, her bosom is as massive as it is solid, and while her furs are clearly comfortable and easy to move in they nevertheless give the impression that the wolfess is just straining at their seams with every step that she takes. A massive, imposing monster; it's not surprising how she wound up being the captain of a mercenary company in her youth, or how she and Garth wound up building a place as impressive as the Frost Hound between the two of them. Even so, up in this miserable place, perhaps Gweyr is at home in a hellscape that hates her as much as she hates it. Anyone lesser would've either perished or given up.
rows.translation: 如果加斯高耸入云，那么格温尔更是…… 庞大的她的个子至少比她丈夫高出一个头，体格也相当魁梧；裂谷地区的严寒环境使得她和其他生物一样，为了抵御寒冷而变得愈发粗壮。或许在年轻时，她可能会更加符合传统意义上的女性美，身形也会更加曲线优美，但多年的艰苦环境已经使她的体格变得粗壮而结实——至少从她身上厚厚的毛皮来看，确实是如此。 它的毛色是灰色的，但在某些地方已经变成了灰白色，尤其是在嘴部周围；不过由于它被衣服裹得严严实实，这些灰白色的部分其实不太容易被看到。 还有她穿的那些衣服。那件厚外套以及那些用皮革和毛皮衬里的靴子——全部都是她自己制作的——这还情有可原，但她把尾巴缠起来的方式却另当别论。将四肢包裹起来以防止冻伤，这种做法确实很有道理，但看到她的尾巴被那些毛皮紧紧缠住，看起来实在……嗯，有点奇怪。更不用说那些雪鞋，还有她戴在眼睛上、固定在鼻梁上的那些带裂口的骨制护具了。 白天外出的时候必须穿上这些，”格韦尔解释道，“所有的积雪和冰面都会不断反射阳光进入你的眼睛，如果不加以保护，你就会失明；这是我来到这个地方后，从那些苍白精灵那里学到的第一件事。 这不是瞬间发生的，而是经过数周乃至数月的时间；这些损害逐渐累积，等到你意识到问题的严重性时，就已经为时已晚，再也无法采取任何措施了。而那些雪鞋，它们能够分散我的体重，这样我在行走时就不会陷入雪堆里。 并不是说这些原住民中对这两种情况有任何意见……但如果你不是在“裂隙之地”出生的，那么那里的人会以你根本无法想象的强烈程度来厌恶你。 她确实看起来像一个疯狂的隐士，这一点毫无疑问。她那粗壮的手部指和像锤子一样的手部部能够承受巨大的力量，而她那些参差不齐的爪子也让人一眼就能看出来。此外，格温尔的几颗牙齿也排列不整齐，而且过度生长，从她的下颌中凸出来，就像兽人的獠牙一样。 [var0|很明显，加勒特更像他母亲那一方——他与母亲的相似之处十分明显。如果加勒特是女性，再加上二十五岁左右的年龄，再去掉他那种喧闹的幽默感，的话，他简直就会和他的母亲一模一样了。 从某种意义上来说，这种失去确实非常令人难过，尤其是如果格温尔的性格也和她儿子一样的话。|] 既然她家里有热水供应，想必洗澡并不成问题，但肥皂……嗯，那就是另一回事了。说实在的，这位女狼看起来就像一块饱经风霜的巨石——她的手部臂和肌肉非常粗壮，胸部既丰满又结实。虽然她的皮毛显然很舒适，穿着也很方便，但每次她走动时，都给人一种皮毛几乎要被撑破的感觉。 一只庞大而令人敬畏的怪物；难怪她在年轻时就能成为一支雇佣兵队伍的队长，也难怪她与加斯能够共同建立起像“霜猎犬”这样令人瞩目的据点。 即便如此，在这个糟糕至极的地方，格薇尔或许反而觉得自己身处一个与她同样憎恨她的地狱之中。换作别人，早就死了或者放弃了。

rows.original:
[rand
        |"Talk, huh. You want to talk."
        
        You do. Does she have something against talking?
        
        "No, not at all. I guess I'm not the best at making small talk, especially not now. Jotuns aren't great talkers, either, so I didn't have much in the way of conversationalists until you came around."
        
        You just want to hear about her past, understand her situation better so that you can move forward.
        
        Gweyr gives you a thin smile. "You're reminding me of the days when I used to lead a company... that's something I'd have done back then. I was a different dog... time changes us all. But yes, I'll talk. What did you want to know?"
        |"I'll talk, sure. My hands may be busy, but my mouth isn't. Truth be told, [pc.name], I'm kind of glad for the chance to talk to someone about these things. To be honest... maybe turn back time for just a little bit."
        
        Oh?
        
        The old wolfess nods. "It helps keep the madness at bay. Even if there weren't the constant wind and cold, being alone all the time wears at you. It's a nice day when I'm fishing out on the ice and a friendly selkie comes along — I know most on the eastern ice shelves by name at this point. They like to gossip a lot, although of late it's just gotten all kinds of depressing.
        
        "But I digress. Did you want to discuss something, [pc.name]?"
        |"Sure, I've time right now."
        
        Really? That's a little surprising.
        
        "Old habits die hard — I don't waste time while doing things, which means there's time left over aplenty after the chores are done and the meat's smoking. Used to fill that with playing the flute for a bit... but it's nice to hear a voice that isn't your own and be able to talk about the past. Old memories are hard to dredge up... but if not now, then when?"
    ]
rows.translation:
[rand
        |想说话，是吧？你想聊天。”

你确实想聊天。难道她有什么不愿意说话的理由吗？

“不，并没有。只是我不太擅长闲聊，尤其是现在这种时候。约顿巨人一族本来也不太喜欢说话，所以在你出现之前，我确实没什么聊天的话题或能力。你只是想了解她的过去，更好地理解她的处境，这样你们才能继续前进。

格温尔对你露出了一丝淡淡的微笑：“你让我想起了我以前管理公司的那些日子。…那是我当时也会做的事情。那时的我已经完全不同了……时间会改变我们所有人。不过，好吧，我会跟你说的。你想知道些什么呢？
        |我当然可以聊天。虽然我的手可能有点忙，但嘴还是闲着的。说实话…… [pc.name]我其实挺高兴有机会和别人聊聊这些事情的。说实话……也许能让时间倒流一点点也好。

哦？

那位年老的母狼点了点头：“这样能帮助我们抑制那种疯狂的情绪。 即使没有持续不断的风和寒冷，长时间独处也会让人感到疲惫。当我在冰面上钓鱼时，如果遇到一只友好的海豹，那真的是美好的一天——到现在为止，我已经认识东边冰架上的大多数海豹了。 他们很喜欢闲聊，不过最近这些闲聊内容都变得很令人沮丧。

“不过，我有点跑题了。你是不是有什么事情想讨论的？ [pc.name]?"
        |当然，我现在有时间。”

真的吗？这有点让人意外。

“老习惯很难改——我做事情时从不浪费时间，所以做完家务、把肉熏好后，就还会有很多空闲时间。过去我常常会用这些时间来吹笛子……不过，能听到别人的声音，一起聊聊过去的事情，也确实挺不错的。那些旧回忆确实很难被唤醒……但如果不在现在，那还要等到什么时候呢？
    ]
