rows.original: How are things looking in the Rift so far? What's the current situation?
rows.translation: 目前在裂谷地区的情况如何？目前的具体状况是怎样的？
rows.raw: "How are things looking in the Rift so far? What's the current situation?"

rows.original: Roughing it out here in the Rift for fifteen years has to have been tough for her.
rows.translation: 在裂谷地区艰难地生活了十五年，对她来说肯定非常不容易。
rows.raw: "Roughing it out here in the Rift for fifteen years has to have been tough for her."

rows.original: What can she tell you of Garth?
rows.translation: 她能告诉你关于加思的什么事情呢？
rows.raw: "What can she tell you of Garth?"

rows.original: Gwyn and Garret... you're sure she has fond memories of them.
rows.translation: 格温和加勒特……你确定她对他们怀有美好的回忆吧。
rows.raw: "Gwyn and Garret... you're sure she has fond memories of them."

rows.original: [rand |What was the name of the mercenary company she led, if she doesn't mind you asking? "Oh, I don't mind at all. We were the Crossed Swords — they're still out there, as far as I know. Last time I heard of them half a year or so back, they were heading down to the Belharan Heartlands in search of work, so you're not likely to run into them anytime soon." She gets news up here? "I don't stay in the Rift all year around. Especially during winter... it's nice to take a week or so to go to some other places, get news of people, maybe hawk off a couple seal pelts for spending money, that kind of thing. But back to the point, they were my father's company, so named because of our banner symbol, a pair of crossed swords. My father told me that it was our family crest from long ago, when we weren't reduced to being sellswords on the road." Her family crest. "My dad didn't believe it himself, but the story about us having been posh once drew in work and helped keep the company together through the tougher times. It was a symbol, that's all, but symbols can have a lot of power, especially when many people believe in them. As far as I know, the lads and lasses have kept the name and the banner symbol in my memory... and hopefully, even though the original line is gone, whoever takes over leadership of the company will keep it the way it is." |"I'm not as young as I once used to be," Gweyr admits with a sigh. "Even if I'd had plenty comfortable living, good food and rigorous training, I'd still be starting to fall apart. That, and living up here for years puts a toll on your body, makes you feel your age faster... "That knowledge when you creep up on a seal and the speed you used to have just doesn't come any more, it's shocking when you realize it. You start to realize that your days are numbered, that the distant future you once looked on with disdain isn't so distant any more. When you always assumed you'd die a violent death, so old age wouldn't ever be a problem... but the gods have other ideas for your life." Oh, she isn't that old yet. Garth's got a bad knee and he's still holding up decently enough. "Maybe now that you're here I can finally finish all of this up so I can go home for good. While it might be fitting, I'd rather not die in a hole in the middle of a freezing hellscape, even if it is a reasonably comfortable hole." |"My dad... he was a good leader, I guess. He had the kind of presence that commanded genuine respect from people, and he tried to teach me the kinds of things that would lead people to see me in the same way. The man believed that we were descended from posh people, some kind of lupine leaders, and tried to get me to act in a way befitting of them. "I don't know if it was ever true — I never felt posh at any time while growing up, but I could see the use in keeping up the act. It's understandable that people look upon sellswords with some measure of suspicion — if you'll fight for money, who's to say you won't turn if someone else offers you more? It's been done before — but if people know you'll stick by your contracts and see that you have the respect of the dogs under you, it's easier to make a living." Did her father ever have any proof that he had any kind of special lineage? Gweyr shakes her head. "No, but he believed it. And maybe that was enough for it to matter — fake it until you make it, as the saying goes. The connections and reputations he made served him well, and me later on, when the word came back to me that a war-hammer had cracked his helmet and stoved in his skull, and that I was presumably in charge of the Crossed Swords now. If he didn't have as many genuine friends as he had who were willing to be sympathetic to the girl that I was, the company would likely have either passed into someone else's hands or outright disbanded by the end of the year." |"Living up alone here has given me a lot of time to think back on my life, the choices I've made, the things I've done. I know that the saying is to have no regrets, and maybe in an ideal world that could be the case, but we can't always have what we want. Maybe I could've handled my father's untimely death better... maybe I could've been more discreet about stopping Tollus and his flunkies from sacrificing that girl, cut them off on their way up to the mountain or something. Maybe I could've tried to see my kids over all these years instead of only hearing about them from their father because I was too ashamed to face them and then tell them I'd have to leave again. "It's usually about then that I find some needlework I really have to do, or play the damned flute. Sometimes the selkies will drop by when I'm feeling down and chat a bit; they alway brighten up my day. I just wish... I thought I'd remain up here until the day I died, and now you're here, [pc.name]. That's something to think about, something indeed." |"Ever since I was a pup, I loved to fight," Gweyr says with a thin, toothy smile. "My father said that it was in our blood; that he started the Crossed Swords partly as an excuse for him to actually get the chance to fight and kill on a regular basis and remain on peoples' good sides. I'd use to pick fights with animals, anyone until he whipped me into shape and told me that stuff was going to get me killed unless I used it properly. "When I left the company and settled down with Garth in Hawkethorne, it kept on eating at me, ha. Sanders and Garth were really the only ones who were any match for me, and hunting... well, it didn't really feel the same. Animals are animals, you know? Sure, we had plenty of meat for the menu, enough to feed the guests and charge them extra for it, but... ah. My blood doesn't run so hot these days, but now that there's a purpose with these freaks having come up to my doorstep, I feel alive in a way that I haven't done for years now. My entire body trembles with excitement, I can tell you as much, [pc.name]. I feel alive. And yes, I know that's part of why I was sent to walk the ice all those years ago... but this is just so amazing, so seductive. You should watch yourself to make sure you don't fall into a fate similar to mine, [pc.name]. Nothing but heartache comes from it all." |"Being a mercenary company, we traveled across much of the continent — work was where you found it, and back at the time there was a whole bunch of conflict down in the Belharan Heartlands from taleer would-be lords and ladies seeking to hold their claims and snatch up those of others. We spent a lot of time down amongst those grasslands, moving from one contract to the other; our reputation was such that few people actually tried to cheat Father out of the payment agreed upon in his contracts, and if they did... well, they wouldn't have much of a claim any more. "And one of the things I realized is that for all their superficial differences between the taleer, humans and brown-skinned orcs who were still squabbling after a couple hundred years over the shattered pieces of that place, they were very much the same when it came down to it — miserable, greedy, broken. Not that it was entirely their fault, given that they were all products of their time and place, but sellwords don't find work in happy peaceful places. "It made me sick — not high revulsion, but a slow-burning disgust with the entire place and the situation of petty warlords that'd emerged, especially with the culture that'd developed amongst the taleer there. Once I received command of the company from my father, I took us around and marched us up back to our roots. There were still jobs to be had there, albeit amongst less comfortable circumstances, but I couldn't stand the heartlands any more after sixteen years of wandering those grassy plains and hills seeking the next contract." ]
rows.translation: [rand |她领导的那个雇佣兵组织叫什么名字呢？如果她不介意的话…… “哦，我完全不介意。我们当时叫‘交叉之剑’——据我所知，他们现在应该还在活动。我最后一次听到他们的消息是在大约半年前，当时他们正前往贝尔哈兰内陆地区寻找工作机会，所以你短期内应该不会遇到他们。” 她在这里也能得到各种消息吗？ “嗯，是的。 留下 在整个裂谷地区，尤其是冬天……花上一周左右的时间去其他地方走走，了解一下人们的生活近况，或许还能卖掉几张海豹皮换些钱花，这类事情确实挺不错的。不过回到正题，那些公司都是我父亲的产业，之所以取这样的名字，是因为我们的标志是一对交叉的剑。 我父亲告诉我，那是我们家族很久以前的族徽了，那时候我们还没有沦落到在道路上当雇佣兵的地步。 她的家族徽章。 “我父亲自己也不太相信这个故事，但关于我们曾经过着富裕生活的这段传说吸引了一些客户，也在那些艰难时期帮助我们家族维持了下来。 那只是一个象征而已，但象征往往具有巨大的力量，尤其是当许多人相信它们时。据我所知，那些年轻人们将那个名称和旗帜象征铭记在心……希望即使原来的创始人已经离世，无论谁接手公司的领导权，都能保持这一切原样。" |我不再像从前那么年轻了，”格温尔叹息着承认道，“即使我拥有舒适的生活环境、美味的食物以及严格的训练，我的身体依然在逐渐衰老。而且，在这里生活了这么多年，身体确实受到了很大的影响，让我更快地感受到了年龄的增长。当你试图悄悄接近海豹时，那种速度已经再也回不来了，意识到这一点真的令人震惊。你会开始意识到，自己的日子已经屈指可数了，而曾经你不屑一顾的遥远未来，其实已经不再那么遥远了。 当你一直以为自己会死得很惨，因此老年根本不会成为你的困扰……但神明对你的命运有着其他的安排。 哦，她并不是这样的。 那个 虽然年纪大了，但加斯的膝盖状况不佳，不过他仍然能够勉强坚持工作。 “也许现在你来了，我终于可以把所有这些事情都完成，然后永远回家了。虽然这样似乎也很合适，但我还是不想在一片冰冷的荒芜之地里死去，哪怕那个地方还算比较舒适。 |我父亲……我想，他确实是个出色的领导者。他身上有一种能让人们自然而然地对他产生敬意的气质，他也一直努力教导我那些能够让我同样获得他人尊重的事情。他坚信我们是某种高贵血统的后代，是某种具有领导才能的族群，因此他也一直希望我能够以符合这种身份的方式行事。 我不知道这是否属实——在我成长的过程中，我从未有过那种高人一等的感觉，但我觉得维持这种假象也是有一定意义的。人们对于雇佣兵抱有怀疑态度，这也是可以理解的——如果你是为了钱而战斗，那么谁又能保证在别人给出更高的报酬时你不会改变立场呢？这种事情以前确实发生过……但如果你能让人们知道你会遵守自己的契约，并且你的部下也尊重你，那么你谋生就会变得容易一些。 她的父亲有没有任何证据证明自己拥有某种特殊的血统？ 格温尔摇了摇头：“没有，但他坚信这一点。也许，对于他来说，这就已经足够重要了——就像那句俗话说的：‘假装成功，直到真的成功为止’。 他建立的人脉和声誉为他带来了很多好处，后来当我听说有一把战锤击碎了他的头盔，砸进了他的头骨里，而我现在大概应该负责管理“交叉之剑”组织时，这些人脉和声誉也对我起到了很大的帮助。 如果他没有那么多真正愿意同情我这样的女孩的朋友，那么到今年年底，这家公司很可能就已经落入别人手中，或者干脆解散了。" |独自生活在这里让我有了很多时间去反思自己的人生、自己所做的选择以及自己做过的事情。我知道有句俗话叫‘不要后悔’，在理想的世界里或许真的可以做到这一点，但我们并不总能得到自己想要的东西。 也许我本可以更好地应对父亲过早离世这一事实……也许我本可以更加谨慎地阻止托卢斯和他的那些走狗牺牲那个女孩，可以在他们前往山上的路上就阻止他们，或者采取其他措施。 也许这些年来，我本应该试着去见见我的孩子们，而不是只通过他们的父亲了解他们的近况。因为我太羞于面对他们，也不敢告诉他们我很快又得离开。 “通常就在那个时候，我会找些手针活来做，或者去吹那该死的笛子。 有时候，当我情绪低落的时候，那些人鱼会过来陪我聊聊天，她们总能让我的心情变得愉快起来。我只是希望……我原本以为自己会在这里一直生活到生命的最后一刻，但现在你们来了。 [pc.name]这确实是个值得思考的问题。 |从我还是只小狗的时候起，我就喜欢打架，”格温尔露出一个露齿而略带狡黠的笑容说道，“我父亲说过，这是我们与生俱来的天性；他创立‘十字剑组织’，其实也是为了给自己一个机会，能够经常参与战斗、杀戮，从而赢得人们的尊重与喜爱。 我以前总喜欢跟动物打架，直到有人把我教训了一顿，告诉我如果不会正确使用那些东西，我肯定会丧命的。 “当我离开那家公司，和加思在鹰棘镇安顿下来后，这种念头还是一直困扰着我，哈哈。 实际上，只有桑德斯和加思真正能与我在狩猎方面一较高下，而其他的……嗯，感觉确实不一样。动物终究还是动物，你懂我的意思吧？当然，我们的菜单上有足够的肉，足够招待客人，甚至还可以额外收费，但是……啊……这些天，我的血液已经不再那么沸腾了，但既然这些怪人出现在我的门前，给了我一个目标，我突然感到自己重新活了过来，这种感觉已经很多年没有过了。我可以告诉你们，我的全身都在因为兴奋而颤抖。 [pc.name]我觉得 活着是的，我知道这也是我多年前被派去在冰上行走的原因之一……但这一切真的太令人惊叹、太令人着迷了。你一定要小心，以免陷入和我一样的命运。 [pc.name]这一切带来的只有痛苦。 |作为一家雇佣兵公司，我们走遍了这片大陆的大部分地区——哪里有工作，我们就去哪里。在那个时候，贝尔哈兰腹地发生了许多冲突，那些渴望争夺领土、抢占他人领地的贵族们纷纷卷入了这些争斗之中。 我们在那些草原上度过了很多时间，从一个合同忙到另一个合同；我们的信誉如此之高，以至于几乎没有人会试图欺骗父亲，让他支付合同中约定的款项。当然，也确实有人这么做过。嗯，那样的话，他们就没什么理由可说了。 我意识到的一点是，尽管泰勒人、人类以及那些皮肤呈棕色的兽人之间存在着种种表面上的差异，尽管他们在那些被毁之地残余的碎片问题上争论了数百年，但实际上他们本质上并没有什么不同——都同样痛苦、贪婪，也都同样心灵破碎。当然，这并不能完全归咎于他们自己，因为他们毕竟都是特定时代和环境的产物，但那些靠兜售谎言为生的人，根本不会出现在幸福安宁的地方。 这让我感到恶心——不是那种强烈的厌恶，而是一种逐渐蔓延的对整个地方以及那些新兴的小军阀势力的厌恶，尤其是对那里的法师们所形成的那种文化的厌恶。当我从父亲手部中接过对这个中队的指挥权后，我就带领我们回到了我们的故乡。 虽然工作条件有些艰苦，但那里仍然有工作机会。然而，在那些草原和山丘上漂泊了十六年，为了寻找下一份合同，我实在再也无法忍受内陆地区的环境了。 ]

rows.original: [var0 |"Since these cloaked freaks arrived in the Rift a little while ago, I've been spying on them, picking them off at the edges. They've turned themselves into these things and thus the cold doesn't bother them in the least, plus some of them are pretty strong, especially the demontaurs; that's something coming from me. Doesn't take a genius to figure out that fighting them head-on and trying to drive them from the glacier that way is a loser's game. "Picking them off and roughing up stragglers and lone cultists has slowed them a little, but they don't have any lack of hands to replace those that I deal with. I've been trying to injure and maim them, because that drains their resources faster than just killing them and letting fresh hands move in. Not that it seems to affect their morale any; these monsters are complete fanatics. I don't imagine they're thinking straight any more, to be honest. "Now that you're here, I think I'll be able to put some of my plans into action. I'd dismissed some of them earlier because one pair of hands alone isn't enough to cut it, but with [party.combatNames] throwing in with me we'll be able to start doing a little real damage to these cultist bastards. Talk to me about the matter when you think you're ready to get moving." In order to progress the storyline, talk to Gweyr about dealing with the cult. |"I don't know where the barrels are coming from, either the wood used to make them or the horrible gray stuff that they contain; we need to figure that out. In order to do that, we need time, and that's in short supply. I already told you where to find the stockpiles that I scouted — I'll create the diversion while you go in and trash the lot of them. Remember: if we can force them to get more of that gray goop, that'll be a chance for us to figure out where exactly it's coming from." She won't accompany you to the sites? "No, I'm a big girl and would stick out with you. Don't worry, I'll know when you'll be there and make a move when you do. Don't worry if you don't see me around — just trust that I'll be doing my job. I'm reliable that way." You still need to sabotage all three goop stockpiles the cultists have about the rift. |Gweyr gives you a nod of satisfaction. "Good work out there, [pc.name]. The cultists bastards still have a couple barrels left of the stuff tucked away in their main encampment, but I'm sure they'll have to send up for more of that stuff soon. As a bonus, they've stopped fouling the snows and streams by dumping the goop all over the place, so that's a bonus. We've bought ourselves some time to act, and that's what matters. "I'll be watching the cultists' main encampment for a while, see what's up with them now that they've had a true setback — or at least, I hope it's one, since we don't know the full extent of their plans yet. I'll let you know when matters either come to a head, or I learn something that we can act upon in a meaningful way. For now, just do your own thing and see if there's anything else that you can do in the rift — even with the cult stirring the pot, there's a lot of bad stuff brewing out there. Keep your head about you." ]
rows.translation: [var0 |自从这些隐藏起来的怪物不久前出现在裂隙地带，我就一直在暗中监视他们，然后在他们薄弱的地方发动攻击。他们已经把自己变成了…… 各种物品 因此，寒冷对他们来说根本不是问题，而且他们中的一些人实力相当强大，尤其是那些拆解者；这是我的个人看法。任何人都能想到，与他们正面交锋、试图把他们从冰川上赶走，这种做法无异于自取灭亡。 一个个消灭他们，同时打击那些落单的狂热信徒，确实让他们的速度有所减缓，但他们完全不缺人手来补充那些被我消灭的人。我一直在试图让他们受伤、致残，因为这样会比直接杀死他们然后让新人替补来得更快地消耗他们的资源。 似乎这些怪物们的士气并没有因此受到任何影响；他们完全就是些狂热分子。说实话，我觉得他们已经无法正常思考了。 “既然你来了，我想我就可以把一些计划付诸实施了。 我之前已经排除了其中一些方案，因为单凭一双手是远远不够完成这项工作的，但是有了…… [party.combatNames] 如果我们齐心协力，就能真正对这些邪教徒混蛋造成打击了。等你准备好行动的时候，再跟我讨论这件事吧。 为了推动故事情节的发展，你需要与格温尔谈谈如何应对那个邪教组织。 |我也不知道这些桶是从哪里来的，无论是用来制作它们的木材，还是它们里面装的那种难看的灰色物质；我们必须要弄清楚这一点。为了做到这一点，我们需要…… 时间而这种物资目前非常稀缺。我已经告诉过你们在哪里可以找到我事先探查到的储备地点——我会制造一些干扰，而你们就趁机进去把那些物资全部毁掉。记住：如果我们能迫使他们再去获取更多的那种灰色粘稠物，那么我们就有机会弄清楚这种物资到底是从哪里来的。她不会陪你一起去那些地方吗？” “不会的，我已经是个成年人了，不会给你添麻烦的。放心吧，我会注意你的动向，当你到达那里的时候，我就会立刻行动。就算你没看到我，也别担心——相信我，我一定会在背后做好我的工作的。 这样我就能够可靠地完成任务了。 你仍然需要破坏那些邪教徒在裂隙附近储存的这三批黏性物质。 |格温尔满意地点了点头：“干得不错。 [pc.name]那些邪教徒的混蛋们在他们的主要营地里还藏着几桶那种东西，但我敢肯定，他们很快就会不得不再去弄更多的。不过，他们不再把那种黏稠的物质乱扔在雪地上和小溪里，这也算是个好处。我们因此获得了一些行动的时间，这才是最重要的。 “我会继续监视那些邪教徒的主要营地，看看他们在遭遇了这样的挫折之后会有什么举动——至少，我是这么打算的。 希望 目前我们还不知道他们计划的全部内容，所以只能先这样做了。等事情发展到了某个临界点，或者我掌握了我们可以采取行动的信息，我会告诉你的。现在，你只需要继续做你自己的事情，看看在裂隙中是否还有其他事情可以去做——即使那个邪教正在挑拨事端，但外面还是有很多不好的事情正在酝酿着。一定要保持警惕。 ]
rows.raw: " [var0 |"Since these cloaked freaks arrived in the Rift a little while ago, I've been spying on them, picking them off at the edges. They've turned themselves into these things and thus the cold doesn't bother them in the least, plus some of them are pretty strong, especially the demontaurs; that's something coming from me. Doesn't take a genius to figure out that fighting them head-on and trying to drive them from the glacier that way is a loser's game. "Picking them off and roughing up stragglers and lone cultists has slowed them a little, but they don't have any lack of hands to replace those that I deal with. I've been trying to injure and maim them, because that drains their resources faster than just killing them and letting fresh hands move in. Not that it seems to affect their morale any; these monsters are complete fanatics. I don't imagine they're thinking straight any more, to be honest. "Now that you're here, I think I'll be able to put some of my plans into action. I'd dismissed some of them earlier because one pair of hands alone isn't enough to cut it, but with [party.combatNames] throwing in with me we'll be able to start doing a little real damage to these cultist bastards. Talk to me about the matter when you think you're ready to get moving." In order to progress the storyline, talk to Gweyr about dealing with the cult. |"I don't know where the barrels are coming from, either the wood used to make them or the horrible gray stuff that they contain; we need to figure that out. In order to do that, we need time, and that's in short supply. I already told you where to find the stockpiles that I scouted — I'll create the diversion while you go in and trash the lot of them. Remember: if we can force them to get more of that gray goop, that'll be a chance for us to figure out where exactly it's coming from." She won't accompany you to the sites? "No, I'm a big girl and would stick out with you. Don't worry, I'll know when you'll be there and make a move when you do. Don't worry if you don't see me around — just trust that I'll be doing my job. I'm reliable that way." You still need to sabotage all three goop stockpiles the cultists have about the rift. |Gweyr gives you a nod of satisfaction. "Good work out there, [pc.name]. The cultists bastards still have a couple barrels left of the stuff tucked away in their main encampment, but I'm sure they'll have to send up for more of that stuff soon. As a bonus, they've stopped fouling the snows and streams by dumping the goop all over the place, so that's a bonus. We've bought ourselves some time to act, and that's what matters. "I'll be watching the cultists' main encampment for a while, see what's up with them now that they've had a true setback — or at least, I hope it's one, since we don't know the full extent of their plans yet. I'll let you know when matters either come to a head, or I learn something that we can act upon in a meaningful way. For now, just do your own thing and see if there's anything else that you can do in the rift — even with the cult stirring the pot, there's a lot of bad stuff brewing out there. Keep your head about you." ] "

rows.original: [rand |Gweyr shrugs. "It's a living. Not a comfortable one, not even for the jotuns or selkies, but it's a living. You soon learn where to find seals' air-holes, how to bash them on the head just right to kill them so the pelt's as intact as possible. You learn how to make cord from gut and needles from bone, and to sew your own clothes, you learn how to go about ice fishing in this blasted landscape, and where the seams of coal are. And even so, I have to leave every so often, get to see a bit of greenery, anything other than white, blue and gray." ... "If I were to be perfectly honest, I wouldn't say living up here has been any worse than my days as the captain of a mercenary company. It's just presented different challenges than herding a pack of mangy, rowdy dogs did. Sometimes, I wonder what might have been different if I didn't choose to settle down with Garth, but there's not much point in wondering about what-ifs, is there?" You don't know about that, by her own admission she's got plenty of time alone, especially when the weather's bad outside. A lot of time to spend in her own mind, if that's what takes her fancy. Gweyr shakes her head. "No, that kind of thing is how you wind up insane. You can't think too deeply about things, wallow in regrets or your past, stew all by yourself... I should have died long before reaching the end of the world, everyone knows that being sentenced to walk the ice is an execution in all but name. That I refused to die means something, and I know what it is and what I have to do. That's all that's left." |"After a while, you realize just how much life's up here, even in a place like this. You just have to look for it." And oftentimes, you don't. Many of the locals are perfectly fine being out and about — for example, those thorny ice flower bushes you keep on seeing growing on the rock and snow. Those are all over the place. "Ha! You know them? If you manage to uproot some of those while they're flowering, they've got tubers down below. Of course, it's a bitch to clear away the plants themselves — what with all the thorns — then if they're growing in ice and stone instead of snow, actually having to dig out the tubers. Every single step's a bitch and a struggle, and the end result is several handfuls of white lumps that taste like dirty water, but it fills the stomach and keeps you going when hunting and fishing's been scarce. It took me a good while before I figured this out; most of the elves next door take one look at the thorns and clear them out before they have the chance to flower. I did, too..." |So, about her elf neighbors... "They keep out of my fur, and I don't go out of my way to antagonise them. I guess they know I'm here and I know they're there, but it's not as if they'd come rushing to my aid if anything happened to them, and frankly I wouldn't lift a finger to save those snooty bastards if they were on fire. They're here for the metals that wash out of the mountains with the snowmelt, sluicing the clear streams for ore with their machines. "It's not all good — the debris that their sluices leave behind fouls the water with minerals and makes it undrinkable, but at least I have my own water source right here at home. They don't have anything I'd want and I don't have anything they'd want, so there's no reason to trade; they get all their stuff from their posh city below, hauling it up the glacier. What do I have? A bunch of pelts and bad-tasting jerky at best. "The likes of them are too snobbish to talk to me, and I'm fine with it staying that way. To them, I'm nothing more than a mad old hermit and there's no harm in keeping with our present state of affairs." |"If you ever need help out here, you can ask a selkie. They mostly hang out on the western side of the ice shelves, doing their thing — playful lot, and they love to gossip and meet new people. The things they told me, though not always strictly true given the way their tales tend to grow in the telling, helped me out a lot when I first arrived here in the Rift. They're good people, so do right by them and they'll do right by you." You'll remember that, thanks. "They're not as temperamental as the jotuns or avanai, and aren't about to pick a fight just because they can like the siorcanna do. Not that they'll lift a finger to actually help you unless there's something in it for them, but gods, do they love to talk. Just take everything they say with a grain of salt and you'll be fine; trust them, but verify when they say that the seals are really moving today." |"While I'd like to say that I've gotten used to living up here, that isn't the case," Gweyr admits with a small sigh. "There isn't a day that passes where the mountains don't remind me that I don't belong here, that this isn't my home, and that I should return to where I actually belong before it's too late. And the worst thing about it all is that I know they're right, but I can't just leave yet." What is life, but a constant struggle? The wolfess laughs at that, a gruff bark of a laugh that echoes about her cave. "There are struggles, and there are struggles. You have to pick your fights carefully, and come out ahead. I do have to wander down into the Frostwood every now and then, see some greenery, give the Rift its due and let it be for a week or two. But I'm a fighter, too, and always come back here in the end; I'm not leaving for good until I can live with myself about it." With things coming to a head in the Rift and several threads getting all tangled up, that time may finally be at hand. "The thought that my waiting, stalking and hunting may finally be over... not because I tracked them down, but because they willingly came to my doorstep..." she shakes her head. "Ah, the gods are merciful in their own way, aren't they? The chance to finish the job I should've closed sixteen years ago..." |"The people of the rift are pretty friendly once you get to know them and they get to know you. They mostly kept their distance when I first set up my home here, but after I'd kept out of the jotuns' feet and thumped a couple of siorcanna on the head to gain their respect, they started to open up to me. Of course, the avanai have always been prudish bastards, but they don't think me that much of an outsider any more. Or at least, I hope. "They're all good people at heart, really. There're no better whalers than the jotuns, and they taught me how to fish in the ice here, with how thick it is and how easily it freezes over. The selkies told me how to make cord from preserved guts, and they shape bone in ways you wouldn't imagine — that, and they love to talk a lot, so much so that they'll come by my door every now and then just to gab. And the siorcanna... they love to fight every bit as much as I do. Doesn't hurt that they're willing to take pelts and meats for some of the stranger things their shamans make from stuff gathered deep under the freezing waves; I haven't gotten sick often while up here, but whatever they put in their stuff, it works. "That's why I'm really concerned with the mood that's taken them of late. It doesn't seem to have affected me, I don't think, but that's little solace when everyone else is turning all tetchy and ornery. I just know it's got something to do with the shit that Tollus is up to here — just the other day I caught one of the sharks sleepwalking all the way in the direction of the Lumian keep on the other side of the rift. Poor bastard was just out of it completely, moving in a daze as if possessed; when I caught up to him and snapped him out of it he didn't realize what he was doing, and was a long way away from where he expected himself to be. These are people I actually give a shit about [pc.name], and this is the second time Tollus is fucking around with folks I actually care for. When I get my hands on him... he's not escaping this time, I tell you. I'll throttle him with my own two hands for everything he's done, not just to me, but to everyone else as well." |"The Lumians? They've been here ever since I arrived in the Rift, have been here since the Godswar, according to the locals. I've never seen fit to bother them much — you can occasionally see some of them out and about the ice doing... whatever it is that they do, and every now and then the elves send up a supply convoy to the keep. I don't think even Tollus and his bastards would be foolhardy enough to try and attack one of those — as tempting a prize as it might be for them, divine warriors aren't something they're willing to face head-on just yet. "If you want to get involved with them, I guess there's no harm in knocking on their door and asking... but I personally keep my distance. Like it or not, I have to share the locals' assessment that they'd be far too snooty to associate with the likes of a weather-worn wolf like me. All warm and comfortable behind those thick stone walls of theirs, with bread and meat delivered up the glacier every week or two — it's like they don't even feel anything of the way the other peoples of the Rift live, and they don't seem to do any useful work whatsoever.[pc.ra valkyrie | Present company excluded, of course. ]" That's a rather bitter tone to take... "If only they could be assed to get out from behind their walls and take on Tollus, I'm sure Lumia and her legions would have this whole mess sorted out within a week, two at most. That they aren't already doing so implies that there's either something more important on their hands that they're dealing with, in which case I should be scared shitless, or that they can't be assed do get out and clean up Tollus and his filth, in which case I should also be scared shitless, if for very different reasons. Either way, I'm not sure if their explanation is going to be any good in my eyes. Feels like a dereliction of duty to me, honestly." |"There's no wood in these mountains — sure, there're plants of a sort, but they mostly melt rather than burn," Gweyr says with a rueful smile. You've noticed that. Instead of burning wood, she's burning these black rocks she's got piled up by the entrance to her home... "It's coal. A strange thing to find up in this miserable snowball, but there're seams of it in the mountains aplenty; maybe this place wasn't always frozen, or the earth moved, or... something. The jotuns sometimes dig out a bunch when they expand their mountain fortresses, but they don't really have any use for fire; they don't even cook their food all the time. Most of it gets traded to the avanai for things... or to me. When the giants aren't forthcoming, I have to go to the trouble of digging out some myself from one of the many exposed seams I know of, but it's terrible, aching work and it screws up your lungs something terrible, even for someone like me. I'd rather avoid it as much as I can." ]
rows.translation: [rand |格韦尔耸了耸肩：“这就是一种生存方式。虽然并不舒适，就连那些巨魔或海妖也不例外，但这就是一种生存方式。你很快就会学会如何找到海豹的呼吸孔，以及如何准确地敲打它们的头部才能将它们杀死，从而让毛皮尽可能保持完好无损。 你学会了如何用动物的肠子制作绳索，用骨头制作针线，也学会了如何自己缝制衣服；你还学会了如何在这片荒凉的土地上进行冰钓，以及如何找到蕴藏煤炭的地方。即便如此，我还是不得不偶尔离开这里，去看看一些绿色的植物，哪怕只是除了白色、蓝色和灰色之外的其他颜色也好。" 如果我要完全诚实的话，我得说，在这里生活并没有比我担任佣兵队队长那段日子更糟糕。只不过，现在面临的挑战与驱赶一群脏兮兮、吵闹的狗相比，确实有所不同。有时候，我会想，如果我没有选择和加斯一起安定下来，现在的情况会不会有所不同，但纠结于这些‘如果’也没什么意义吧？ 你可能不知道，据她自己所说，她有很多时间可以独自待着，尤其是在外面天气不好的时候。她有足够的时间沉浸在自己的思绪中，如果她喜欢这样的话。 格温尔摇了摇头。 不，那种做法只会让人发疯。你不能过度深入地思考某些事情，不能一直沉溺于悔恨或过去，也不能独自一个人闷闷不乐……我早该在到达世界尽头之前就死去，大家都知道，被判处在冰原上行走，其实就等同于被处决。 我拒绝死亡，这一事实一定意味着什么，我知道那意味着什么，也知道自己该做些什么。这就是我目前剩下的全部力量了。 |过了一段时间，你就会意识到，即使是在这样的地方，生活中也充满了各种乐趣。你只需要去寻找它们而已。” 然而，很多时候人们并不会去主动寻找这些乐趣。许多当地人日常的生活其实也非常惬意——比如那些你经常看到的、生长在岩石和积雪上的带刺的冰花灌木。 那些 哈！你认识这些植物吗？如果能在它们开花的时候把其中一些连根拔起，就会发现它们的根部下面有块茎。当然，清除这些植物本身也非常麻烦——毕竟它们长满了刺；而如果这些植物生长在冰雪而不是雪地里，那就更得费力地去挖那些块茎了。 每一步都充满艰辛与困难，最终得到的只是几把味道像脏水一样的白色块状物，但它们能填饱肚子，帮助你在狩猎和捕鱼都十分困难的时候继续坚持下去。我花了很长时间才弄明白这一点；隔壁的大多数精灵们只要看一眼那些带刺的植物，就会在它们有机会开花之前把它们清除干净。 我也是…… |那么，关于她的那些精灵邻居…… “他们不会来打扰我，而我也不会特意去招惹他们。我想他们知道我在这里，我也知道他们在那里，但要是他们出了什么事情，他们应该也不会赶来帮助我；说实话，就算那些自命不凡的家伙着火了，我也不会动一根手指去救他们。 他们来这里是为了获取那些随着雪水融化从山上冲下来的金属，他们用机器将这些金属从清澈的溪流中分离出来。 “不过这也并非全是好事——他们的作业留下的残渣会向水中释放矿物质，使水变得无法饮用，但至少我家里有自己独立的水源。 他们没有我想要的东西，而我也没有他们想要的东西，所以根本没有交易的必要；他们所有的东西都是从下面那个豪华的城市里弄来的，然后通过冰川运到这里。而我呢？最多也就是有一些皮毛和味道难吃的干肉而已。 他们这种人太自命不凡了，根本不愿意和我搭话，而我也不介意就这样。在他们眼里，我不过是个疯疯癫癫的隐士罢了，维持现状其实也没什么坏处。 |如果你在这里需要帮助，可以去找塞尔基人。它们大多聚集在冰架的西侧，做着各自的事情——这些小家伙非常爱玩闹，也喜欢闲聊和结识新朋友。虽然它们告诉我的那些事情，由于故事在流传过程中往往会添油加醋，所以并不总是完全真实的，但当我第一次来到裂谷这里时，那些信息确实帮了我大忙。 他们是好人，所以善待他们，他们也会善待你。 你会记住这个的，谢谢。 “他们不像那些乔顿人或阿瓦奈人那样容易情绪化，也不会仅仅因为想打架就动手，就像那些西奥卡纳人那样。 他们除非能从中得到好处，否则根本不会主动帮你一把，但天啊，他们确实特别爱说个不停。对他们说的每一句话都持保留态度吧，这样就不会出问题了；虽然可以相信他们，但当他们说今天那些封印真的开始移动时，你还是得亲自去核实一下才行。" |虽然我想说自己已经习惯了在这里生活，但实际上并非如此，”格温尔轻轻叹了口气说道，“没有一天不让我想起，这些山脉在提醒我：我并不属于这里，这里并不是我的家，我应该在为时已晚之前回到真正属于我的地方去。 而最糟糕的是，我知道他们是正确的，但我却无法就此离开。 人生，不就是一场无休止的挣扎吗？ 那只母狼发出了笑声，那是一种低沉而粗哑的笑声，在她的洞穴中回荡着。 困境有很多，各种各样的困境。你必须谨慎地选择该与哪些困难抗争，才能最终取得胜利。 做 我偶尔也会走进寒冰森林，看看那些绿色的植物，承认裂隙的存在，然后让它安静一两周。但我也是一个战士，最终总会回到这里；直到我能对自己这样做感到心安理得之前，我是不会永远离开的。随着裂隙地区的局势逐渐紧张，各种矛盾也日益复杂，那个时刻或许终于到来了。 “想到我漫长的等待、暗中追踪以及不懈的努力，终于要得到回报了…………并不是因为我找到了他们，而是因为他们主动来到了我的面前……”她摇了摇头，“啊，神明也有他们自己的慈悲之心，不是吗？这给了我一个机会，去完成那件十六年前就应该完成的事情。.." |一旦你真正了解了裂隙中的那些人，他们也会开始了解你，他们会变得相当友善。当我最初在这里安家时，他们大多保持着距离，但后来我避开了那些巨魔的侵扰，还打了几只西奥卡纳的头以赢得他们的尊重，从那以后他们才开始对我敞开心扉。当然，那些阿瓦奈人一直都相当保守，但他们不再把我当作外人来看待了。至少，我是这么希望的。 他们内心都是善良的人，真的。没有比 jotuns 更出色的捕鲸人了，他们还教会了我如何在这种冰层如此厚、而且很容易结冰的环境中捕鱼。那些 selkies 则教我如何用保存下来的动物内脏制作绳索，他们还会用一些你根本想象不到的方法来加工骨头——除此之外，他们还非常喜欢聊天，以至于经常会来找我闲聊几句。 而那些西奥卡纳人……他们和我一样，也非常喜欢战斗。他们愿意用兽皮和肉类来换取萨满们用从冰封的海浪下采集来的材料制作的一些奇怪物品，这一点确实很方便；我在这里生活的时候，很少生病，不过不管他们在这些物品里加了什么，效果确实很明显。 这就是为什么我最近真的很担心他们的情绪状态。我觉得这种情绪似乎并没有影响到我，但当周围的人都变得易怒、暴躁的时候，这就没什么安慰作用了……我只是…… 知道 这肯定和托卢斯在这里干的那些坏事有关——就在前几天，我碰到有一条鲨鱼在梦游，一直朝着裂隙另一边的卢米安据点方向走去。那个可怜的家伙完全处于迷糊状态，动作呆滞得就像被附身了一样；当我追上它并将其唤醒时，它根本不知道自己刚才在做什么，而且已经偏离了原本应该去的方向。这些人才是我真正会在意的人呢。 [pc.name]这已经是第二次了，Tollus总是来招惹那些我在乎的人。等我抓到他的时候……我告诉你，他这次绝对逃不掉。我会亲手部掐死他，为他所做的一切付出代价——不仅仅是因为他对我做了那些事，也因为他对其他人造成的伤害。 |那些卢米安人？据当地人说，从我来到裂隙地带以来，他们就一直在这里，甚至可以追溯到神战时期。我一直觉得没有必要过多打扰他们——偶尔你会看到他们中的一些人在冰原上活动。无论他们在做什么，精灵们偶尔会派遣补给车队前往那座堡垒。我认为，就连托卢斯和他的那些手部下也不敢贸然攻击这样的车队——尽管这些补给车队对他们来说可能是非常诱人的目标，但神圣战士们目前还不是他们愿意直接面对的对手部。 如果你想和他们打交道，我想去他们家敲门问问也没什么坏处……但就我个人而言，我会保持距离。不管你喜不喜欢，我得同意当地人的看法：他们肯定太傲慢了，根本不会愿意和像我这样饱经风霜的人为伍。 在他们那些厚厚的石墙后面，一切都温暖而舒适，每隔一两周就会有面包和肉类被送到他们那里——他们似乎完全感受不到裂谷地区其他人们的艰辛生活，而且他们似乎也从不做任何有意义的工作。[pc.ra valkyrie | 当然，现在在场的这些人除外。 ]这种肌肉度未免太尖刻了……” “要是他们能鼓起勇气走出自己的堡垒，去迎战托卢斯的话，我相信卢米娅和她的军队最多用一两周就能解决这一切麻烦。 如果他们还没有采取行动，那就意味着要么他们手部头有更重要的事情需要处理，这样的话我确实应该吓得要死；要么就是他们根本懒得去清理托卢斯和他的脏乱，这种情况下，我同样应该吓得要死，只不过原因截然不同罢了。 不管怎样，我不确定他们的解释在我看来是否站得住足部。说实话，我觉得这简直就是失职行为。 |这些山上根本没有木材——当然，也有一些植物，但它们大多会融化而不是燃烧，”格韦尔带着一丝无奈的微笑说道。 你注意到了这一点。她并没有烧木材，而是烧那些堆在自家门口的黑色岩石。这是煤炭。在这种冰天雪地的环境中找到这种东西确实很奇怪，但山区里其实到处都有煤层；也许这个地方并不是一直处于冰封状态，又或者是地壳发生了变动，又或者是别的什么原因。那些巨魔在扩建他们的山中堡垒时有时也会挖出一些煤炭，但他们其实并不需要火来使用；他们甚至并不总是用火来烹饪食物。 大部分这些资源都被用来和阿瓦奈人交换各种物品……或者被卖给我。当那些巨人不愿意提供这些资源时，我就不得不亲自去那些我知道的、暴露在外的矿脉中挖掘，但这工作实在太辛苦了，会严重损害你的肺部健康，即使是对我这样的的人来说也是如此。 我尽量会避免这样做。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |Gweyr shrugs. "It's a living. Not a comfortable one, not even for the jotuns or selkies, but it's a living. You soon learn where to find seals' air-holes, how to bash them on the head just right to kill them so the pelt's as intact as possible. You learn how to make cord from gut and needles from bone, and to sew your own clothes, you learn how to go about ice fishing in this blasted landscape, and where the seams of coal are. And even so, I have to leave every so often, get to see a bit of greenery, anything other than white, blue and gray." ... "If I were to be perfectly honest, I wouldn't say living up here has been any worse than my days as the captain of a mercenary company. It's just presented different challenges than herding a pack of mangy, rowdy dogs did. Sometimes, I wonder what might have been different if I didn't choose to settle down with Garth, but there's not much point in wondering about what-ifs, is there?" You don't know about that, by her own admission she's got plenty of time alone, especially when the weather's bad outside. A lot of time to spend in her own mind, if that's what takes her fancy. Gweyr shakes her head. "No, that kind of thing is how you wind up insane. You can't think too deeply about things, wallow in regrets or your past, stew all by yourself... I should have died long before reaching the end of the world, everyone knows that being sentenced to walk the ice is an execution in all but name. That I refused to die means something, and I know what it is and what I have to do. That's all that's left." |"After a while, you realize just how much life's up here, even in a place like this. You just have to look for it." And oftentimes, you don't. Many of the locals are perfectly fine being out and about — for example, those thorny ice flower bushes you keep on seeing growing on the rock and snow. Those are all over the place. "Ha! You know them? If you manage to uproot some of those while they're flowering, they've got tubers down below. Of course, it's a bitch to clear away the plants themselves — what with all the thorns — then if they're growing in ice and stone instead of snow, actually having to dig out the tubers. Every single step's a bitch and a struggle, and the end result is several handfuls of white lumps that taste like dirty water, but it fills the stomach and keeps you going when hunting and fishing's been scarce. It took me a good while before I figured this out; most of the elves next door take one look at the thorns and clear them out before they have the chance to flower. I did, too..." |So, about her elf neighbors... "They keep out of my fur, and I don't go out of my way to antagonise them. I guess they know I'm here and I know they're there, but it's not as if they'd come rushing to my aid if anything happened to them, and frankly I wouldn't lift a finger to save those snooty bastards if they were on fire. They're here for the metals that wash out of the mountains with the snowmelt, sluicing the clear streams for ore with their machines. "It's not all good — the debris that their sluices leave behind fouls the water with minerals and makes it undrinkable, but at least I have my own water source right here at home. They don't have anything I'd want and I don't have anything they'd want, so there's no reason to trade; they get all their stuff from their posh city below, hauling it up the glacier. What do I have? A bunch of pelts and bad-tasting jerky at best. "The likes of them are too snobbish to talk to me, and I'm fine with it staying that way. To them, I'm nothing more than a mad old hermit and there's no harm in keeping with our present state of affairs." |"If you ever need help out here, you can ask a selkie. They mostly hang out on the western side of the ice shelves, doing their thing — playful lot, and they love to gossip and meet new people. The things they told me, though not always strictly true given the way their tales tend to grow in the telling, helped me out a lot when I first arrived here in the Rift. They're good people, so do right by them and they'll do right by you." You'll remember that, thanks. "They're not as temperamental as the jotuns or avanai, and aren't about to pick a fight just because they can like the siorcanna do. Not that they'll lift a finger to actually help you unless there's something in it for them, but gods, do they love to talk. Just take everything they say with a grain of salt and you'll be fine; trust them, but verify when they say that the seals are really moving today." |"While I'd like to say that I've gotten used to living up here, that isn't the case," Gweyr admits with a small sigh. "There isn't a day that passes where the mountains don't remind me that I don't belong here, that this isn't my home, and that I should return to where I actually belong before it's too late. And the worst thing about it all is that I know they're right, but I can't just leave yet." What is life, but a constant struggle? The wolfess laughs at that, a gruff bark of a laugh that echoes about her cave. "There are struggles, and there are struggles. You have to pick your fights carefully, and come out ahead. I do have to wander down into the Frostwood every now and then, see some greenery, give the Rift its due and let it be for a week or two. But I'm a fighter, too, and always come back here in the end; I'm not leaving for good until I can live with myself about it." With things coming to a head in the Rift and several threads getting all tangled up, that time may finally be at hand. "The thought that my waiting, stalking and hunting may finally be over... not because I tracked them down, but because they willingly came to my doorstep..." she shakes her head. "Ah, the gods are merciful in their own way, aren't they? The chance to finish the job I should've closed sixteen years ago..." |"The people of the rift are pretty friendly once you get to know them and they get to know you. They mostly kept their distance when I first set up my home here, but after I'd kept out of the jotuns' feet and thumped a couple of siorcanna on the head to gain their respect, they started to open up to me. Of course, the avanai have always been prudish bastards, but they don't think me that much of an outsider any more. Or at least, I hope. "They're all good people at heart, really. There're no better whalers than the jotuns, and they taught me how to fish in the ice here, with how thick it is and how easily it freezes over. The selkies told me how to make cord from preserved guts, and they shape bone in ways you wouldn't imagine — that, and they love to talk a lot, so much so that they'll come by my door every now and then just to gab. And the siorcanna... they love to fight every bit as much as I do. Doesn't hurt that they're willing to take pelts and meats for some of the stranger things their shamans make from stuff gathered deep under the freezing waves; I haven't gotten sick often while up here, but whatever they put in their stuff, it works. "That's why I'm really concerned with the mood that's taken them of late. It doesn't seem to have affected me, I don't think, but that's little solace when everyone else is turning all tetchy and ornery. I just know it's got something to do with the shit that Tollus is up to here — just the other day I caught one of the sharks sleepwalking all the way in the direction of the Lumian keep on the other side of the rift. Poor bastard was just out of it completely, moving in a daze as if possessed; when I caught up to him and snapped him out of it he didn't realize what he was doing, and was a long way away from where he expected himself to be. These are people I actually give a shit about [pc.name], and this is the second time Tollus is fucking around with folks I actually care for. When I get my hands on him... he's not escaping this time, I tell you. I'll throttle him with my own two hands for everything he's done, not just to me, but to everyone else as well." |"The Lumians? They've been here ever since I arrived in the Rift, have been here since the Godswar, according to the locals. I've never seen fit to bother them much — you can occasionally see some of them out and about the ice doing... whatever it is that they do, and every now and then the elves send up a supply convoy to the keep. I don't think even Tollus and his bastards would be foolhardy enough to try and attack one of those — as tempting a prize as it might be for them, divine warriors aren't something they're willing to face head-on just yet. "If you want to get involved with them, I guess there's no harm in knocking on their door and asking... but I personally keep my distance. Like it or not, I have to share the locals' assessment that they'd be far too snooty to associate with the likes of a weather-worn wolf like me. All warm and comfortable behind those thick stone walls of theirs, with bread and meat delivered up the glacier every week or two — it's like they don't even feel anything of the way the other peoples of the Rift live, and they don't seem to do any useful work whatsoever.[pc.ra valkyrie | Present company excluded, of course. ]" That's a rather bitter tone to take... "If only they could be assed to get out from behind their walls and take on Tollus, I'm sure Lumia and her legions would have this whole mess sorted out within a week, two at most. That they aren't already doing so implies that there's either something more important on their hands that they're dealing with, in which case I should be scared shitless, or that they can't be assed do get out and clean up Tollus and his filth, in which case I should also be scared shitless, if for very different reasons. Either way, I'm not sure if their explanation is going to be any good in my eyes. Feels like a dereliction of duty to me, honestly." |"There's no wood in these mountains — sure, there're plants of a sort, but they mostly melt rather than burn," Gweyr says with a rueful smile. You've noticed that. Instead of burning wood, she's burning these black rocks she's got piled up by the entrance to her home... "It's coal. A strange thing to find up in this miserable snowball, but there're seams of it in the mountains aplenty; maybe this place wasn't always frozen, or the earth moved, or... something. The jotuns sometimes dig out a bunch when they expand their mountain fortresses, but they don't really have any use for fire; they don't even cook their food all the time. Most of it gets traded to the avanai for things... or to me. When the giants aren't forthcoming, I have to go to the trouble of digging out some myself from one of the many exposed seams I know of, but it's terrible, aching work and it screws up your lungs something terrible, even for someone like me. I'd rather avoid it as much as I can." ] "

rows.original: [rand |"Let me tell you, Garth wasn't very much of anything when he tried to join up with my company. Scrawny little runt, underfed, kicked out from amongst his own people for stealing from them. Good with a knife, but not much else. My lieutenants were of the opinion that I wouldn't gain anything by taking him on, and his presence would be our loss." So what motivated her to accept him into her fold, then? Gweyr grins a sharp, toothy grin. "I guess I kinda liked him. That, and a good portion of our company was made up of people who were given second chances. Just turning him away would've felt... false. Against what we stood for, in a sense. Then again, I remember towering over the scrawny-ass pup that he was and telling him in no uncertain terms that if I caught him stealing from us the same way he'd done to his own folks I'd break his neck with my own two hands, then crush his head with my thighs. Poor bastard popped a boner there and then. Now that was funny. "In the years that followed, I've never been given reason to regret my choice, and Garth himself kind of grew with keeping, so that was nice, too. Like I said, we were all about second chances, and I'm not sure what he would've done had I turned him away." |"I remember when Garth first brought up the idea of building the Frost Hound, of putting down roots. It was scary at the time — the idea of leaving the company and ceding leadership to Llewyn, of settling down to a life that didn't involve putting my head on the line every day. It made sense, of course — we were going to be raising pups pretty soon, and we wanted them to have a better life than we did. Something in my gut hated the idea, maybe worrying that I'd grow soft being a barmaid or something, but I saw the reason in it. We'd be the center of the fledgling village, we'd get to hear all kinds of news passing through, and if my old company ever visited us we'd have accommodations and drink on tap. "After seeing the site, though, I warmed up to the idea. We'd made a lot of contacts during our time as mercenaries, so getting good lumber shipped out here — under guard by my own people — wasn't a problem. While most people pitched in, Garth and I hoisted up the central support beam by ourselves, and I daresay we still did a lot of the work." Yeah, that does remind you... every time something needs to be built in town, people tend to go through Garth, and he always says he knows the best people. No matter what the job is, it's always completed in a fraction of the time one might expect. "Haha! Ha! Sixteen years, and he's still running to the same old dogs to get stuff built. Can't say I blame him, though — they are the best people in the Marches. But back to the point, I guess I took to the life better than I'd imagined I would. There was no way I was cut out to be serving drinks and flashing my tits and ass, so Garth and I hired one of the local girls to do that while I busied myself with the heavy lifting. Logistics, inventory... an army moves on its stomach, [pc.name], and after that a tavern was nothing by comparison. I thought as a girl that I'd know no greater happiness than the rush of battle and the thrill of combat, but as it turned out, I didn't know what happiness was until I settled down with Garth and the pups. Haha! Ha!" Can she elaborate? "Fighting's a rush, that's to be sure. Sweating under your fur with your blood pumping, feeling your heart pound and your ears roar. But this kind of happiness I finally found, you don't need to keep taking more and more of it in ever greater amounts to feel satisfied, and at the time it was strange and new to me. I don't think I would've found it if I hadn't listened to Garth and settled down with him, and my only regret is that it couldn't have lasted longer before it was taken away from me." |"I remembered when Garth first figured out for himself that he gave a shit about me for real. I was having a spot of fun with the lads and lasses in the command tent one day when he came up and asked to speak with me privately; I knew from a single look at him that he was up to something, but I wasn't sure what. At the time... yeah, I figured that he probably was up for fucking, we'd been doing a lot of that lately and it made sense that he wanted more. What I didn't expect was for the poor bastard to propose to me, just straight-up ask if I wanted to be his wife." He just... got her alone in her tent and asked the question? "That's the long and short of it, yes. Closed the flaps, turned around with a stupid sheepish look on his face and said that since he'd gotten me pregnant and I was intent on keeping the pups, he might as well make it official and marry me." So he just said it. You don't know, it sounds a little anticlimactic, even given the circumstances. You'd have at least expected him to try and impress her. "It doesn't work that way, [pc.name], not up in these parts. Life's short and brutal, and doubly so in a mercenary company — if you give a shit about someone else, there's no time for faffing about with rings and roses and that kind of nonsense. You come out and tell that person, and if said person gives a shit back at you they'll tell you as much. I do appreciate that he didn't put me on the spot by asking me in front of all the lads and lasses and pressuring me into accepting that way." Surely, though, since he'd gotten her pregnant with Gywn and Garret, he'd have expected her to accept? Gweyr sighs, and her gaze grows distant. "I wish. [pc.Name], my father was the leader of the company before me, and my mother a camp follower who'd had one too many nights with him. He paid her enough to stick with the company until I was whelped, and then she ran off to the gods know where. It's not an uncommon story — a mercenary company, an army, isn't a place for pups to be conceived and born, but neither is a brothel and yet it still happens. My father was kinder about it and didn't force any of the lasses who wound up pregnant to leave the company, partly so that I had wet nurses when I was really little. But the point is that people grow up in ugly, dirty circumstances and they have to make the most of the hand they're dealt." [pc.bg slumRat |Recalling your own youth on the streets as a slum rat, you nod and gesture for Gweyr to go on. |It's a hard truth to swallow for some. ] "Garth didn't need to propose to me; I... I was thinking of doing what my father had done, raise them as best as I could amongst the company. Someone would need to inherit in the same way I did from my father, after all. That's why when he suggested we marry and settle down in the village that River and Sanders were putting together, I was floored. I'd never have imagined leaving the company, leaving my father's inheritance — it wasn't an easy decision by any means. But the more I thought about it, about what Garth was saying, the more it made sense. "So I said yes." And the rest is history. "I only wish the years in between had lasted longer, but we can't always get what we want. It was more than I expected, maybe more than I deserved." |What was Garth like when traveling with Gweyr's mercenary company? "He was the adventurous type, I remember as much. It wasn't that he didn't like the contracts that were basically easy money — watching fields, patrolling easy roads, manning walls. Well, I take that back: some of those were pretty damned brutal. But even though he performed to every standard that the Crossed Swords demanded of him, that my father had set down, I don't think his heart was truly in it. "No, what his nose was after were the weird contracts we'd receive once in a blue moon: guard a dig site, explore some old Belharan ruins, deal with a monster from whatever pit that it'd crawled out of. He wanted excitement, adventure, but that sort of stuff isn't really what a mercenary company is all about. Sometimes, though, sellswords are all you have to direct at the problem when heroes are in short supply." You nod. "He really liked it, as in really liked. Wouldn't be able to sleep the night before, dreaming of things that we'd find. Of course, it never turned out the way he'd imagine it'd be — instead of the handful braving the ancient mysteries of the unknown, it'd be our entire company methodically sweeping through the place. No great treasures, either, and the clients would always want anything we actually managed to find. "They were all adventures that he mostly made up in his mind, but he was having fun and they kept him going, made him smile. And you need people like that sometimes, they help with morale. Garth realized within a handful of weeks that joining a mercenary company wasn't the way to have adventures like he'd wanted... but it was a reasonable compromise and he never really lost that sense of himself until we finally settled down. Then, and only then, was he willing to let go..." |"Garth always had a better head for numbers than me. Before, I was eyeing him for replacing our quartermaster when the old dog finally retired; it wasn't as if he wasn't already helping with the bookkeeping to begin with. When we settled down and started running the Frost Hound, he was the one with the ledger, and at the end of each week he'd basically come up to me and tell me if we were in the black or red, much in the same way he'd do in our mercenary days. "Now, don't you give me that look — I learned my numbers on my father's knee. I just don't really care for them and would prefer someone else do the bookkeeping, that's all. I'm a big-picture woman, Garth had an eye for the details, and we worked together well. I guess that's one of the reasons the Hound was such a success in the first years of its opening — success as measured by the standards of a small-town tavern, at any rate." ]
rows.translation: [rand |我跟你说，加斯当初试图加入我们公司的时候，其实什么本事都没有。那个瘦巴巴的小家伙，营养不良，还因为偷窃被自己的族人赶了出来。用刀的技术还算不错，但除此之外，实在没什么特别的本领。 我的副手们认为，接纳他并不会给我带来任何好处，相反，他的存在只会给我们带来麻烦。 那么，究竟是什么促使她决定接纳他呢？ 格温尔露出了一抹尖锐而露齿的笑容。 我想，我其实是挺喜欢他的。而且我们公司里也有很多人都是得到了第二次机会才取得现在的成就的。如果直接拒绝他，会让我觉得……有些不对。从某种意义上说，这违背了我们公司的价值观。不过，我记得当时我站在那个瘦弱的小家伙面前，非常明确地告诉他：如果我发现他像对待自己家人那样偷我们的东西，我会亲手扭断他的脖子，然后再用我的大腿碾碎他的头。 那个可怜的家伙当场就射精了，真是太好笑了。 “在之后的那些年里，我从未有过任何后悔自己那个决定的理由，而且加斯本人也在与我的共同生活中逐渐成长，这一点也很不错。 正如我所说，我们都相信第二次机会的重要性，而我也不确定如果我当时拒绝了他，他会做出什么来。 |我记得当初加思第一次提出建造‘霜冻猎犬’，想要在这个地方安定下来的时候，我其实感到很害怕——离开公司，把领导权交给莱文，过上一种不再每天都需要冒风险的生活，这个想法让我感到非常不安。 感知当然了——我们很快就要养小狗了，我们希望它们能拥有比我们更好的生活。但我内心深处却对这个想法感到抵触，或许是因为担心自己会因为当酒吧女招待而变得软弱吧。不过，我也能理解其中的道理。 我们会成为这个新兴村庄的中心，能够听到各种消息的流传；如果我的老公司有来访的打算，我们也能提供住宿和饮品。 “不过，在看过那个地点之后，我开始对这个想法产生了兴趣。 在我们担任雇佣兵的这段时间里，我们结识了许多人，因此让优质的木材在我的亲信的护送下运到这里，并不是什么难题。虽然大多数人都帮忙参与了搬运工作，但加斯和我还是亲自负责起了那根中央支撑梁的搬运，说实话，大部分重活其实都是我们俩完成的。是啊，这确实会让人想起……每次镇上需要修建什么东西的时候，人们都会去找加斯，而他总是说自己认识最合适的人选。无论是什么工作，完成起来所花费的时间总是远低于人们的预期。 哈哈！十六年了，他仍然去找那些老家伙帮忙做事。不过也不能怪他——他们…… 是 马奇地区最优秀的人才们。不过回到正题，我想我适应这种生活的能力比自己想象的要强。我显然不适合干端盘倒酒、卖弄身材的工作，所以加斯和我雇了当地的一个女孩来负责这些事，而我则负责处理那些更繁重的工作——后勤保障、库存管理……毕竟，一支军队是要靠粮食来维持运转的。 [pc.name]与之相比，酒馆简直算不了什么。小时候，我以为没有什么比投入战斗、体验战斗的刺激更令人快乐的了，但直到和加思以及那些小狗们一起安定下来，我才真正明白了什么是幸福。 哈哈！哈！” 她能进一步解释吗？ “战斗确实是一种令人兴奋的体验。当你全身是汗，血液在体内奔腾，感受到心脏剧烈跳动，耳边回响着自己的喘息声时，那种感觉确实很棒。但是这种快乐，是我后来才真正发现的。其实，你并不需要不断地去追求更多、更大的刺激才能获得满足感。当初，这种感觉对我来说确实是很新鲜、很不可思议的。 如果我没有听从加思的建议，没有和他一起静下心来寻找，我想我是永远也找不到它的。我唯一遗憾的是，它没能在我手部中停留更久，就被夺走了。 |我记得当初加斯第一次意识到自己是真的在乎我的时候。有一天，我在指挥帐篷里和小伙伴们一起玩得开心，这时他走过来，要求和我单独谈谈。仅仅看他一眼，我就知道他肯定有什么打算，但我当时并不确定…… 什么当时……嗯，我以为他可能是想发生性关系，最近我们确实经常这样做，所以他想要更多也是情有可原的。但我完全没有预料到，那个可怜的家伙竟然会向我求婚，直接问我是否愿意成为他的妻子。他就……把她带到她的帐篷里，然后提出了那个问题？ “就是这么回事，没错。他关上了帐篷的门，转身时脸上带着那种傻傻的、害羞的表情，然后说既然他已经让我怀孕了，而我也打算把孩子生下来，那他还不如正式跟我结婚吧。所以他就这么直接说出来了。你不知道，就算考虑到当时的情况，这句话听起来也显得有点虎头蛇尾。你至少会期望他试着给她留下好印象吧。 “事情并不是这样的。 [pc.name]在这地方可不是这样。人生短暂而残酷，在雇佣兵队伍里更是如此——如果你真的在乎别人，就根本没有时间去搞什么浪漫的事情。你直接把心里的话说出来，如果对方也在乎你，他们也会同样坦诚地告诉你。 我确实很感激他没有在所有人和面前问我这个问题，也没有逼我非得接受才行。 不过，既然他让她怀上了Gywn和Garret，他应该也预料到她会同意吧？ 格温尔叹了口气，她的目光变得恍惚起来。“我希望能如此。 [pc.Name]在我之前，我父亲是这家公司的负责人，而我母亲则是一个追随他的人，和她在一起度过了许多夜晚。他给了她足够的钱，让她留在公司里，直到我出生；之后，她就不知去了哪里。 这样的故事并不少见——雇佣兵公司或军队本来就不是适合女性生育的地方，妓院也同样如此，但这种情况还是会发生。我父亲对待这类事情比较宽容，他没有强迫那些怀孕的女子离开公司，这样在我还很小的时候，我就有奶妈来照顾我。 但关键在于，人们是在恶劣、肮脏的环境中长大的，他们必须充分利用自己所拥有的条件。 [pc.bg slumRat |回想起自己年轻时在街头过着贫民生活，你点了点头，示意格韦尔继续说下去。 |对某些人来说，这个事实确实很难接受。 ] 加斯没有。 需要 他向我求婚了；我……我原本在考虑是否应该像我父亲那样，尽我所能在公司里抚养他们。毕竟，总得有人来继承我的父亲留下的事业。因此，当他提议我们结婚，然后在River和Sanders正在筹备的那个村庄安顿下来时，我简直惊呆了。 我从未想过会离开这家公司，放弃我父亲留下的遗产——这个决定绝非易事。但当我越深入思考，越仔细回味加思的话，就越觉得这个决定是有道理的。 “于是，我选择了同意。剩下的，就是历史了。 “我只希望那些在一起的时光能更长一些，但我们总是无法得到我们想要的一切。这一切超出了我的预期，也许也超出了我应得的。 |加斯和格韦尔的雇佣兵队伍一起出行时，他是怎样的一个人呢？ “我记得，他是个喜欢冒险的人。并不是说他不喜欢那些能轻松赚到钱的任务——比如看守田地、在安全的道路上巡逻、负责守卫城墙之类的工作。 好吧，我收回刚才的话：其中有些确实残酷到了极点。但尽管他完全满足了“十字剑组织”对他提出的所有要求，也完全符合我父亲设定的标准，我认为他内心其实并没有真正投入其中。 不，他真正感兴趣的其实是那些偶尔才会收到的奇怪任务：守卫挖掘现场、探索贝尔哈兰的古老遗迹、对付从某个坑里爬出来的怪物。他想要刺激和冒险，但这类事情其实并不是雇佣兵公司的主要业务所在。 不过，有时候当英雄数量不足时，雇佣兵就成了解决这个问题的唯一手部段。” 你点了点头。 “他真的很喜欢这个想法，我是说…… 真的 太让人兴奋了。前一天晚上根本睡不着，满脑子都是我们会发现的东西。当然，结果从来都不会像他想象的那样——那些勇敢面对未知古老神秘的事物的人并不是少数几个人，而是我们整个团队，有条不紊地对那个地方进行了彻底的搜查。 里面也没有什么珍贵的宝物，而客户们总是想要我们真正找到的东西。 “那些都只是他自己在脑海中虚构出来的冒险故事，但他说起来很开心，这些故事也让他继续坚持下去，让他露出笑容。 有时候，你确实需要这样的人，他们能够帮助提升团队的士气。加思在短短几周内就意识到，加入雇佣兵组织并不是他想象中那种冒险的生活方式……但这也是一种合理的折中方案。直到我们最终安定下来，他才真正找回了自我。 直到那时，他才终于愿意放手部…… |加斯在处理数字方面总是比我更在行。之前，我就考虑过等我们的财务主管退休后让他接替这个职位；毕竟他之前就已经在帮忙处理账务工作了。 当我们安定下来开始经营“霜猎犬”公司后，负责管理账目的就是他。每周结束时，他都会来找我，告诉我我们的经营是盈利还是亏损——这种方式，和我们在做佣兵那段日子时一模一样。 现在，别用那种眼神看我——我可是跟着我父亲学习的，那些数字知识都是他教给我的。我只是对它们不太感兴趣，更希望别人来负责记账工作，仅此而已。我是一个注重整体的人，而加斯则擅长关注细节，我们俩配合得很好。 我想，这大概也是为什么“猎犬酒馆”在开业最初的几年里能够取得如此成功的原因吧——至少，用小镇酒馆的标准来衡量的话，它确实是成功的。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Let me tell you, Garth wasn't very much of anything when he tried to join up with my company. Scrawny little runt, underfed, kicked out from amongst his own people for stealing from them. Good with a knife, but not much else. My lieutenants were of the opinion that I wouldn't gain anything by taking him on, and his presence would be our loss." So what motivated her to accept him into her fold, then? Gweyr grins a sharp, toothy grin. "I guess I kinda liked him. That, and a good portion of our company was made up of people who were given second chances. Just turning him away would've felt... false. Against what we stood for, in a sense. Then again, I remember towering over the scrawny-ass pup that he was and telling him in no uncertain terms that if I caught him stealing from us the same way he'd done to his own folks I'd break his neck with my own two hands, then crush his head with my thighs. Poor bastard popped a boner there and then. Now that was funny. "In the years that followed, I've never been given reason to regret my choice, and Garth himself kind of grew with keeping, so that was nice, too. Like I said, we were all about second chances, and I'm not sure what he would've done had I turned him away." |"I remember when Garth first brought up the idea of building the Frost Hound, of putting down roots. It was scary at the time — the idea of leaving the company and ceding leadership to Llewyn, of settling down to a life that didn't involve putting my head on the line every day. It made sense, of course — we were going to be raising pups pretty soon, and we wanted them to have a better life than we did. Something in my gut hated the idea, maybe worrying that I'd grow soft being a barmaid or something, but I saw the reason in it. We'd be the center of the fledgling village, we'd get to hear all kinds of news passing through, and if my old company ever visited us we'd have accommodations and drink on tap. "After seeing the site, though, I warmed up to the idea. We'd made a lot of contacts during our time as mercenaries, so getting good lumber shipped out here — under guard by my own people — wasn't a problem. While most people pitched in, Garth and I hoisted up the central support beam by ourselves, and I daresay we still did a lot of the work." Yeah, that does remind you... every time something needs to be built in town, people tend to go through Garth, and he always says he knows the best people. No matter what the job is, it's always completed in a fraction of the time one might expect. "Haha! Ha! Sixteen years, and he's still running to the same old dogs to get stuff built. Can't say I blame him, though — they are the best people in the Marches. But back to the point, I guess I took to the life better than I'd imagined I would. There was no way I was cut out to be serving drinks and flashing my tits and ass, so Garth and I hired one of the local girls to do that while I busied myself with the heavy lifting. Logistics, inventory... an army moves on its stomach, [pc.name], and after that a tavern was nothing by comparison. I thought as a girl that I'd know no greater happiness than the rush of battle and the thrill of combat, but as it turned out, I didn't know what happiness was until I settled down with Garth and the pups. Haha! Ha!" Can she elaborate? "Fighting's a rush, that's to be sure. Sweating under your fur with your blood pumping, feeling your heart pound and your ears roar. But this kind of happiness I finally found, you don't need to keep taking more and more of it in ever greater amounts to feel satisfied, and at the time it was strange and new to me. I don't think I would've found it if I hadn't listened to Garth and settled down with him, and my only regret is that it couldn't have lasted longer before it was taken away from me." |"I remembered when Garth first figured out for himself that he gave a shit about me for real. I was having a spot of fun with the lads and lasses in the command tent one day when he came up and asked to speak with me privately; I knew from a single look at him that he was up to something, but I wasn't sure what. At the time... yeah, I figured that he probably was up for fucking, we'd been doing a lot of that lately and it made sense that he wanted more. What I didn't expect was for the poor bastard to propose to me, just straight-up ask if I wanted to be his wife." He just... got her alone in her tent and asked the question? "That's the long and short of it, yes. Closed the flaps, turned around with a stupid sheepish look on his face and said that since he'd gotten me pregnant and I was intent on keeping the pups, he might as well make it official and marry me." So he just said it. You don't know, it sounds a little anticlimactic, even given the circumstances. You'd have at least expected him to try and impress her. "It doesn't work that way, [pc.name], not up in these parts. Life's short and brutal, and doubly so in a mercenary company — if you give a shit about someone else, there's no time for faffing about with rings and roses and that kind of nonsense. You come out and tell that person, and if said person gives a shit back at you they'll tell you as much. I do appreciate that he didn't put me on the spot by asking me in front of all the lads and lasses and pressuring me into accepting that way." Surely, though, since he'd gotten her pregnant with Gywn and Garret, he'd have expected her to accept? Gweyr sighs, and her gaze grows distant. "I wish. [pc.Name], my father was the leader of the company before me, and my mother a camp follower who'd had one too many nights with him. He paid her enough to stick with the company until I was whelped, and then she ran off to the gods know where. It's not an uncommon story — a mercenary company, an army, isn't a place for pups to be conceived and born, but neither is a brothel and yet it still happens. My father was kinder about it and didn't force any of the lasses who wound up pregnant to leave the company, partly so that I had wet nurses when I was really little. But the point is that people grow up in ugly, dirty circumstances and they have to make the most of the hand they're dealt." [pc.bg slumRat |Recalling your own youth on the streets as a slum rat, you nod and gesture for Gweyr to go on. |It's a hard truth to swallow for some. ] "Garth didn't need to propose to me; I... I was thinking of doing what my father had done, raise them as best as I could amongst the company. Someone would need to inherit in the same way I did from my father, after all. That's why when he suggested we marry and settle down in the village that River and Sanders were putting together, I was floored. I'd never have imagined leaving the company, leaving my father's inheritance — it wasn't an easy decision by any means. But the more I thought about it, about what Garth was saying, the more it made sense. "So I said yes." And the rest is history. "I only wish the years in between had lasted longer, but we can't always get what we want. It was more than I expected, maybe more than I deserved." |What was Garth like when traveling with Gweyr's mercenary company? "He was the adventurous type, I remember as much. It wasn't that he didn't like the contracts that were basically easy money — watching fields, patrolling easy roads, manning walls. Well, I take that back: some of those were pretty damned brutal. But even though he performed to every standard that the Crossed Swords demanded of him, that my father had set down, I don't think his heart was truly in it. "No, what his nose was after were the weird contracts we'd receive once in a blue moon: guard a dig site, explore some old Belharan ruins, deal with a monster from whatever pit that it'd crawled out of. He wanted excitement, adventure, but that sort of stuff isn't really what a mercenary company is all about. Sometimes, though, sellswords are all you have to direct at the problem when heroes are in short supply." You nod. "He really liked it, as in really liked. Wouldn't be able to sleep the night before, dreaming of things that we'd find. Of course, it never turned out the way he'd imagine it'd be — instead of the handful braving the ancient mysteries of the unknown, it'd be our entire company methodically sweeping through the place. No great treasures, either, and the clients would always want anything we actually managed to find. "They were all adventures that he mostly made up in his mind, but he was having fun and they kept him going, made him smile. And you need people like that sometimes, they help with morale. Garth realized within a handful of weeks that joining a mercenary company wasn't the way to have adventures like he'd wanted... but it was a reasonable compromise and he never really lost that sense of himself until we finally settled down. Then, and only then, was he willing to let go..." |"Garth always had a better head for numbers than me. Before, I was eyeing him for replacing our quartermaster when the old dog finally retired; it wasn't as if he wasn't already helping with the bookkeeping to begin with. When we settled down and started running the Frost Hound, he was the one with the ledger, and at the end of each week he'd basically come up to me and tell me if we were in the black or red, much in the same way he'd do in our mercenary days. "Now, don't you give me that look — I learned my numbers on my father's knee. I just don't really care for them and would prefer someone else do the bookkeeping, that's all. I'm a big-picture woman, Garth had an eye for the details, and we worked together well. I guess that's one of the reasons the Hound was such a success in the first years of its opening — success as measured by the standards of a small-town tavern, at any rate." ] "

rows.original: [rand |"Truth be told, I'm afraid of going back to them. It's part of why I haven't returned home despite everyone who exiled me being gone these days... having to face up to them and provide answers that everyone's refused to give. How am I going to explain Tollus and that day to them? What am I going to say?" Gweyr shakes her head slowly. "And now that we're actually going to be dealing with Tollus, finally have a shot at the bastard, I have to think about what I'm going to say to my pups when I finally get home. Or do you think I'm counting my chickens before they've hatched?" So long as she doesn't go about engineering a heroic death so that she doesn't have to face up to Garret and Gwyn, she'll be able to take it one step at a time. "You... you really think I'd do such a thing?" You shrug. Gweyr lowers her gaze and looks pensively at the cavern floor. "Would I do such a thing? My own father always said that he wanted me to remember him at his prime, that he didn't want my last memories of him to be of a straw-death, lying in bed just waiting for the end. I... did he get his skull stoved in on purpose? No, that couldn't be, he was still strong back then. No, [pc.name], I don't think I'd do such a thing. I still want to go home, even though I'm still afraid of the idea. You don't have to worry about me doing something like that, I'm not so cowardly as to not be able to face up to what I've done. You'll see." |She does know how well Gwyn and Garret have grown over these years, hasn't she? Gweyr pauses at your words, then nods slowly. "I've seen them from afar, from beyond the walls. I've never entered Hawkethorne for these fifteen years, but they've left on occasion with their father, sometimes to pick up stuff from Morwen's down in the valley, sometimes for other matters. I can't say that I would've approved of all the choices they made in life, especially my daughter, but they're making a decent living for themselves and aren't getting into any trouble. That's about as much as a mother could hope for." She can't say that she would approve... you guess that given the context, she's referring to what Gwyn has chosen to do with her life. "Garth tells me that she hates me, thinks I abandoned both her and her brother. Which, to be fair, has an element of truth to it; certainly no one would be seeking to lynch me if I stepped foot in Hawkethorne these days, they're all either dead or left. Maybe that's why sought to be the exact opposite of me in as many ways as she could imagine, to the point of being stupidly submissive and a perpetual puppy. I just..." Now, she knows that can't really be the case... "Is it, though? How do you know? It's what I might have done were I in her place. If my father had abandoned me as a pup, disappeared from my life — those nights when I was young and we were on campaign, lying down in the tent and wondering if he'd come home from battle or not at all... at least Garret is the easygoing kind, from everything I've seen, so that's not too bad. But what am I going to say to Gwyneth when I return?" At least she's looking at it the right way — when she returns, not if she returns. That's a step forward. |"If I could, of course I'd be back with Gwyneth and Garret. If I could, of course I wouldn't have missed all these years of our lives. Who in their right mind would want to give up all that time of being with your own kids, of having the chance to shape them as they grow? "But there's also the knowledge that there're forces out there, forces served by people like that asshole Tollus, who want to make the world a shitty place for your kids to live in. And while ideally you'd be able to fight them and go back home to your kids every day, that rarely ever manages to be the case. Fighting's dangerous. If those kinds of shitheads knew you had vulnerable people you cared about, they'd drag your kids into the fray, no questions asked. So you wind up distancing yourself from them so you can fight for them, wondering when it'll all end so that you can finally go home for good." ... "...And of course, they don't understand and blame you for being away when you do finally return. You know that their bitterness at not being present isn't unjustified, but how do you explain when they're still young and their world is all that matters to them? "...That's why I'm out here. That's why you're out here. To fight these freaks now so that our kids don't have to down the line, under worse circumstances. We're going to be resented by the very pups whom we're fighting for, but that's another price we have to pay, isn't it? After fifteen, sixteen years out here, I just want to go home to my husband and children, make peace with myself so I can do that." |"Gwyneth takes after her father so much, it's uncanny. Well, save for her body — there's a lot of me in there, too. But given how the girl is so easy to please and quick to apologize in the glimpses of her I've had over the years, I can say she certainly didn't get that from my side of the family. Must've been something of my husband's that skipped a generation or two, because even he wasn't that much of a [silly|simp|pushover] when we were younger. Ha ha! Ha! "Sure, she leads a softer life than I do... but I guess that was what we set out to create when Garth and I decided to build the Frost Hound. Give them the chance to at least be able to choose between the sword and the doll. Whether it was something inside of her, or because she hates me that she chose the doll, the choice was there for her to make it, and at least I can feel some pride in that. At the end of it all, my efforts weren't in vain, and even if my blood sleeps for a generation or two I'm sure it'll rise to the fore when it's needed." You think about that a moment. Gwyn's the sweetest, curviest little puppy you could ever imagine — save for the fact that the both of them are broad in stature in the loosest sense of the term, you'd never have imagined that she and Gweyr would be mother and daughter. Certainly not this walking brick of a lupine woman before you... "It's too late to think about what-ifs, anyway," Gweyr murmurs, bowing her head. "I chose to forego my chance to influence her life, and she's her own woman now. The best I can do at this point... is to let go." |"From what little I've seen of and heard about him, Garret's much like I was when I was younger," Gweyr says with a little smile. "That's a good thing... and a bad one, too. I wish I had the kind of wisdom that I have right now when I was younger with all the energy I had back then, but we can't have everything that we want in life. That's why it's important for people of different generations to work well together, that way we all benefit." ... "I see a bit of his father in him, too. He really needs to run around a bit, get that wanderlust out of his system — I sure didn't like traipsing around the heartlands with my father when I was a pup, so he must've gotten it from Garth. I'm sure he'll grow out of it when he gets a bit older like his father did, but then again he's not as much of a [silly|simp|pushover] as his dad was... I wonder how that'll turn out. Hey, what're you looking at me like that for?" It's just funny to hear someone describe Garth as a [silly|simp|pushover]. "Well, maybe not to you or most other people, but to me he damn well was. Ha ha! Ha! I miss my boy; he was the last person I saw on my way out of Hawkethorne. If I'd been around for more of his life..." He's still determined to look for his mother. "So don't you go and tell him where I am," Gweyr replies, wagging a thick furry finger at you. "Please. Just a little more, and we can all go home, I'm sure..." ]
rows.translation: [rand |说实话，我害怕回到他们身边。这也是为什么尽管那些把我流放的人都已经不在了，我还是没有回家……因为我必须面对他们，并且给出那些一直以来都被他们拒绝给出的答案。 我该怎么向他们解释托卢斯以及那天发生的事情呢？该说些什么好？”格温尔缓缓地摇了摇头。“现在我们终于要真正对付托卢斯了，终于有机会报那混蛋的仇了，我得好好想想回家后该怎么跟我的孩子们解释这些事情。 还是说，你认为我是在未发生的事情上过早地高兴起来了呢？” 只要她不刻意去制造一场“英勇的死亡”，从而逃避与加勒特和格温对质，她就能够一步一步地应对这一切。 你……你真觉得我会做出这种事吗？” 你耸了耸肩。 格温尔低下头，若有所思地望着洞穴的地面。会吗？ 我会做出这种事吗？我自己的父亲总是说，他希望我在记忆中保留他最壮年的样子，他不希望我对他的最后印象，是他在床上奄奄一息、等待死亡降临。我……他是被人故意撞碎头骨的吗？不，不可能，那时候他身体还很健壮。不…… [pc.name]我想我是不会做出那种事的。虽然我还是害怕面对这个想法，但我还是想回家。你不必担心我会做出那样的事，我并没有懦弱到连自己做过的事情都不敢面对。你会看到我的。 |她应该很清楚，这些年来格温和加勒特成长得有多快，不是吗？ 格温尔听到你的话后停顿了一下，然后缓缓点了点头。“我从远处看着他们，从城墙之外看着他们。这十五年来，我从未踏入鹰棘镇，但他们偶尔会和他们的父亲一起外出——有时是去山谷里的莫尔文那里取东西，有时则是有其他事情要处理。 我必须承认，对于他们在生活中做出的所有选择，我并不都表示赞同，尤其是我女儿的选择。不过，他们现在能够过上不错的生活，也没有遇到任何麻烦。对于一位母亲来说，这已经算是最好的结果了。她不能说自己会赞同……不过从上下文来看，她指的是格温对自己人生所做出的选择。 “加思告诉我，她恨我，认为我抛弃了她和她的弟弟。 公平地说，这其中确实有一定道理；如今如果我踏入鹰棘镇，肯定没有人会想要对我动粗——那些人要么已经死了，要么早就离开了。也许正因为如此，她才在各个方面努力成为与我完全相反的人，甚至到了愚蠢地顺从他人、永远像个乖巧的小狗一样的地步。 我只是…… 现在，她知道那样是行不通的。 真的 真的是这样吗？你怎么知道的？如果我处在她的位置，我也可能会这么做。如果我的父亲在我还小的时候抛弃了我，从我的生活中消失——那些夜晚，当我们正在征战途中，躺在帐篷里，不知道他是否会从战场上回来，甚至不知道他是否还会回来……至少从我所看到的来看，加勒特是个随和的人，所以这还算不错。但等我回去后，该怎么跟格温妮丝说呢？” “至少她看待这件事的态度是正确的—— 当……的时候 她回来了，但…… 如果 她回来了。这确实是一个进步。 |如果可以的话，我当然会回到格温妮丝和加勒特身边。如果可以的话，我一定会…… 过程 我绝不会错过我们共同度过的这些岁月。哪个神志清醒的人会愿意放弃与自己的孩子共度的时光，放弃在孩子成长过程中塑造他们的可能性呢？ “但是，我们也知道，这个世界上存在着一些势力，有些像那个混蛋托卢斯这样的人在为这些势力效力，他们想要让这个世界变得不再适合你的孩子居住。而理想情况下，你是应该与这些势力抗争的。 以及
