Come on, let's make these people pay for putting me through that." |Quin emerges from the pool with a quick forward flip, scattering droplets of water all over the cold masonry. Your bunny-boy companion shakes himself off, then wrings the water out of his long ears and tail. "Wow, this place sure is miserable." You're sure it used to be better-looking in its heyday. Does he know anything about this? "Not of this place exactly, but Tollus used to be really big into old ruins and the like. I'm not surprised this is where his goons have put up." He peers into the distant darkness. "Don't see any trace of the bastards, though." Patience. This is a big castle, no doubt sized for the giants who once lived here. He'll get to slake his thirst for revenge soon enough. "Revenge?" Quin chuckles dryly. "I guess it may have started as that, but after what I've learned on this journey with you, it's more than just plain revenge. Come on, [pc.name], we've still got a lot of ground to cover. Let's go hunting." |One hand appears on the edge of the pool, followed by another. With all her clothes and fur, the water clinging to Kiyoko weighs a lot, and she spends a good while just wringing the ocean brine out of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails. Is she fine? "It was cold," your fox-wife replies flatly. "Cold and unpleasant. It is not something I wish to experience again, but I understand that my wishes are nothing compared to a matter of such import and immediacy." Ah, she never complains, so for her to do so the descent must have been truly harrowing for her. Truth be told, it wasn't very comfortable for you, either... Kiyoko's only response is to shake herself like a dog, a motion that all at once is most undignified and endearing as droplets of water scatter all over the cold masonry. You chuckle and give your fox-wife a hug for the warmth, then settle back. Ah, her mere presence dispels a little of the gloom that pervades this place. Good thing, you'll need it. |"Whoa!" Atugia's eyes grow as wide as dinner plates as she pulls herself out of the water and takes a look around her. "Actually seeing something like this..." Something about this place catch her fancy? She doesn't answer you immediately, instead stepping forward to trail her fingers along one set of runic carvings on the walls. Atugia looks hopeful for a moment, then shakes her head and lets her shoulders sag — whatever it was she was looking for in the ancient jotun script, it wasn't in there. Is she fine? "Yeah, I'll be okay. It just... it was just a long way down, and I'm a bit out of sorts." She tries to smile, then coughs up a bit of water. "Yeah." |Nimbly clambering out of the pool, Einin doesn't take the hand you offer her and instead hauls herself out of the water under her own power. Even though Imora's tattoo should have protected her from the cold, you notice that your mecian companion is shivering. Something the matter? Einin's only response is to wring the water out of her ears, then cough up a bit of water. Guess not, if she's feeling this well. "I'll be fine," she says at last. "It's just that the thought of confronting those people again..." Bravery isn't the absence of fear, but rather, doing what's right in spite of it. "Yeah, well, that's also for other people." She folds her arms and looks a little downcast. "That, and this place doesn't look like it's got any good loot in it. All this dark and dreariness, without the spark of... that... that thing." You give your mecian companion a pat on the head. Come now, appearances can be misleading, as she knows well enough. You're sure there's got to be something here that the cult hasn't taken to finance their shenanigans up on the surface just yet. |While Ryn might be impervious to the cold, the descent has clearly taken something out of her. She's keeping a brave face for the moment, but the long journey through the utter darkness has her clinging tightly to your fingers as you help her out of the pool. "Lumia's light," she murmurs softly before spitting up a bit of water. "Of which there's none to be had here..." Is she all right? "Just the memory of some childhood nightmares. You can feel it too, can't you?" Feel what? "This place. It's getting into your head, trying to feel out your fears so it can use them against you. Can't you — " No, you can't. "M-Maybe it's just my imagination, then." Sighing, Ryn wrings the water out of her hair and cloak. "That trip down through the water was... unsettling." That, you'll agree with. Is she all right? A nod. "A moment to catch my breath, my champion, and I'll be with you." |While Gweyr examines your surroundings, you take a moment to sit down, dry yourself off, get back your bearings. That trip through the trench was harrowing, even if it wasn't putting you in that much danger directly. This sensation, like the castle itself is getting into your head, trying to feel out your fears so it can use them against you — no, that's silly. And yet even so... Shaking your head, you pull yourself to your feet. ] "Ready to go?" Gweyr says, stepping forward and using the haft of her spear to tap the ground ahead of where she's walking. Wonder why she does that... it's like she does it instinctively at this point. You are. "Good, we shouldn't keep Tollus's ass waiting. It needs a good kicking, after all."
rows.translation: 首先，是沟渠中那些岩石墙壁在轻型线渐弱时逐渐失去了色彩，随后，上方海浪反射出的微轻型也逐渐减弱，最终变成了一道细线，然后彻底消失了。你越往深处沉沦，就越不得不继续向下探索，尽管你的身体会因为足部下没有坚实的地面而产生恐惧感；不久之后，唯一能防止你撞到沟渠墙壁的东西，就只剩下那块被交给你的小珊瑚碎片了——它散发出的微弱轻型芒，将暗影挡在了你的身后。 越来越深…… 从下方涌出的冷水流量越来越大，这减缓了你的下降速度；有什么力量正在以隐秘而强大的力量将这些水推向水面。如果不是因为伊莫拉的魔法纹身，你根本无法判断哪个方向是上方；越来越多的水压在你脆弱而多肉的身体上，这种巨大的压迫力几乎要将你的肺和心脏挤得停止跳动，但伊莫拉的魔法纹身却让你坚持到了最后，让你能够继续呼吸。 仿佛转瞬即逝，漫长的时间就这样过去了。而唯一能够证明这一切并非梦境的证据，就是…… [party.som |格韦尔的手 |[party.compNames] 还有格温尔的双手部 |[party.compNames]手部 ] 终于，你的双足部再次踏上了坚实的地面，落地时扬起了阵阵古老的淤泥和沙尘。你不确定是否遇到了什么障碍，便用珊瑚轻型四处照射，但很快确认——看来你确实已经到达了这条沟渠的下装。 这个地方并非毫无生机——漆黑的暗影中，偶尔会有微弱的轻型点在水面上闪烁片刻，然后又立刻消失不见。当你向前迈步时，你甚至会觉得自己足部下有东西在移动。 正如格韦尔所指出的，她伸出的手部只呈现出一个模糊的轮廓，你也看到了这一点。 那座城堡被埋在壕沟墙之中，有一半的部分突了出来，看起来就像某种岩石构造。破碎的雕像残骸散落在地上：那些巨大的头部和肢体的残片遍布海床，它们的特征显然属于冰巨人——乔顿人。 你越是靠近那些废墟，就越能清楚地看到：这座城堡显然是为巨人建造的，而不是为萨瓦拉那些体型较小的种族设计的——所有的设施都符合巨人的体型，其规模也是据此而设计的。 至于那个邪教组织，他们的存在痕迹显而易见——零散的绳子、旧瓶子、腐烂的木头等等，这些垃圾散落在深海岩石覆盖的沙地上，被随意丢弃在那里，同时也为潜藏在海洋深处的生物提供了食物。显然，这些生物并没有觉得有必要刻意隐藏自己的存在，这也情有可原——毕竟，究竟有什么生物会愿意追赶到这么深的暗影之中去追捕他们呢？ 不过，这样反而让入口更容易被找到。 [pc.weapon] 顺着这些痕迹继续前进——在淤泥和黏土中，那些被重物拖过的地方留下了明显的痕迹，而这些痕迹几乎没有被破坏，因此它们依然清晰地指引着你前进的方向。最终，你来到了一扇巨大的双开门前，但真正的入口其实是在城堡地板下方的一个洞穴，那里的砖石已经坍塌，形成了一个缺口。 向上游去，你伸出手部，深深地吸了一口空气—— 是空气！虽然寒冷而潮湿，有点让人难受，但总归是空气。你连续喘了几口气，感觉水从鼻子和嘴里涌了出来，然后把自己拉到冰冷的石头上，帮着格韦尔也上了陆地。 那头老母狼花了一两秒钟的时间把衣服和毛皮上的水分拧干，然后咳出了肺里剩下的海水。 “蒂拉的奶子……”她低声说道，同时叹了口气，“不知道我们现在在什么地方。 就连那些巨人们自己，也不会讲述他们建造这类事物的辉煌往事；据我所知，他们谈论的始终都是部落生活。 [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran quintillus kiyoko atugia einin etheryn |凯特把自己从水中拉了出来，首先是用胳膊推了自己一下…… [cait.weapon] 她在爬上岸后，咳嗽着、喘着气，花了一些时间把尾巴和头发弄干。 “哦，等我们回去后，我又得把头发和毛色重新染一下了。什么时候 我们会回来的，”格温尔微笑着说道，“保持这种斗志吧，姑娘。现在我们还有更多事情要担心，但等我们回来后，我会按照你的意愿把你的毛色染成任何你想要的颜色，还会教你一些我在行军途中学到的、能让你看起来更漂亮的技巧。不过现在……先让自己保持冷静吧。 |布林特拖着身子从泳池中爬出来，看到自己终于又能站在坚实的地面上了，他显得无比欣慰。他摇掉头发上的海水，而他的弥诺陶洛斯伙伴则满脸敬畏地环顾四周。 哇，这可真够大的。” 从他嘴里说出来，这已经算是夸奖了，不过这也挺意料之中的，对吧？毕竟这个地方应该是巨人们建造的，所以规模这么大也是理所当然的。 是啊，但是……”布林特托着下巴，若有所思地说，“当我离开科尔米诺斯的时候，我根本想象不出还有比那里更宏伟、更壮观的地方。而这里看起来，似乎正处于它的鼎盛时期。我想，在我们的这段旅程中，我确实学到了很多东西。他确实离开了家去看看这个世界，对吧？嗯，他的愿望终于实现了。” “是啊，我当时根本没想过自己会真的去那么远的地方。 [silly |海底两万里 |一直深入到海洋的最深处 ] 当我第一次离开那个村庄的时候。”布林特擦去脸上最后一滴咸水，然后站了起来。 [brint.weapon] 并凝视着前方的暗影。“所以，你想让我来带头吗？ |布蕾妮拖着身子爬出了泳池，终于能够再次站在坚实的地面上，她看起来无比欣慰。她摇掉头发上的海水，那位牛仔风格的同伴则满脸敬畏地环顾四周。 哇，这可真够大的。” 从她嘴里说出来，这已经算是夸奖了，不过这也挺符合常理的，对吧？毕竟这个地方应该是巨人建造的，所以规模巨大也是理所当然的。 是啊，但是……”布蕾妮一边拧干头发中的水分，一边若有所思地说，“当我离开科尔米诺斯的时候，我根本想象不出还有比那里更宏伟、更壮观的地方。而这里看起来，似乎正处于它的鼎盛时期。我想，在我们的这段旅程中，我确实学到了很多东西。嗯，她确实离开了家去看看这个世界。嗯，她的愿望终于实现了。” “是啊，我当时根本没想过自己会真的走到这个地步。 [silly |海底两万里 |一直深入到海洋的最深处 ] 当我第一次离开那个村庄的时候……”布蕾妮擦去脸上最后一滴咸水，然后站了起来。 [brienne.weapon] 并凝视着前方的暗影。“所以，你想让我来带头吗？ |咳嗽着、喘息着，阿罗娜艰难地爬上了陆地。 [arona.weapon] 首先，然后是她的其他部分。当她从泳池中冲出来时，水像瀑布一样从她身上倾泻而下，她不停地咳嗽、喘息，同时还发出吼叫和低吼声。 “靠，太冷了！ 像她这样一位来自Sailgraves的女性来说，这种说法肯定有一定的道理。 “人们说……人们说，深海里充满了溺水的水手部们的鬼魂，它们无法进入来世。 该死，我觉得在我们船沉的时候，我在那里的某个地方看到了我的爷爷。我以前还见过他几次，那时候他还只是个小孩子，但他的船在一次袭击中被击沉了，他再也没有能回家。 你在下山的路上根本没看到任何鬼魂或类似的东西。 阿罗娜轻轻拍了拍你的后脑勺：“你当然看不到啦，笨蛋。他…… 我的 爷爷，那不是你的。” 其实你并不是这个意思，但是……好吧。 阿罗娜甩掉手部上的咸水，紧紧握住了手部中的东西。 [arona.weapon]凝视着暗影中的某处，他心想：“该死。为了应对这种情况，我最好在这里能找到一些强大的对手部，因为否则…… 我 在这种地方，我可不想和任何东西发生关系。只是个直觉而已，就像赫蕾莎会说的那样。 |阿兹兰费力地从水池中爬出来，咳嗽着、喘着气，这样的样子实在不符合一位蜂巢骑士的身份。她的翅膀在空气中扑腾着。你走上前，帮她从水中爬出来，然后让她站稳身子。 [azyrran.weapon] 她现在没事吧？ “我、我没事。”阿兹兰喘着气说道，然后猛地向前倾倒，把肺里的水都吐了出来，发出一阵相当不体面的声音。“不过我得承认，我永远都无法习惯呼吸水的这种感觉……就是觉得…… 错误然后就是那种仿佛在水中坠落的感觉……呃。” 嗯，本来就应该这样吧——她毕竟是个维斯帕兰人，又不是希奥克人或其他任何水生种族。她的归宿应该在蜂巢里，而不是海浪之下。 还有那些重型的几丁质物质压在她身上…… “我们只是在做职责要求我们做的事情而已，而且——”她又一次摇摇晃晃地站了起来。 是啊，不管是不是海水，不管有没有逞强表现，她的情况其实并不乐观。 你找到一些碎石，便坐在那里等阿兹兰恢复过来，同时观察周围的环境。过了好一会儿，她才终于摆脱了寒冷、盐分以及湿气的困扰，最终站了起来，活动了一下四肢，看起来状态已经好多了。 准备好了吗？ “我已经准备得足够充分了。快点，让我们让那些让我遭受那些痛苦的人付出代价吧。 |奎因用一个快速的前空翻从水池中跃出，水花四溅，洒在了冰冷的石墙上。你的小兔子伙伴抖了抖身体，然后把长耳朵和尾巴上的水拧干。 哇，这个地方真是太破败了。” “你确定它在鼎盛时期肯定比现在好看多了吧？他对此了解些什么吗？” “不是关于这个地方的具体情况，不过托卢斯以前对古老的遗迹之类的东西非常感兴趣。 我并不惊讶他的那些手部下会把这里作为藏身之处。”他凝视着远处的暗影，“不过，却看不到那些混蛋的任何踪迹。” 耐心点。这可是一座巨大的城堡，毫无疑问，它的规模是为曾经居住在这里的巨人们准备的。 他很快就能满足自己的复仇欲望了。 “复仇？”奎因干笑道，“我想一开始或许确实是出于复仇的念头，但在与你一同经历这段旅程之后，我发现，这已经不仅仅是单纯的复仇了。 来吧， [pc.name]我们还有很多工作要做，让我们开始行动吧。 |一只手部出现在池边，紧接着另一只手部也出现了。由于身上穿着所有的衣服，身上还覆盖着毛发，水附着在清子身上，使得她的体重大大增加。因此，她花费了相当长的时间才把身上多余的水分拧干。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 她没事吧？” “天气太冷了，”你的狐狸妻子平淡地回答，“又冷又难受。我真不想再经历那种感觉，但我也明白，与这样重要且紧迫的事情相比，我的愿望根本算不了什么。啊，她从来都不会抱怨，所以她这次之所以会这么说，一定是那段下降过程实在太折磨人了。说实话，对你来说也并不舒服…… 清子的唯一反应就是像狗一样摇晃身体，这个动作瞬间显得既不体面又十分惹人喜爱，水珠也因此散落在冰冷的石墙上。你轻声笑了笑，然后抱了抱你的狐狸妻子，感受着那份温暖，随后便重新坐了下来。 啊，她的出现让这个地方弥漫的阴郁气氛稍微消散了一些。幸好，你会需要这种气氛的。 |哇！”阿图吉娅从水中爬出来，眼睛瞪得像餐盘一样大，环顾四周说道：“真正亲眼看到这样的景象……” 这个地方似乎有什么地方吸引了她？ 她没有立即回答你，而是走上前，用手部指轻轻触摸着墙上那些符文雕刻。阿图吉娅有那么一刻显得充满希望，但随后她摇了摇头，肩膀也耷拉了下来——显然，她在那些古老的约顿文字中寻找的东西，并没有找到。 她没事吧？ “嗯，我应该没什么大问题。只是……掉下来的距离太长了，现在有点不舒服。”她试图微笑，但随后又咳出了一口水。“嗯。 |艾宁灵巧地爬出了水池，她并没有接受你伸出的手部，而是依靠自己的力量从水中爬了出来。尽管伊莫拉的纹身本应让她免受寒冷的影响，但你还是注意到，你的这位机械伙伴正在发抖。 怎么了？” 艾宁唯一的反应就是把耳朵里的水拧出来，然后咳出一些水来。看来她并没有觉得有什么大问题。 “我没事的，”她终于说道。 只是一想到要再次面对那些人……” 勇气并不是没有恐惧，而是在恐惧存在的情况下依然去做正确的事情。 “嗯，其实这也是为了别人。她双臂交叉，看起来有些沮丧。“而且这个地方看起来也没什么好东西可捡的。到处都是暗影和阴郁的气氛，完全没有任何……那种……活力。 东西你轻轻拍了拍你的机械伙伴的脑袋。来吧，外表有时候会骗人，她自己也深谙这一点。你肯定觉得，里面肯定有什么…… 某个东西 事实上，这个邪教组织目前还没有公开通过金融手部段来资助他们的各种非法活动。 |虽然瑞恩似乎对寒冷毫无感觉，但这段下坡路程显然让她消耗了不少体力。目前她还在强忍着，但当你帮助她走出水池时，她紧紧抓住了你的手部指——显然，这段在完全暗影中的长途跋涉让她感到非常疲惫。 卢米娅的轻型芒……”她轻声呢喃着，随后吐出了一口水，“而在这里，这样的轻型芒是根本不存在的……” 她没事吧？ “只是有些童年噩梦的记忆罢了。 你也能感觉到这一点，对吧？” “感觉到什么？” “就是这个地方。它正在侵入你的思维，试图探查你的恐惧，这样就能利用这些恐惧来对付你。 你就不能——” “不行，你真的做不到。” “也许只是我的想象而已。”瑞恩叹了口气，把头发和斗篷上的水拧干，“那次在水中的经历…………真是让人不安。” 你会同意的。她现在没事吧？ 他点了点头：“让我稍作休息，我的勇士，很快就会陪在你身边的。 |当格韦尔观察着你的周围环境时，你找了个机会坐下来，擦干身上的水，重新整理思绪。那次在沟渠中的穿越实在令人胆战心惊，尽管它并没有直接给你带来太大的危险。这种感觉……就好像那座城堡本身正在侵入你的脑海，试图探查你的恐惧，然后利用这些恐惧来对付你——不，这种想法太荒谬了。然而，即便如此…… 你摇摇头，站了起来。 ] 准备好了吗？”格韦尔说着，向前迈了一步，用长矛的柄在前进的路面上轻敲了几下。不知道她为什么这么做……现在看来，这已经成了她的本能反应。 “好了，我们不能再让托卢斯等着了。毕竟，他确实该受到应有的惩罚。
rows.raw: " First, it's the trench's rocky walls that lose color as the light fades, then the glimmer of light from the waves above shrinks to a seam before disappearing completely. Further and further you sink into the darkness, forcing yourself to descend ever deeper even though your body shies at the sensation of falling with no solid ground underfoot; soon enough, the only thing keeping you from scraping against the trench's walls is the small shard of coral Seastone handed you, keeping the darkness at bay with a faint circle of light. Deeper and deeper... The current of cold water welling up from below strengthens, slowing your descent; something is driving it up to the surface with insidious force. It not for it, telling which direction is up would be hard; more and more water presses in upon your frail, fleshy body, an intense crushing force that threatens to squeeze the life out of your lungs and heart, but Imora's magical tattoo keeps you alive and breathing to the bitter end. An eternity passes by in what feels like the blink of an eye, the only tell that this isn't some kind of dream the presence of [party.som |Gweyr's hand |[party.compNames] and Gweyr's hands |[party.compNames]' hands ] in your own. But at last, your feet touch solid ground, kicking up a cloud of ancient silt and sand as you land. Wondering if you've just hit a snag, you shine the coral light around, but soon confirm that you've reached the bottom of the trench, by all appearances. This place isn't without life of its own — the pitch-black darkness is populated with pinpricks and flashes of light that flicker briefly in the water before winking out, and you swear you feel things moving against your feet as you step forward. And then as Gweyr points, her outstretched hand but a dim silhouette, you see it too. The castle's buried in trench wall, half of it jutting out like some kind of rock formation. The shattered remains of statues lie all about the ground: the remains of colossal heads and limbs lying strewn on the seabed, their features undeniably that of ice giants — jotuns. The closer you draw to the ruins, the more obvious it becomes that the castle is made for giants and not the smaller races of Savarra — everything is jotun-sized, and scaled to match. As for the cult, signs of their presence are evident — scattered bits of rope, old bottles, rotting wood and more litter the rocky sand of the depths, strewn around without care and feeding whatever creatures that lurk this deep beneath the surface of the ocean. They mustn't feel particularly inspired to hide their presence here, and rightly so — what sort of creature could, or would, pursue them all the way down into the deep dark? Still, that makes it easy to find the entrance. [pc.weapon] in hand, you follow the trail — tracks have been left in the silt and clay where heavy loads have been dragged across it, and without much to disturb them they've lingered for you to find. You arrive at a set of great double doors, but the actual entrance is a hole in the underside of the castle's floor, a break where the masonry's fallen away. Swimming upwards, you reach out and take a deep lungful of — — Air! It's cold and clammy, more than a little miserable, but it's air all right. You heave a couple of times, feeling water gush out of your nose and mouth, then haul yourself up onto cold stone and help Gweyr up onto solid ground. The old wolfess takes a second or two to wring the water out of her clothes and fur, then coughs the last of the sea out from her lungs. "Tira's tits," she mutters, heaving a sigh. "Wonder where we are. Even the jotuns themselves don't tell any stories about their glory days building this kind of thing; as far as I've ever known them it's been all about the tribal life." [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran quintillus kiyoko atugia einin etheryn |Cait hauls herself out of the water, first shoving her [cait.weapon] onto dry land before pushing herself up and over. With her being as top-heavy as she is, it takes both you and Gweyr helping her to get her front up up and out of the water, but once that's done and over with the rest is easy by comparison. Coughing and spluttering, Cait takes a moment to dry off, wringing her tail and squeezing her hair dry. "Ooohh. I'm going to have to dye my hair and fur again when we get back." "When we get back," Gweyr affirms with a small smile. "Keep up that morale, girl. We've got more things to worry about now, but when we make it back I'll dye your fur all you want, teach you a couple tricks I learned to look good on the march. For now, though... keep yourself together." |Brint drags himself out of the pool, looking very, very relieved at finally being able to walk on solid ground once more. Shaking salt water out of his hair, your minotaur companion looks around him with an expression of awe on his face. "Wow. Now this is big." Coming from him, that's a compliment, but it's to be expected, isn't it? This place was presumably built by giants, after all. Makes sense it'd be giant-sized. "Yeah, but..." Brint taps his chin and looks thoughtful. "When I left Khor'minos, I couldn't imagine anywhere bigger or grander than it. This looks like it might have been in its heyday. I guess I've learned a lot so far on our travels..." He did leave his home to see the world, didn't he? Well, he got his wish. "Yeah, I didn't imagine I'd be going all the way [silly |twenty thousand leagues under the sea |all the way to the bottom of the ocean ] when I first left the village." Wiping the last of the salt water from his face, Brint hefts his [brint.weapon] and peers into the gloom ahead. "So, you want me to take point?" |Brienne drags herself out of the pool, looking very, very relieved at finally being able to walk on solid ground once more. Shaking salt water out of her hair, your cowgirl companion looks around her with an expression of awe on her face. "Wow. Now this is big." Coming from her, that's a compliment, but it's to be expected, isn't it? This place was presumably built by giants, after all. Makes sense it'd be giant-sized. "Yeah, but..." Brienne looks thoughtful as she wrings water out of her hair. "When I left Khor'minos, I couldn't imagine anywhere bigger or grander than it. This looks like it might have been in its heyday. I guess I've learned a lot so far on our travels..." She did leave her home to see the world. Well, she got her wish. "Yeah, I didn't imagine I'd be going all the way [silly |twenty thousand leagues under the sea |all the way to the bottom of the ocean ] when I first left the village." Wiping the last of the salt water from her face, Brienne hefts her [brienne.weapon] and peers into the gloom ahead. "So, you want me to take point?" |Coughing and spluttering, Arona claws her way onto dry land, [arona.weapon] first, followed by the rest of her. Water pours off her body in cascades as she bursts out of the pool , hacking and coughing, roaring and growling. "Fuck, that's cold!" Coming from a Sailgraves woman like her, that's got to be something. "They say... they say that the deep ocean's haunted by the ghosts of drowned sailors and the like, unable to move on to the next life. Damn, I think I saw my granddad in there somewhere while we were sinking. I saw him a couple times as a sprat, but his ship got scuttled on a raid and he never made it home." Really? You didn't spot any ghosts or anything on your way down. Arona taps you lightly on the back of your head. "Of course you wouldn't, you idiot. He's my granddad, not yours." That wasn't what you meant, but... all right. Flicking the worst of the salt water from her hands, Arona clenches her [arona.weapon], peering into the darkness. "Fuck. For that, I'd better have something good to fight down here, because even I wouldn't want to fuck anything in a place like this. Just a hunch, as Hretha would say." |Azyrran hauls herself hand over foot from the pool, coughing and spluttering in a fashion most unbecoming of a hive knight while her wings beat at the air. You step up, give her a hand out of the water, and let her right herself with [azyrran.weapon] in hand. Is she all right? "I-I'm fine." Azyrran gasps, then lurches forward, emptying her lungs of water with a most undignified noise. "But I'll say that I'll never get used to the idea or feeling of breathing water. It just feels wrong. And then there's the sensation of falling through the water... ugh" Well, it should — she's a vesparan, not a siorc or any of the water-dwelling peoples. Her place is in a hive, not under the waves. Then there's all the chitin weighing her down... "We do what duty demands of us, and — " she lurches again. Yeah, salt water or not, bravado or not, she's not fine. You find a bit of rubble and sit down Azyrran for a bit while she recovers, the survey your surroundings. It's a while before she shakes off the cold, salt and wet, but eventually she stands and flexes her limbs, looking a bit better for it. Ready to proceed? "As ready as I'll ever be. Come on, let's make these people pay for putting me through that." |Quin emerges from the pool with a quick forward flip, scattering droplets of water all over the cold masonry. Your bunny-boy companion shakes himself off, then wrings the water out of his long ears and tail. "Wow, this place sure is miserable." You're sure it used to be better-looking in its heyday. Does he know anything about this? "Not of this place exactly, but Tollus used to be really big into old ruins and the like. I'm not surprised this is where his goons have put up." He peers into the distant darkness. "Don't see any trace of the bastards, though." Patience. This is a big castle, no doubt sized for the giants who once lived here. He'll get to slake his thirst for revenge soon enough. "Revenge?" Quin chuckles dryly. "I guess it may have started as that, but after what I've learned on this journey with you, it's more than just plain revenge. Come on, [pc.name], we've still got a lot of ground to cover. Let's go hunting." |One hand appears on the edge of the pool, followed by another. With all her clothes and fur, the water clinging to Kiyoko weighs a lot, and she spends a good while just wringing the ocean brine out of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails. Is she fine? "It was cold," your fox-wife replies flatly. "Cold and unpleasant. It is not something I wish to experience again, but I understand that my wishes are nothing compared to a matter of such import and immediacy." Ah, she never complains, so for her to do so the descent must have been truly harrowing for her. Truth be told, it wasn't very comfortable for you, either... Kiyoko's only response is to shake herself like a dog, a motion that all at once is most undignified and endearing as droplets of water scatter all over the cold masonry. You chuckle and give your fox-wife a hug for the warmth, then settle back. Ah, her mere presence dispels a little of the gloom that pervades this place. Good thing, you'll need it. |"Whoa!" Atugia's eyes grow as wide as dinner plates as she pulls herself out of the water and takes a look around her. "Actually seeing something like this..." Something about this place catch her fancy? She doesn't answer you immediately, instead stepping forward to trail her fingers along one set of runic carvings on the walls. Atugia looks hopeful for a moment, then shakes her head and lets her shoulders sag — whatever it was she was looking for in the ancient jotun script, it wasn't in there. Is she fine? "Yeah, I'll be okay. It just... it was just a long way down, and I'm a bit out of sorts." She tries to smile, then coughs up a bit of water. "Yeah." |Nimbly clambering out of the pool, Einin doesn't take the hand you offer her and instead hauls herself out of the water under her own power. Even though Imora's tattoo should have protected her from the cold, you notice that your mecian companion is shivering. Something the matter? Einin's only response is to wring the water out of her ears, then cough up a bit of water. Guess not, if she's feeling this well. "I'll be fine," she says at last. "It's just that the thought of confronting those people again..." Bravery isn't the absence of fear, but rather, doing what's right in spite of it. "Yeah, well, that's also for other people." She folds her arms and looks a little downcast. "That, and this place doesn't look like it's got any good loot in it. All this dark and dreariness, without the spark of... that... that thing." You give your mecian companion a pat on the head. Come now, appearances can be misleading, as she knows well enough. You're sure there's got to be something here that the cult hasn't taken to finance their shenanigans up on the surface just yet. |While Ryn might be impervious to the cold, the descent has clearly taken something out of her. She's keeping a brave face for the moment, but the long journey through the utter darkness has her clinging tightly to your fingers as you help her out of the pool. "Lumia's light," she murmurs softly before spitting up a bit of water. "Of which there's none to be had here..." Is she all right? "Just the memory of some childhood nightmares. You can feel it too, can't you?" Feel what? "This place. It's getting into your head, trying to feel out your fears so it can use them against you. Can't you — " No, you can't. "M-Maybe it's just my imagination, then." Sighing, Ryn wrings the water out of her hair and cloak. "That trip down through the water was... unsettling." That, you'll agree with. Is she all right? A nod. "A moment to catch my breath, my champion, and I'll be with you." |While Gweyr examines your surroundings, you take a moment to sit down, dry yourself off, get back your bearings. That trip through the trench was harrowing, even if it wasn't putting you in that much danger directly. This sensation, like the castle itself is getting into your head, trying to feel out your fears so it can use them against you — no, that's silly. And yet even so... Shaking your head, you pull yourself to your feet. ] "Ready to go?" Gweyr says, stepping forward and using the haft of her spear to tap the ground ahead of where she's walking. Wonder why she does that... it's like she does it instinctively at this point. You are. "Good, we shouldn't keep Tollus's ass waiting. It needs a good kicking, after all." "

rows.original:
Gweyr gives you a glance, then shrugs. "Best to take this carefully, rather than rush it. You're the one best able to act on the information we learned back on the ship, so make whatever preparations you need to go forward.
        
        "Do be mindful, though. I may be able to wait twenty years, but the siorcanna are a hasty people and don't like being kept in a holding pattern."
        
        With that, the wolfess settles in her cross-legged pose and leans back against the cave wall with her eyes closed, seemingly deep in thought.
rows.translation:
格温尔看了你一眼，然后耸了耸肩。“最好谨慎行事，不要急于求成。你才是最能根据我们在船上获得的情报采取行动的人，所以请做好一切必要的准备，然后再继续前进吧。
        
        不过，你一定要记住。我或许可以等待二十年，但那些西奥卡纳人可没有耐心，他们不喜欢被长时间搁置不管。”

说完，这只母狼便盘腿而坐，背靠洞壁闭上了眼睛，似乎陷入了沉思。

rows.original: "Something the matter?" Garret inquires, looking at you over the top of his tankard. "You look pretty out of it." There's something you have to tell him, and he's got to promise he won't freak out or anything when you do, all right? Now that gets Garret's attention; you see his fingers tighten about the handle of his tankard as he sits up just that bit straighter at the table, throwing a furtive glance at his father by the bar. "[var0 |Hit me with it. After that time you told me I'd knocked you up despite me taking the blank powder that Mistress Ivriss sells, I don't think anything can really surprise me anymore. Whatever could top that? |Hey, you're getting all weird, [pc.name]. Look, you can hit me with it, okay? Can't be the strongest man in the world if I can't take something coming out of the blue beyond any day. Just tell me, and I'll roll with the punches. ]" All right, then — he told you to give it to him straight, so you'll do just that. You've found his mom, and you need his help convincing her to come home. Garret's tankard stops halfway to his muzzle, and he slowly sets it down again onto the table with a solid thunk. To his credit, he manages to keep a straight face, throws another glance over his shoulder at Garth, then lowers his voice and looks you dead in the eye. "I'm not sure I heard you right. Mind repeating yourself?" No, he did hear you right. You've found his mother, and you need his help convincing her to come home. Now then, he promised not to be rash about the matter... Garret doesn't say anything for a bit, instead choosing to raise the tankard to his lips and drain it of his father's best mead in one deep draught. With a calm slowness that's very pointedly deliberate, he swallows, smacks his lips and flashes you a sharp-toothed grin. "[var0 |Well, there I go again, saying things and getting ahead of myself. Not that I'm ever going to stop, though. You came this close to surprising me, [pc.name] — didn't quite beat that announcement, but it came pretty damned close. |You're not fucking with me, are you?" No, you aren't. "I should've guessed as much. Maybe I mightn't have believed you, once upon a time... but you've helped both me and my dad out, and word about town is packed with the things you've done out there. Makes a man like me have to work harder to be able to catch up with you in good time. Got to defend the title of strongest man in Savarra, after all[pc.mf |, don't I | — even if you're a woman, yeah ]? ]" "Go on, then. Tell me all about it. But not here — not in the old man's place, not where Gwyn might hear. Not in my home. Take a walk, if you don't mind?" Without waiting for an answer, Garret tumps the empty tankard on the table just loud enough for Garth to turn his head at the noise, then beckons you to step out of the Frost Hound and into Hawkethorne's main square. [dayNight |The daily hubbub of the village at work and the soft tones of River's singing |The village square is largely empty save for a few stragglers — Hawkethorne's grown to the point where the village never completely sleeps — but the soft sighing of the wind as it sweeps down from the glaciers ] provide plenty of cover for your conversation. Keeping to the shadows, the both of you pace in a large circle about the statue, keeping your footfalls muted and tones hushed. It strikes you that Garret is being uncharacteristically serious here, but... it's his mom. If not now, then when? And if not when pertaining to this topic, then what? "So then, my mom. Go on." And you do. It takes a good while to get through the whole story — all the way from meeting her in the rift, to working with her against Tollus's cult, and finally delving into the darkest [silly |dungeon beneath |depths under ] the ocean to face the pelagic nightmare they were attempting to suborn to their purposes. "Ah." To protect itself, the lureling drew out the deepest fears and secret weaknesses of you and your companions, turned them against you. While you don't doubt that it did the same to Gweyr, she hasn't said anything about it to you, nor has she shown any blatant signs of breaking down like everyone else did... on the other hand, you don't believe that she's that hard of a woman to be able to no-sell an ancient eldritch being's terrors. One of the final things she told you was that with the driving of Tollus's cult from the rift and the realization that the adventure she'd just had was her last, she felt like her existence didn't have meaning any more. "But that's not true." Exactly. The both of you walk in silence for a minute or two, soaking in the [dayNight |atmosphere of the town square |chill night wind ] and letting the tale you've just told Garret sink in. At length, he raises his gaze and scratches his chin. "I don't remember if I've told you this before, [pc.name], but I'll say it again anyway: every single memory I have of my old woman is hazy save for her face. An old brick. The smell of blood, without any danger in it. Her hands on my head, for some reason. The streets, filled with snow. She said something to me... it was important, I know, but I don't remember the words. Just that they were important, and that's all." Will he come with you? Up to the rift and onto the ice, to convince his mother that even though her long hunt is over, there's still something worth living for in her later years? Asking Garth is a non-starter. Asking Gwyn is a fool's errand, for the daughter will never forgive the mother. But the son... he just might have the ability and the will to pull it off, might be the only man in all of Savarra capable of accomplishing this feat. Another moment's pause from Garret, and at length he reaches into his vest and pulls out a medallion with a thick golden chain. A glint of light catches the insignia upon its face, that of two crossed swords, and at length he sighs and tucks it away once more. "Probably." Probably? "Look, [pc.name]. Would you do me a favor? Head back to my old man's and wait for me there — I shouldn't be longer than an hour or so. After all you've told me, I just need to go and ask old man Sanders some questions." Hey, he's not to do anything rash — strongest man in Savarra or not, Sanders would kick his ass seven ways before the hour's out. "I didn't say I was going to start a ruckus or anything; I just want some answers. Answers that he's been keeping from me for a long time... [pc.name], I don't doubt that he did what he thought was best, and the pained look on his face every time I asked him the same questions growing up is proof enough that he's still hurting over it. But even after listening to what you've had to say, I still want to hear it from his mouth. "So if you don't mind... wait for me at my old man's place. Like I said, this shouldn't take long." Garret's smiling, but the smile is very obviously forced as he claps you on the shoulder and steps around you, making a beeline for the other side of the village square and the chapel of Velun. You watch his departing form for a little while, wondering if you should go after him, and then the moment passes and he's gone...
rows.translation: 怎么了？”加勒特一边用酒杯遮住眼睛，一边看着你问道，“你看起来有点不对劲啊。” 有件事你必须告诉他，而且你得保证他听到后不会大惊小怪，好吗？ 这个请求终于引起了加勒特的注意。你看到他握着酒杯的手部指紧了紧，他在桌边坐得更直了一些，同时偷偷瞥了瞥吧台那边的他父亲。[var0 |你倒是说说看吧。从那次你告诉我我让你们怀孕了之后，尽管我一直在服用伊弗里斯女士卖的那种避孕药，我觉得再也没有什么事情能真正让我感到惊讶了。还有什么能比这更离谱的呢？ |嘿，你变得有点奇怪了…… [pc.name]听着，你可以用它来打我，好吗？如果连这种突如其来的打击都无法承受，那我怎么可能成为世界上最强大的人呢？只要你告诉我，我会坦然面对的。 ]好吧，那么——他让你直接告诉他实情，你就照做吧。你已经找到了他妈妈，现在需要他的帮助来说服她回家。” 加勒特的酒杯在离他嘴还有半截距离的地方停住了，他缓缓地把它放回了桌上。 咚值得称赞的是，他成功地保持了面无表情的神情，又回头瞥了加斯一眼，然后压低声音，直视着你的眼睛说道： “我不太确定自己听清了你的话。你能再重复一遍吗？不，他确实听清楚了。你找到了他的母亲，现在需要他的帮助来说服她回家。他当初确实承诺过不会轻率处理这件事…… 加勒特沉默了一会儿，然后拿起酒杯，一饮而尽了他父亲珍藏的最上等的蜂蜜酒。 他以一种刻意营造出的从容缓慢的动作，咽下食物，咂了咂嘴唇，然后向你露出一个露着尖锐牙齿的微笑。[var0 |唉，我又开始说话太快、提前把事情讲完了。不过，我也不会因此而停止的。你来了。 这个 差点让我感到惊讶。 [pc.name] — 虽然没有完全达到那个宣传效果，但也已经非常接近了。 |你该不会在跟我开玩笑吧？” “不，我没有。” “我早该猜到的。也许以前我并不会相信你……但你确实帮助过我和我父亲，而且镇上到处都在传你做的那些事。这就让我这样的男人必须更加努力，才能及时赶上你的步伐。毕竟，我还是要捍卫‘萨瓦拉最强男人’的这个头衔的。[pc.mf |难道不是这样吗？ | — 即使你是女性，也没关系。 ]? ]那好吧，那就跟我详细讲讲吧。但不要在这里——不要在老人的家里，也不要让格温听到。也不要在我的家里。如果你不介意的话，我们出去走走吧。” Garret没有等待回答，就把那个空酒壶重重地放在桌子上，声音刚好大到足以让Garth听到动静，然后示意你离开霜犬酒馆，前往鹰棘镇的主广场。 [dayNight |村庄里日常忙碌的场景，以及River轻柔的歌声…… |村庄的广场上空无一人，只有零星几个人影——鹰棘镇已经发展到了这样一个程度：这个村庄从来都没有真正意义上的“夜晚”……只有风从冰川上吹下来的时候，才会发出那种轻柔的叹息声。 ] 你们的谈话需要有足够的掩护。你们俩躲在阴影中，绕着雕像走成一个大圈，脚步尽量轻柔，说话声音也压得很低。你注意到，加勒特这次表现得异常严肃……所以，就是我妈妈。如果不是现在，那还能什么时候呢？如果在这个问题上不是现在，那还能等到什么时候呢？” “那么，就是我妈妈。继续说吧。” 你确实这么做了。花了很长时间才把整个故事讲完——从在裂隙中遇见她，到与她一起对抗托卢斯的邪教，最后深入探讨那些最黑暗的秘密…… [silly |地下迷宫 |深不见底的地方 ] 海洋，面对着那些他们试图利用来达成自己目的的远洋噩梦…… “啊……” 为了保护自己，这个诱饵挖掘出了你和你的同伴内心最深处的恐惧与隐秘弱点，然后将它们用来对付你们。 虽然你毫不怀疑它也对格温尔产生了同样的影响，但她却从未向你提起过这件事，也没有表现出像其他人那样崩溃的迹象……另一方面，你也不认为她是个如此难以被吓倒的人，以至于连一个古老的邪异生物带来的恐惧都无法让她动容。 她最后告诉你的其中一件事是：由于托卢斯的邪教势力被赶出了裂隙，同时也意识到自己刚刚经历的那次冒险已经是最后一次了，她觉得自己的存在已经失去了意义。 但那不是真的。” 确实如此。 你们俩沉默地走了一两分钟，静静地感受着周围的气氛。 [dayNight |城镇广场的氛围 |凉爽的夜风 ] 让他仔细思考你刚刚告诉他的这个故事。过了一会儿，他抬起头，挠了挠下巴。 “我不确定之前有没有跟你说过这个…… [pc.name]但我还是要再说一遍：关于我的那位老妇人，我所有的记忆都模糊不清，只有她的脸庞清晰地留在我的脑海中。一张布满皱纹的脸，散发着血腥的气息，但却没有任何危险的感觉。还有她的手部，不知为何总是放在我的头上。还有那些被积雪覆盖的街道…… 她对我说了些什么……我知道那些话很重要，但我已经想不起来具体内容了。只记得那些话确实很重要，仅此而已。 他会和你一起去吗？会陪你一起前往那片裂隙，一起踏上冰面，去说服他的母亲：尽管她漫长的追寻已经结束，但在她的晚年生活中，仍然有值得继续活下去的理由。 去问加思根本没用，去问格温更是徒劳无功——因为女儿永远也不会原谅自己的母亲。但儿子……他或许拥有完成这件事的能力和决心，也许他是整个萨瓦拉地区唯一有能力做到这一点的人。 加勒特又停顿了片刻，最终他从背心里掏出一枚挂着粗金链子的奖章。奖章正面的图案在轻型线下闪烁着轻型芒——那是两把交叉的剑。最终，他叹了口气，又将奖章收了回去。 大概吧。” “大概？” “听着， [pc.name]你能帮我个忙吗？回到我父亲那里等我吧——我应该不会超过一个小时就回来。听了你告诉我的那些事情，我只需要去问桑德斯老人一些问题而已。” “嘿，他可千万不能做出什么鲁莽的事情来——不管他是不是萨瓦拉最强的人，桑德斯肯定会在一个小时之内把他打得落花流水。” “我并不是说要惹麻烦或者什么的；我只是想要一些答案而已。那些他长期以来一直瞒着我的一些答案…… [pc.name]我毫不怀疑，他确实是做了他认为最正确的事情。而在我成长过程中，每次我问他同样的问题时，他脸上那痛苦的表情，已经足以证明他至今仍在为此事而苦恼。但即便听了你所说的一切，我还是想亲耳听他本人怎么说。 所以，如果你不介意的话……就在我父亲家等我吧。就像我说的，这应该不会花太长时间。” 加勒特面带微笑，但那笑容显然很勉强。他拍了拍你的肩膀，然后从你身边绕过去，径直朝村庄广场的另一边、也就是维伦小教堂的方向走去。 你望着他远去的背影，犹豫着是否应该追上去，然而转眼间，他就消失得无影无踪了……
rows.raw: " "Something the matter?" Garret inquires, looking at you over the top of his tankard. "You look pretty out of it." There's something you have to tell him, and he's got to promise he won't freak out or anything when you do, all right? Now that gets Garret's attention; you see his fingers tighten about the handle of his tankard as he sits up just that bit straighter at the table, throwing a furtive glance at his father by the bar. "[var0 |Hit me with it. After that time you told me I'd knocked you up despite me taking the blank powder that Mistress Ivriss sells, I don't think anything can really surprise me anymore. Whatever could top that? |Hey, you're getting all weird, [pc.name]. Look, you can hit me with it, okay? Can't be the strongest man in the world if I can't take something coming out of the blue beyond any day. Just tell me, and I'll roll with the punches. ]" All right, then — he told you to give it to him straight, so you'll do just that. You've found his mom, and you need his help convincing her to come home. Garret's tankard stops halfway to his muzzle, and he slowly sets it down again onto the table with a solid thunk. To his credit, he manages to keep a straight face, throws another glance over his shoulder at Garth, then lowers his voice and looks you dead in the eye. "I'm not sure I heard you right. Mind repeating yourself?" No, he did hear you right. You've found his mother, and you need his help convincing her to come home. Now then, he promised not to be rash about the matter... Garret doesn't say anything for a bit, instead choosing to raise the tankard to his lips and drain it of his father's best mead in one deep draught. With a calm slowness that's very pointedly deliberate, he swallows, smacks his lips and flashes you a sharp-toothed grin. "[var0 |Well, there I go again, saying things and getting ahead of myself. Not that I'm ever going to stop, though. You came this close to surprising me, [pc.name] — didn't quite beat that announcement, but it came pretty damned close. |You're not fucking with me, are you?" No, you aren't. "I should've guessed as much. Maybe I mightn't have believed you, once upon a time... but you've helped both me and my dad out, and word about town is packed with the things you've done out there. Makes a man like me have to work harder to be able to catch up with you in good time. Got to defend the title of strongest man in Savarra, after all[pc.mf |, don't I | — even if you're a woman, yeah ]? ]" "Go on, then. Tell me all about it. But not here — not in the old man's place, not where Gwyn might hear. Not in my home. Take a walk, if you don't mind?" Without waiting for an answer, Garret tumps the empty tankard on the table just loud enough for Garth to turn his head at the noise, then beckons you to step out of the Frost Hound and into Hawkethorne's main square. [dayNight |The daily hubbub of the village at work and the soft tones of River's singing |The village square is largely empty save for a few stragglers — Hawkethorne's grown to the point where the village never completely sleeps — but the soft sighing of the wind as it sweeps down from the glaciers ] provide plenty of cover for your conversation. Keeping to the shadows, the both of you pace in a large circle about the statue, keeping your footfalls muted and tones hushed. It strikes you that Garret is being uncharacteristically serious here, but... it's his mom. If not now, then when? And if not when pertaining to this topic, then what? "So then, my mom. Go on." And you do. It takes a good while to get through the whole story — all the way from meeting her in the rift, to working with her against Tollus's cult, and finally delving into the darkest [silly |dungeon beneath |depths under ] the ocean to face the pelagic nightmare they were attempting to suborn to their purposes. "Ah." To protect itself, the lureling drew out the deepest fears and secret weaknesses of you and your companions, turned them against you. While you don't doubt that it did the same to Gweyr, she hasn't said anything about it to you, nor has she shown any blatant signs of breaking down like everyone else did... on the other hand, you don't believe that she's that hard of a woman to be able to no-sell an ancient eldritch being's terrors. One of the final things she told you was that with the driving of Tollus's cult from the rift and the realization that the adventure she'd just had was her last, she felt like her existence didn't have meaning any more. "But that's not true." Exactly. The both of you walk in silence for a minute or two, soaking in the [dayNight |atmosphere of the town square |chill night wind ] and letting the tale you've just told Garret sink in. At length, he raises his gaze and scratches his chin. "I don't remember if I've told you this before, [pc.name], but I'll say it again anyway: every single memory I have of my old woman is hazy save for her face. An old brick. The smell of blood, without any danger in it. Her hands on my head, for some reason. The streets, filled with snow. She said something to me... it was important, I know, but I don't remember the words. Just that they were important, and that's all." Will he come with you? Up to the rift and onto the ice, to convince his mother that even though her long hunt is over, there's still something worth living for in her later years? Asking Garth is a non-starter. Asking Gwyn is a fool's errand, for the daughter will never forgive the mother. But the son... he just might have the ability and the will to pull it off, might be the only man in all of Savarra capable of accomplishing this feat. Another moment's pause from Garret, and at length he reaches into his vest and pulls out a medallion with a thick golden chain. A glint of light catches the insignia upon its face, that of two crossed swords, and at length he sighs and tucks it away once more. "Probably." Probably? "Look, [pc.name]. Would you do me a favor? Head back to my old man's and wait for me there — I shouldn't be longer than an hour or so. After all you've told me, I just need to go and ask old man Sanders some questions." Hey, he's not to do anything rash — strongest man in Savarra or not, Sanders would kick his ass seven ways before the hour's out. "I didn't say I was going to start a ruckus or anything; I just want some answers. Answers that he's been keeping from me for a long time... [pc.name], I don't doubt that he did what he thought was best, and the pained look on his face every time I asked him the same questions growing up is proof enough that he's still hurting over it. But even after listening to what you've had to say, I still want to hear it from his mouth. "So if you don't mind... wait for me at my old man's place. Like I said, this shouldn't take long." Garret's smiling, but the smile is very obviously forced as he claps you on the shoulder and steps around you, making a beeline for the other side of the village square and the chapel of Velun. You watch his departing form for a little while, wondering if you should go after him, and then the moment passes and he's gone... "

rows.original: Moments tick by as you wait at the bar in the Frost Hound, awaiting Garret's return. It feels like forever, yet the hour isn't up yet... and there've been no cries of bloody murder from the other side of the village square, so you can only assume that Garret's kept his word to not be rash. Still, it doesn't stop the mug of rye beer or whatever it is you've ordered from being absolutely flat and tasteless as you keep one eye on the main door, scrutinizing everyone that enters the Hound. And then, good to his word, Garret returns, the doors swinging ominously as his feet land heavily on the straw-covered floorboards. Several of the Hound's patrons look up at him, swallow hard, then find something very interesting indeed in the bottoms of their tankards and mugs. No bruises, no blood, no broken bones. Maybe he really did just have a talk with Sanders. On the other hand, you feel Garret's presence press against you as he stops before the bar, dark and dour; he gives you a nod, then turns to his father. "Old man." Garth doesn't miss a beat. "What's it you want, pup? It's too early for another drink, even if you're paying like anyone else." "Let's take this out back. It's about my mother." Garth starts to speak, clearly having been asked about this many times over the years, but Garret cuts him off. "This time it's different, old man. Sanders told me everything." "Did he, now." "He filled in the blanks [pc.name] here didn't. That's enough, old man — I've got the whole picture now. You lied to me. You lied to me and Gwyn all these years. You told us that Mom was dead in her exile when you've been secretly meeting her outside of town every few months all this time. For years, decades." A tense moment passes as everyone in the tavern's common room holds their breath, and you feel the charged air all but crackle between father and son. Eventually, though, Garth folds his arms, raises his chin, and nods over to the door in the back. "All right, pup. Let's take this back out to the yard. [pc.name], since you were kind enough to tell my son all you knew, why don't you come too?" Oh, you'll do that all right, but not for the reasons he thinks. Garth sets down the mug he's polishing and takes the lead, Garret and you trailing behind until it's just the three of you in the yard. Father and son have another little staring competition, two wolves fighting in silence for dominance, and then at long last, Garth takes charge and speaks. "So, then. Your mother." "Fine. [var0 |Before we begin, though, just so you don't have anything to hold over my head: you know those pups Gwyn's taking care of for [pc.name], old man? They're mine." "I was wondering when you'd own up to that." "I took my blank powder, old man. It was an accident." "Yes, I found a couple of the empty pouches she sells them in. You aren't as good at covering your tracks as you think you are, pup. Age and wisdom beats youth in these matters every time." Garth sighs. "An accident isn't the end of the world, son. You and your sister were accidents as well, but your mother and I rolled with the punches, and here we are today. We lived by the sword in her company, those crossed swords... and would've eventually died by them if the two of you hadn't come along. "Still, we need to talk about this... later. Tossing your get to your sister for her to raise on the quiet isn't going to fool anyone, even if the resemblance wasn't plain for all to see. Nor am I that old that I don't know what's going on under my own roof when you show a particular bunch of pups when bothering with kids has never crossed your mind at all in the past." "Fine, old man, we can deal with that later. Now then, about Mom. |Let's begin. ] Why did you let us think that our mother was dead? Sure, she was exiled as you said... but she was still alive! You've been seeing her outside of town every season or so these past twenty years! Why?" "Because she may as well have been when it came to your upbringing." Garret recoils as if his father had slapped him. "The fuck did you say, old man?" "At first she couldn't come back, for obvious reasons. Then after several years and the families involved in what happened had moved on from Hawkethorne, she wouldn't have come back anyway. I told her that it'd more or less blown over, that the only people left in town who might remember were Sanders, River and the baroness herself, that I'd deal with Sanders if he protested. She flat-out refused, until her job was done and she'd proven that she was right in the end to have killed all those kids." Garret jabs his son with a finger squarely on the ribs. "Kids like what you are now." "So that means lying to us? Making Gwyn hate her mother?" "I didn't set out to poison your mother in Gwyneth's eyes. She... your sister just fell into that by herself." Garth sighs. "What would've been the point? You might've gotten to see her three or four times a year, if you could sneak out of town with me. You wouldn't have learned anything. You wouldn't have an upbringing, not from her at the least. She could've come back, but she didn't want to, not until she'd exhausted herself hunting Tollus. I saw where she was coming from — it was part of why I fell for your mother — but that also meant she wasn't there for either of you. If you want to split hairs about it, your mother was still alive, yes. But what would've changed?" "Maybe we wouldn't have grown up believing our mother was dead, having been sent to walk the ice. And yes, old man, it does matter." "...You're just like your mother." For a split second there, your hackles rise and you instinctively ready yourself to step in between the two should Garret strike his father, but it never comes. "You know what I think, old man? I think you just told a pair of pups a convenient lie, so that we wouldn't keep on asking when we could go and see our mother. So that I wouldn't sneak off to be with her. And once you'd dug that hole deep enough, there wasn't any way to go but to dig even deeper. I can't say I don't understand, or that I wouldn't have been tempted to do the same had I been in your place, old man. It was, of course, very reasonable. But I'm still fucking disgusted that you chose to do it. "And at the end of the day, everyone — old man Sanders, River, and you, old man — everyone still pretended to not know anything when [pc.name] here stepped up to the plate when Tollus came knocking once more. You don't have an excuse for that, not putting [pc.himHer] in danger just because the three of you wanted to bury your shame." "Think what you like, pup. If you heard the story from Sanders, then you know that many such stories don't have good endings. We just try to do the best we can, with the means we have, according to what we believe in." "Then clearly that wasn't enough." Garth rubs the bridge of his muzzle. "Oh, Gweyr, Gweyr, how your son has grown. And [pc.name] — why spill the beans now, of all times?" Because having exhausted herself after hounding him for twenty years, she's lost the will to live. No, that's not right — it would be more correct to say that she feels there's nothing left to live for, given that she's defeated Tollus as thoroughly as she could. Her last adventure, in her own words. Even if one takes the dimmest view of her actions that led to her exile from the Hawkethorne of decades past, you feel that the old wolf has done enough to atone for her actions, if she was even in the wrong to begin with. "...So, you think you have the full picture, then." After hounding Tollus through Harvest Valley and up in the cold north? Yes. Gods know where he's going to show that ugly face and bald head of his again. Gweyr doesn't deserve to just lie down and die peacefully knowing her purpose in life is complete — [pc.isDK |she's been far too useful to you for that |there's so much more to live for ] and so many people need her. Her son, for example. And her daughter, even if Gwyn resents her. And Garth himself. "...You're treading on thin ice here." If he didn't need his wife, would he have bothered sneaking out of town to meet her without fail for the last twenty years? "..." Who was at fault, how the entire ugly mess turned out, that stain in Hawkethorne's past — that's up to them to dig up if they don't want to bury it peacefully. But as far as you're concerned, this is as much as Gweyr deserves after twenty years of walking the ice. If Garth and Sanders can't let it go because there're two kids under his roof here who need their mother, then it sounds like a them problem. Garth scowls and looks fit to launch some kind of angry retort at you, and judging by the way Garret's ears have perked up on his head, he's just itching to come to blows already. It's just then that Gwyn chooses to make a timely entrance, [gwyn.isPregnant |hands on her swollen belly |arms akimbo ] as she gazes despondently between her father and brother. "Dad, Garret, just stop it already. Please. [pc.name], please don't push them any further." It's because nothing was done, that nothing changed over the years up till this point that things have come to a head again once more. You don't doubt that Garth originally intended to tell the two of them what exactly happened to their mother when they were old enough to understand; it's just that he kept on putting it off until tomorrow, and then that tomorrow had another tomorrow, and it just kept on rolling on for twenty years until here you are today having this discussion for the simple reason that it can't be put off any more. Garth looks between his son's scowling expression, his daughter's pleading face, and finally at you. The old wolf is clearly torn — he must've known that this day would eventually come, but not so soon. Then again, "soon" had been waiting for twenty years. "So, what are the two of you going to do, then?" he says quietly at last. You're going to go up to the rift with Garret, because he's the only person in the world who could convince Gweyr that there's still meaning to her life and that people still need her. After that, she's coming home at long last. "And does my daughter want that?" There's a distinctly empty spot where Gwyn was standing a moment ago — she must've slipped back into the nursery when the three of you weren't looking. Garret considers the empty space for a bit, his eyes turning to the nursery entrance, then shrugs. "If I don't bring Mom home, there'll be no chance that they ever manage to fix things between them. If I do bring Mom home, there's at least a small chance that they might at least learn to tolerate each other. Those are chances I'm willing to take, and let's face it: you're at least partly responsible for the way she turned out, old man. "I'm done here."
rows.translation: 在“霜猎犬”酒吧等待加勒特归来的时间里，时间仿佛一分一秒地流逝。感觉就像过了很久很久，但实际上时间还没到……而且村广场的另一边也没有传来任何紧急求救的声音，所以你可以推测加勒特确实遵守了自己的承诺，没有轻举妄动。不过，这丝毫没有改变你手部中的黑麦啤酒——或者说你点的其他饮品——变得索然无味、毫无味道的事实。你始终紧盯着大门，仔细观察每一个走进“霜猎犬”酒吧的人。 果然说到做到，加勒特回来了。当他沉重的足部步落在铺着稻草的地板上时，门扇发出令人不寒而栗的声响。酒馆里的几位常客抬头看了他一眼，硬生生咽了口唾沫，然后又把目光重新投向自己手部中的酒杯，仿佛在酒杯底部发现了什么非常有趣的东西。 没有淤青，没有流血，也没有骨折。也许他真的只是和桑德斯谈了谈而已。但另一方面，当加勒特站在吧台前时，你能感受到他的存在给你带来的压迫感——他面色阴沉，向你点了点头，然后转向他的父亲。 “老头。 加斯没有丝毫迟疑：“你想说什么，小家伙？现在还没到喝酒的时间呢，就算你付的钱和其他人一样多也没用。” “我们出去谈吧。这件事和我母亲有关。”加斯开始说道，显然这些年来这个问题已经被问过很多次了，但加勒特打断了他：“这次不一样，老头。桑德斯把一切都告诉了我。 他真的这么做了吗？” “他把那些空缺的地方都填上了。 [pc.name] 这里并没有。够了，老头——我现在全明白了。你一直在骗我，这些年来你一直在骗我和格温。你告诉我们妈妈在流亡期间已经去世了，而实际上你却每隔几个月就偷偷地去镇外与她见面。这么多年来，你一直在撒谎。 几十年紧张的气氛在酒馆的公共房间里弥漫着，所有人都屏住了呼吸，而你…… 感受到 父子两人之间的气氛紧张得几乎要爆发出来。不过最终，加思双臂交叉抱在胸前，抬起下巴，朝后面的门点了点头。 “好吧，小家伙。我们把这个拿到院子里去吧。 [pc.name]既然你这么好心，把你知道的一切都告诉了我的儿子，那你为什么不也一起来呢？” “哦，你肯定会来的，不过原因肯定不是他想象的那样。”加思放下他正在擦拭的杯子，走在前面，加勒特和你跟在后面，直到只剩下他们三个人在院子里。父子俩又进行了一场无声的对视——就像两只狼在默默争夺主导权。最后，加思终于开口说道： “那么，关于你的母亲…… 好的。 [var0 |不过，在开始之前，我想先说明一点，免得你们以后拿这个来指责我：你们应该知道格温正在照顾那些小狗吧…… [pc.name]老头，那些东西都是我的。” “我早就想知道你什么时候会承认这一点。” “我拿了自己的空白药粉，老头，这只是个意外而已。” “是啊，我确实找到了她用来装那些药粉的几个空袋子。 小家伙，你其实并没有自己想象中那么擅长掩盖自己的痕迹。在这些事情上，年龄和智慧总是比年轻更有力量。”加思叹了口气，“一场意外并不会意味着一切的终结，儿子。你和你的妹妹也是意外诞生的，但你的母亲和我一起度过了那些困难，才有了今天的我们。 在她的公司里，我们每天都生活在刀光剑影之中，那些针锋相对的局面……要是没有你们俩的出现，我们最终肯定会因此丧命。 “不过，我们还是需要以后再谈这件事。把孩子交给你的妹妹，让她在安静的环境中抚养，这个办法根本骗不了任何人，即使他们的相貌并没有那么明显地让人看出差别来。 我也没老到连自己家里发生什么都不明白的地步。当你带着那群小狗出现的时候，我立刻就意识到你们之前根本没考虑过会打扰到孩子们。” “好吧，老头子，这个我们以后再谈吧。 那么，关于妈妈的事。 |让我们开始吧。 ] 你为什么让我们以为我们的母亲已经去世了呢？当然，正如你所说，她被流放了……但她其实还活着！在过去的二十年里，每个季节你都应该都在城外与她见面吧！为什么你要这样对我们隐瞒呢？ 因为在她参与你的成长过程时，她其实根本就不存在。” 加勒特猛地后退了一步，仿佛父亲刚刚打了他一样。“你他妈在说什么，老头？” “起初，由于一些显而易见的原因，她无法回来。 几年过去了，那些与这件事有关的家庭都已经离开了鹰棘镇，她本来也不会再回来的。我告诉她，这件事差不多已经平息了，镇上可能还记得这件事的，只有桑德斯、里弗以及那位女男爵本人。如果桑德斯提出异议，我会处理他的问题。 她坚决拒绝了，直到她完成了自己的工作，也证明了当初杀死那些孩子其实是正确的决定。“加勒特用手部指戳了戳儿子的肋骨，说道：‘现在的孩子们正是喜欢你这样的。 这么说来，就是在对我们撒谎？就是想让格温恨她的母亲？” “我本来并没有打算在格温妮丝的眼中让你们的母亲变得可恶。她……你的妹妹，完全是自己陷入了这种境地。”加思叹了口气，“这样做到底有什么意义呢？ 如果你能和我一起偷偷离开这座城市，你或许每年能有三四次机会见到她。但你根本什么也学不到，至少无法从她那里得到任何成长或教育。她本可以回来，但她并不想这么做，直到她把追逐托卢斯的事情彻底做完为止。 我理解她的立场——这也是我当初喜欢你母亲的原因之一——但这也意味着她其实并没有真正为你们中的任何一个人着想。如果你非得追究细节的话，确实，在你母亲在世的时候，情况还是有些不同的。但那又有什么改变呢？" 也许如果我们没有被送到冰原上行走，就不会一直以为我们的母亲已经去世了。没错，老人家，确实是这样。 做 这很重要。” “……你和你妈妈一模一样。” 有那么一瞬间，你的怒火瞬间被点燃，你本能地准备在加勒特攻击他父亲的时候介入其中，但那一刻终究没有到来。 你知道我怎么想的吗，老头？我觉得你只是编了个方便的谎言，好让我们不再追问什么时候能去看我们的妈妈，这样我就不会偷偷溜去陪她了。而一旦你把那个坑挖得足够深，就只能继续往更深处挖了。 我不能说我不理解，也不能说如果我处在你的位置，就不会有同样的冲动，老兄。当然，那确实是一件很…… 合理的但我还是他妈的觉得你选择这么做实在令人作呕。 “归根结底，所有人——老桑德斯、里弗，还有你，老兄——在事情发生之后，仍然装作什么都不知情的样子。 [pc.name] 当托卢斯再次找上门来时，正是你站了出来承担了责任。对于这种事，你没有任何借口，根本没有理由逃避。 [pc.himHer] 仅仅因为你们三个想要掩盖自己的羞耻，就陷入了危险之中。” “你想怎么想都行，孩子。如果你是从桑德斯那里听到这个故事的，那么你就应该知道，很多这样的故事都没有好的结局。我们只是尽自己所能，利用我们手部头现有的资源，按照我们自己的信念去行事而已。” “那么显然，这样的努力还不够。” 加思揉了揉自己的鼻子。“哦，格韦尔，格韦尔，你的儿子已经长大了啊…… [pc.name] 为什么偏偏现在才把秘密说出来呢？” 因为经过二十年的不懈追讨，她已经筋疲力尽，失去了继续活下去的勇气。不，这么说并不准确——更确切地说，是因为她已经彻底击败了托卢斯，因此觉得再也没有理由活下去了。 用她自己的话来说，这就是她最后一次冒险。即便人们以最苛刻的眼光来看待她那些导致她数十年前被逐出鹰棘镇的行为，也会觉得这只老狼已经为自己的过错付出了足够的代价——前提是，她当初真的有错的话。 ……所以，你认为自己已经掌握了全部真相，是吗？” 在追着托卢斯穿过收获谷，一路来到寒冷的北方之后？是的。天知道他还会在哪里再次露出他那丑陋的面孔和光秃秃的脑袋。 格温尔根本不应该就这样安详地死去，因为她的人生目标还未实现啊…… [pc.isDK |她对你来说实在太有用了，不可能做出那种事。 |生活中还有许多值得珍惜的东西等待我们去体验。 ] 有那么多人需要她。比如她的儿子，还有她的女儿，即使格温对她心怀怨恨；当然，加思自己也同样需要她。 “……你现在可是踩在薄冰上啊。” 如果他不需要自己的妻子，那么在过去的二十年里，他还会费心偷偷地离开城镇去见她吗？ ……” 究竟是谁的过错，这场闹剧是如何发生的，鹰棘镇过去的那些丑事——如果他们不想让这些事情被永远埋葬，那就由他们自己去调查清楚。但对你来说，经过二十年在冰原上艰难生存，格韦尔所遭受的一切，已经是他应得的报应了。 如果加斯和桑德斯因为这里还有两个需要母亲的孩子而无法释怀，那么这似乎就是他们自己的问题了。 加斯皱着眉头，看起来随时都会对你发怒反击；而从他耳朵竖起来的样子来看，他简直迫不及待想要动手部了。 就在这时，格温选择适时登场了。 [gwyn.isPregnant |用手抚摸着自己隆起的腹部 |双臂叉腰 ] 当她沮丧地望着自己的父亲和哥哥时， “爸爸，加勒特，请你们别这样了。真的。 [pc.name]请不要再把事情推得更远了。” 正是因为多年来什么都没有采取行动，什么都没有改变，所以事情才再次陷入了僵局。你不会怀疑加思原本是打算在他们足够懂事的时候，告诉他们母亲到底发生了什么；只是他一直把这件事推迟到明天，而明天又变成了后天，就这样拖了二十年，直到今天，这场讨论终于不得不进行了，因为再也无法拖延下去了。 加思看着儿子愤怒的表情，女儿恳求的眼神，最后将目光转向了你。这位老狼显然陷入了矛盾之中——他肯定早就知道这一天终会到来，但没想到会来得这么快。不过，说起来，“很快”这个概念对他来说，其实已经意味着等待了二十年。 那么，你们两个接下来打算做什么呢？”他终于轻声问道。 你们要和加勒特一起前往那个裂隙，因为他是这个世界上唯一能够让格薇尔相信她的生命仍然有意义、人们仍然需要她的人。之后，她终于可以回家了。 那么，我的女儿真的想要那个吗？” 刚才格温还站在那里的地方现在空空如也——肯定是在你们三个人没注意的时候悄悄回到了婴儿房里。加勒特盯着那个空荡荡的位置看了一会儿，目光随后转向婴儿房的入口，最后耸了耸肩。 如果我不把妈妈带回家，他们就永远没有机会修复彼此之间的关系。但如果我带妈妈回家，至少还有一线希望，让他们学会互相容忍。这些风险我是愿意去承担的。而且说实话，老兄，她现在的样子，你至少也负有一部分责任。 我在这里的任务已经完成了。
rows.raw: " Moments tick by as you wait at the bar in the Frost Hound, awaiting Garret's return. It feels like forever, yet the hour isn't up yet... and there've been no cries of bloody murder from the other side of the village square, so you can only assume that Garret's kept his word to not be rash. Still, it doesn't stop the mug of rye beer or whatever it is you've ordered from being absolutely flat and tasteless as you keep one eye on the main door, scrutinizing everyone that enters the Hound. And then, good to his word, Garret returns, the doors swinging ominously as his feet land heavily on the straw-covered floorboards. Several of the Hound's patrons look up at him, swallow hard, then find something very interesting indeed in the bottoms of their tankards and mugs. No bruises, no blood, no broken bones. Maybe he really did just have a talk with Sanders. On the other hand, you feel Garret's presence press against you as he stops before the bar, dark and dour; he gives you a nod, then turns to his father. "Old man." Garth doesn't miss a beat. "What's it you want, pup? It's too early for another drink, even if you're paying like anyone else." "Let's take this out back. It's about my mother." Garth starts to speak, clearly having been asked about this many times over the years, but Garret cuts him off. "This time it's different, old man. Sanders told me everything." "Did he, now." "He filled in the blanks [pc.name] here didn't. That's enough, old man — I've got the whole picture now. You lied to me. You lied to me and Gwyn all these years. You told us that Mom was dead in her exile when you've been secretly meeting her outside of town every few months all this time. For years, decades." A tense moment passes as everyone in the tavern's common room holds their breath, and you feel the charged air all but crackle between father and son. Eventually, though, Garth folds his arms, raises his chin, and nods over to the door in the back. "All right, pup. Let's take this back out to the yard. [pc.name], since you were kind enough to tell my son all you knew, why don't you come too?" Oh, you'll do that all right, but not for the reasons he thinks. Garth sets down the mug he's polishing and takes the lead, Garret and you trailing behind until it's just the three of you in the yard. Father and son have another little staring competition, two wolves fighting in silence for dominance, and then at long last, Garth takes charge and speaks. "So, then. Your mother." "Fine. [var0 |Before we begin, though, just so you don't have anything to hold over my head: you know those pups Gwyn's taking care of for [pc.name], old man? They're mine." "I was wondering when you'd own up to that." "I took my blank powder, old man. It was an accident." "Yes, I found a couple of the empty pouches she sells them in. You aren't as good at covering your tracks as you think you are, pup. Age and wisdom beats youth in these matters every time." Garth sighs. "An accident isn't the end of the world, son. You and your sister were accidents as well, but your mother and I rolled with the punches, and here we are today. We lived by the sword in her company, those crossed swords... and would've eventually died by them if the two of you hadn't come along. "Still, we need to talk about this... later. Tossing your get to your sister for her to raise on the quiet isn't going to fool anyone, even if the resemblance wasn't plain for all to see. Nor am I that old that I don't know what's going on under my own roof when you show a particular bunch of pups when bothering with kids has never crossed your mind at all in the past." "Fine, old man, we can deal with that later. Now then, about Mom. |Let's begin. ] Why did you let us think that our mother was dead? Sure, she was exiled as you said... but she was still alive! You've been seeing her outside of town every season or so these past twenty years! Why?" "Because she may as well have been when it came to your upbringing." Garret recoils as if his father had slapped him. "The fuck did you say, old man?" "At first she couldn't come back, for obvious reasons. Then after several years and the families involved in what happened had moved on from Hawkethorne, she wouldn't have come back anyway. I told her that it'd more or less blown over, that the only people left in town who might remember were Sanders, River and the baroness herself, that I'd deal with Sanders if he protested. She flat-out refused, until her job was done and she'd proven that she was right in the end to have killed all those kids." Garret jabs his son with a finger squarely on the ribs. "Kids like what you are now." "So that means lying to us? Making Gwyn hate her mother?" "I didn't set out to poison your mother in Gwyneth's eyes. She... your sister just fell into that by herself." Garth sighs. "What would've been the point? You might've gotten to see her three or four times a year, if you could sneak out of town with me. You wouldn't have learned anything. You wouldn't have an upbringing, not from her at the least. She could've come back, but she didn't want to, not until she'd exhausted herself hunting Tollus. I saw where she was coming from — it was part of why I fell for your mother — but that also meant she wasn't there for either of you. If you want to split hairs about it, your mother was still alive, yes. But what would've changed?" "Maybe we wouldn't have grown up believing our mother was dead, having been sent to walk the ice. And yes, old man, it does matter." "...You're just like your mother." For a split second there, your hackles rise and you instinctively ready yourself to step in between the two should Garret strike his father, but it never comes. "You know what I think, old man? I think you just told a pair of pups a convenient lie, so that we wouldn't keep on asking when we could go and see our mother. So that I wouldn't sneak off to be with her. And once you'd dug that hole deep enough, there wasn't any way to go but to dig even deeper. I can't say I don't understand, or that I wouldn't have been tempted to do the same had I been in your place, old man. It was, of course, very reasonable. But I'm still fucking disgusted that you chose to do it. "And at the end of the day, everyone — old man Sanders, River, and you, old man — everyone still pretended to not know anything when [pc.name] here stepped up to the plate when Tollus came knocking once more. You don't have an excuse for that, not putting [pc.himHer] in danger just because the three of you wanted to bury your shame." "Think what you like, pup. If you heard the story from Sanders, then you know that many such stories don't have good endings. We just try to do the best we can, with the means we have, according to what we believe in." "Then clearly that wasn't enough." Garth rubs the bridge of his muzzle. "Oh, Gweyr, Gweyr, how your son has grown. And [pc.name] — why spill the beans now, of all times?" Because having exhausted herself after hounding him for twenty years, she's lost the will to live. No, that's not right — it would be more correct to say that she feels there's nothing left to live for, given that she's defeated Tollus as thoroughly as she could. Her last adventure, in her own words. Even if one takes the dimmest view of her actions that led to her exile from the Hawkethorne of decades past, you feel that the old wolf has done enough to atone for her actions, if she was even in the wrong to begin with. "...So, you think you have the full picture, then." After hounding Tollus through Harvest Valley and up in the cold north? Yes. Gods know where he's going to show that ugly face and bald head of his again. Gweyr doesn't deserve to just lie down and die peacefully knowing her purpose in life is complete — [pc.isDK |she's been far too useful to you for that |there's so much more to live for ] and so many people need her. Her son, for example. And her daughter, even if Gwyn resents her. And Garth himself. "...You're treading on thin ice here." If he didn't need his wife, would he have bothered sneaking out of town to meet her without fail for the last twenty years? "..." Who was at fault, how the entire ugly mess turned out, that stain in Hawkethorne's past — that's up to them to dig up if they don't want to bury it peacefully. But as far as you're concerned, this is as much as Gweyr deserves after twenty years of walking the ice. If Garth and Sanders can't let it go because there're two kids under his roof here who need their mother, then it sounds like a them problem. Garth scowls and looks fit to launch some kind of angry retort at you, and judging by the way Garret's ears have perked up on his head, he's just itching to come to blows already. It's just then that Gwyn chooses to make a timely entrance, [gwyn.isPregnant |hands on her swollen belly |arms akimbo ] as she gazes despondently between her father and brother. "Dad, Garret, just stop it already. Please. [pc.name], please don't push them any further." It's because nothing was done, that nothing changed over the years up till this point that things have come to a head again once more. You don't doubt that Garth originally intended to tell the two of them what exactly happened to their mother when they were old enough to understand; it's just that he kept on putting it off until tomorrow, and then that tomorrow had another tomorrow, and it just kept on rolling on for twenty years until here you are today having this discussion for the simple reason that it can't be put off any more. Garth looks between his son's scowling expression, his daughter's pleading face, and finally at you. The old wolf is clearly torn — he must've known that this day would eventually come, but not so soon. Then again, "soon" had been waiting for twenty years. "So, what are the two of you going to do, then?" he says quietly at last. You're going to go up to the rift with Garret, because he's the only person in the world who could convince Gweyr that there's still meaning to her life and that people still need her. After that, she's coming home at long last. "And does my daughter want that?" There's a distinctly empty spot where Gwyn was standing a moment ago — she must've slipped back into the nursery when the three of you weren't looking. Garret considers the empty space for a bit, his eyes turning to the nursery entrance, then shrugs. "If I don't bring Mom home, there'll be no chance that they ever manage to fix things between them. If I do bring Mom home, there's at least a small chance that they might at least learn to tolerate each other. Those are chances I'm willing to take, and let's face it: you're at least partly responsible for the way she turned out, old man. "I'm done here." "

rows.original: And so it happens that the both of you return to the Hound's interior, Garret making a beeline for what's left of his drink and downing it in one massive gulp. He makes a show of smacking his lips, then exhales deeply and rubs his temples. "Well, fuck." Is Garth going to be all right? "I think I went a little hard on the old man, but he kind of deserved it. I can see why he kept the whole of the truth from us all these years, but that doesn't mean I have to like it in the least. I saw him slip into the nursery — he's probably gone off to see to that silly puppy I have for a sister." So, what's he going to do now? Garret scratches the back of his head. "What you asked me to do. Go and get my mom back, of course. You needed me, right?" That's true, you did say as much. You wouldn't be able to convince Gweyr with your words, but her own son, with a temperament as legendary as hers... "Hm." Garret fingers his chin and tries to look at himself in the reflection of his tankard. "You think she'll recognize me?" rows.translation: 结果，你们俩又回到了猎犬的内部。加勒特径直走向自己剩下的那杯酒，一饮而尽。他故作夸张地咂了咂嘴，然后深深地呼了口气，揉了揉太阳穴。 “唉，真见鬼。 加思会没事吧？ “我想我对那个老人有点太严厉了，但他确实活该。我能够理解他为什么这些年来一直对我们隐瞒真相，但这并不意味着我就得接受这一点。我看到他溜进了育儿室——他大概去照顾我妹妹养的那只傻小狗了吧。 那么，他现在打算做什么呢？ 加勒特挠了挠后脑勺：“你让我做的事情啊，当然是去把我的妈妈救回来。你确实是需要我的帮助，对吧？” 确实如此，你也是这么说的。你用言语是无法说服格薇尔的，但她的亲生儿子，拥有和她一样传奇的性格…… 嗯。”加勒特用手托着下巴，试图通过酒杯的反射来观察自己的模样。“你觉得她会认出我来吗？” “也许从外表上看不出来，但就像你刚才说的，他们两人之间确实存在着某种特殊的联系。她肯定能知道他是谁的，你放心吧。 要是我也有你这样的信心该多好。那好吧，我想我该开始收拾行李了。在城里还有几件事需要处理，比如和桑德斯老头的一些未了事宜，不过应该很快就能出发了。像我这样的人，行李本来就不多。我们就在冬城的大厅电梯那里见面吧？ 他知道这件事？ “哦，当然知道了。就是你带回来的那个苍白精灵，那个偶尔会出现的家伙——她在我喝着我老头酿的加了香料的酒时，把这一切都告诉了我。听起来挺有意思的，我也很想亲眼看看。 [party.has etheryn |是我做的！”莱恩在你旁边兴奋地说道，“那部通往裂隙的电梯，就是我祖母委托我制作的。我父亲为此感到非常自豪！ ] 他一个人能安全到达那里吗？ 加勒特虚弱地笑了笑，活动了一下手臂。“对萨瓦拉最强壮的人来说，森林根本不是问题；只要我能进入城市，那么进入城内也应该不会有什么困难。 [party.has etheryn |让你身边那个漂亮的精灵女孩给我写张便条什么的，应该不是什么问题吧？既然这是为了你的工作，应该不会有什么麻烦吧？” “只要你不在我所在的城市里惹出什么麻烦，你随时都可以来试试我的法术。” 加勒特听到瑞恩的话，干笑了一声：“嘿，我可能有点傻，但至少我不是个惹麻烦的人。 愚蠢的好的，我会在你离开之前过去一趟。 [pc.name] 然后获得一份……我父亲以前总是用哪个词来形容的来着？“令状”吧？就是一份允许进入你住所的令状。 |那个苍白的精灵女孩，应该会给我写张便条之类的吧……我刚才肯定在酒吧里看到她了。我敢肯定，如果我告诉她我是为你办事的，她肯定会主动联系我的。 这也太明显了吧？ “所有常客都知道你救了她的王国之类的，所以她确实欠你一个人情。这种推论其实并不难得出吧。 ] 他似乎对能够再次见到自己的母亲这件事感到非常兴奋…… “处理这件事的最佳方式就是直接行动。我知道无论如何我都会去做，所以担心或害怕又有什么意义呢？”他隔着桌子伸过手，拍了拍你的肩膀，说道：“听着…… [pc.name]这次真是多亏了你。 [var0 |其实有两个原因：你愿意接受我的小狗，而且当我告诉你那些事情确实发生过时，你也没有怀疑我——尽管我当时服用了伊弗里斯夫人的那种迷药。我认识的其他人，在那种情况下，几乎都会当面指责我是骗子，但你却相信了我的话。不过，这确实是事实。你不得不承认，当初你确实有过怀疑，因为这个方法对大多数其他人来说都效果显著，但自从加斯说了那些话之后……还有他和他父亲的那次谈话，这些因素都让人无法不产生疑虑。 如果我们要把我的妈妈接回家的话，我觉得他会把这件事推迟到那时候再做。只是我的一种直觉而已，这样她就可以来管管我或者什么的…… |你本可以像我父亲和桑德斯那样对此保持沉默，什么都不说，那样我也不会多想什么。” “嗯，如果他想要低调处理这件事的话，那就是你之前说的那番话了。 确实，这件事主要涉及到格温和他，但归根结底，它还是关于格韦尔的。就像你之前说的，无论她过去做过什么，无论责任应该如何划分，她在过去的二十年里一直在努力弥补那些过错。 她还有很多事情要做，因此并没有去追捕托卢斯和他的那些手下，而他需要让她明白这一点。如果加勒特非得担心些什么的话，他应该考虑一下当你们两人到达那里时，该对格韦尔说些什么。 加勒特用手揉了揉太阳穴。“嗯……我本身就不太擅长用语言表达。但那通常是针对普通人的情况。如果我真的像我爸爸说的那样，和妈妈很像；或者像里弗和桑德斯说的那样，那么应该就不会有问题了吧。 ] 不管怎样，事情就是这么定了。我会去看看我的老头子和格温，然后开始收拾行李，去见桑德斯，之后再出发。你们不用为我担心等我了——如果老天保佑的话，我会比你们先到！

rows.original:
You're just about to speak, but catch yourself in the act and consider Garret. Sure, he might be the only chance you may have at turning around Gweyr's outlook on the rest of her life, but that's just the problem: you're only going to get one shot at this. And looking at him now... well, he might be up to the task, and he might not.
    
    There's more to this story that needs to be told, and as he is right now you're not sure Garret's in a state fit to be presented to his mom for the purpose you have in mind. Maybe you should uncover more of the history pertaining to Garth's family and let Garret know; while you can't make a horse drink, you can certainly lead it to the water. Ultimately, it's up to the dog to have the epiphany he needs to come into himself, but you can certainly create the circumstances to help him along.
rows.translation:
你正要开口说话，但请先停下来想一想加勒特。没错，他可能是你改变格薇尔对未来生活的看法的唯一机会，但问题就在于：你只有一次这样的机会。 现在看着他……嗯，他或许能够胜任这项任务，也或许不能。

这个故事还有更多内容需要被讲述，而就他目前的状况来看，你并不确定加勒特是否处于一个适合被介绍给他的母亲的状态，以满足你心中的那个目的。 也许你应该进一步探究与加思家族相关的历史，并将这些信息告诉加勒特；虽然你无法强迫一匹马喝水，但至少可以把它带到水边。最终，是否能让这只狗领悟到所需的道理，取决于它自己，不过你完全可以创造一些条件来帮助它。
