rows.original:
Pausing to take a breather, you look around the elevator landing, trying to see if Garret's around. In his typical fashion, while he told you that he'd meet up with you here after dealing with whatever business he had with Sanders, he didn't tell you when... 
    
    You're just about to curse him for his rashness and yourself for not asking when you spot him: Garret's donned a thick fur coat and has got a simple pack slung about a shoulder, but that posture, that cocksure attitude is unmistakable at this distance. He's chatting up one of the elevator operators, telling her what by all appearances are a bunch of jokes amidst the constant clacking of pulleys and bleating of shaggy goats as they turn winches and unload carts of ore.
    
    [party.has etheryn
        |"Looks like he's having fun," Ryn says a little wistfully. "Must be nice to be as carefree as he is; would I be able to talk to my own people like that."
        
        Well, Garret's lack of worries stems in part from his lack of responsibility for very much in the world, and you don't think that's necessarily a very good thing. Ryn, on the other hand, has all kinds of expectations of her from everyone.
        
        "..."
    ]
    
    Hey, if he's done being friendly with the locals, how about getting a move on, eh?
    
    Garret doesn't immediately show any sign of having heard you, but quickly makes his excuses to the elf and starts heading in your direction, that same easygoing grin on his face as he gives you a nod. "Sorry about that, hope I didn't keep you waiting too long. I arrived a bit ago and didn't see you around, so I thought I'd get to know the locals. Haven't had that many chances to talk with their kind save for Ryn and that druidess, and the latter wasn't much of a conversationalist."
    
    [party.has etheryn
        |"No one's given you any trouble so far, have they?" Ryn asks.
        
        "Well, there was a bit of trouble at the gate, but I showed them the writ that you had your seneschal write up and it was all good."
        
        Ryn frowns. "I don't have a seneschal. Was it signed as such?"
        
        "Well, not as much, whoever Elthara is — that's the name on the writ the messenger handed to me."
        
        That gets a nervous and relieved laugh out of your elven companion. "Oh. Elthara's not my seneschal or anything, Garret. She's just the high priestess and my sometimes advisor, that's all."
        
        A shrug. "Don't know or care what her title is. Looks like a duck, smells like a duck, walks like a duck, is a duck. People here are pretty friendly and they take hawks here, but then again there's only one of me. You know the saying — one stranger's a novelty, a dozen's a worry."
        |Looks like he got into the city no trouble.
        
        "There was a bit of concern at the gates, and I don't blame them; folk wouldn't be doing their job otherwise. Not that it was a problem — the writ Ryn's seneschal sent got me through no problems."
        
        Ryn doesn't have a seneschal. Was it signed as such?
        
        Garret shrugs. "Whoever this Elthara woman is, then; that's the name on the writ."
        
        Oh, she's just Ryn's high priestess and sometimes advisor. And well... coming to think of the position Elthara's slid into following Alissa's deposal... yeah, saying that she's Ryn's de facto seneschal isn't too far off the mark.
        
        A shrug. "Don't know or care what her title is. Looks like a duck, smells like a duck, walks like a duck, is a duck."
    ]
    
    Either way, is he ready to head up into the rift?
    
    "Yeah."
    
    Has he thought of what he's going to say to his mother when he finally meets her?
    
    "No."
    
    That's a bit surprising.
    
    "Is it really? [pc.name], when we bring my mom back home, she'll have to live with me for the rest of her life. If I try and fake the kind of person I am and she takes that as my first impression, then she'll be mighty disappointed when we get back and she realizes that I wasn't the son she thought I was. Here and now, with something and someone so important, I think I'm just going to be honest, both with my mom and myself. That's the best way to go about it, and once I realized that I stopped worrying about this whole trip and just let it happen."
    
    That's a bit of a roundabout way of thinking about it, but it makes sense in a very Garret sort of way. All right, then — time to take him to Gweyr. You step onto the elevator, the ropes creak, and then you're hurtling upwards to the top of the glacier; the air is already chilly, but gains a distinct nip the higher you go. Garret is quiet all the way as [party.yall] lead him onward through the rift valley, his feet crunching in the snow as you make your way across the permafrost. He's a little underdressed for the occasion, but doesn't seem to be bothered by the cold any; even if he were, the strongest man in Savarra wouldn't be inclined to complain, would he?
rows.translation:
你停下来喘口气，环顾电梯厅，试图看看加勒特是否在附近。以他的一贯作风，虽然他说会在处理完与桑德斯的事情后在这里与你会面，但他并没有具体说明会是什么时候。你简直要骂他太鲁莽，也要骂自己当初见到他时没有多问几句：加勒特穿着一件厚厚的毛皮外套，肩上还挎着一个简单的背包，但从这个距离来看，他的姿势以及那副自信满满的神情，是再明显不过了。 他正在和其中一位电梯操作员聊天，一边讲述着一些笑话。在电梯绳索不断咔嗒作响、那些毛茸茸的山羊也在不停地咩咩叫着的同时，他们还在转动绞车、卸下装满矿石的货车。
    
    [party.has etheryn
        |看起来他玩得很开心呢，”瑞恩带着一丝淡淡的羡慕说道，“能够如此无忧无虑，一定很幸福吧……我也能像他那样和自己的族人坦诚地交谈吗？”

不过，加勒特之所以没有烦恼，部分原因在于他对世界上大多数事情都并不负有责任；而你并不认为这一定是件好事。相比之下，瑞恩却对所有人都抱有各种各样的期望。

“……
    ]
    
    嘿，如果他已经和当地人相处得挺友好了，那是不是该继续前进了呢？

加勒特并没有立刻表现出听到了你的话，但他很快就找了个借口，向那位精灵道别，然后开始朝你的方向走去。他脸上依然挂着那副随和的笑容，还向你点了点头。 实在抱歉，希望我没有让您等待太久。我刚才到这儿，没看到您在附近，所以就想着先去了解一下当地人的情况。除了瑞恩和那位德鲁伊女祭司之外，我其实并没有太多机会和他们交谈，而那位女祭司也不是个很爱聊天的人。"
    
    [party.has etheryn
        |到目前为止，还没有人给你带来任何麻烦，对吧？”莱恩问道。

“嗯，在入口处确实发生了一些小麻烦，但我向他们出示了你让管家起草的那份文件，之后一切就都解决了。
        
        瑞恩皱起了眉头：“我没有首席管家。这份文件上确实是这么写的吗？”

“嗯，不完全是。那个叫埃尔萨拉的人——信使交给我的文件上就是写着这个名字。”

听到这里，你的精灵同伴既紧张又松了一口气，笑了起来。 哦，加勒特，埃尔萨拉并不是我的幕僚长之类的职位，她只是大祭司，偶尔也会给我提供建议而已。”

他耸了耸肩：“我不知道，也不在乎她有什么头衔。她看起来像鸭子，闻起来像鸭子，走路也像鸭子，其实就是鸭子嘛。 这里的人们都非常友善，他们也会养鹰。不过，毕竟只有我一个人在这里。你知道那句话吧——一个陌生人只会让人觉得新奇，而如果有十几个陌生人，那就麻烦了。
        |看起来他进城时没有遇到任何麻烦。

“在城门口确实有些耽搁，但我也能理解他们的做法；如果他们不认真履行职责，那谁来保障秩序呢？不过其实并没有什么问题——莱恩的管家发出的授权令让我顺利通过了检查。Ryn并没有设立任何高级官员来管理事务。这份文件上是不是就这样写的呢？

        Garret耸了耸肩：“不管这个名叫埃尔萨拉的女人是谁，文件上写的就是她的名字。”

        哦，她只不过是Ryn的大祭司，偶尔也会担任顾问而已。 嗯……仔细想想，在艾莉莎被废黜之后，埃尔萨拉所处的位置……没错，说她是瑞恩实际上的管家也并不为过。

“不知道，也不在乎她有什么头衔。”她耸了耸肩。 看起来像鸭子，闻起来像鸭子，走起来也像鸭子，其实就是鸭子。
    ]
    
    无论如何，他准备好进入那个裂隙了吗？

“是的。”

他有没有想过当终于见到自己的母亲时，该对她说些什么？

“没有。”

这有点令人惊讶。

“真的吗？ [pc.name]当我们把妈妈带回家时，她将不得不和我一起生活余生。如果我试图伪装成另一个样子，而她把那当作我对她的第一印象，那么当我们回到家后，当她发现我并不是她想象中的那个儿子时，她一定会非常失望的。 就在此刻，面对如此重要的人和事，我觉得我应该对自己和妈妈都坦诚相待。这才是最好的处理方式。一旦我明白了这一点，我就不再为这次旅行而烦恼，而是让它顺其自然地发生吧。这种思考方式确实有点绕弯，但用加勒特的方式来理解的话，倒也挺有道理的。好吧，那么——是时候带他去格韦尔了。你走进电梯，绳索发出吱嘎声，然后你就开始急速向上冲向冰川的顶部；空气本来就已经很寒冷了，但随着你爬得越高，寒意就会变得愈发刺骨。 加勒特一路上都保持着沉默。 [party.yall] 你引领他穿过裂谷，他的足部步在积雪中发出咔嚓声，而你们正在永久冻土上前行。他的穿着对于这样的环境来说有点单薄，但似乎并不觉得寒冷；即便感到寒冷，萨瓦拉最强壮的男人也应该不会抱怨吧？
rows.raw:
"
    Pausing to take a breather, you look around the elevator landing, trying to see if Garret's around. In his typical fashion, while he told you that he'd meet up with you here after dealing with whatever business he had with Sanders, he didn't tell you when... 
    
    You're just about to curse him for his rashness and yourself for not asking when you spot him: Garret's donned a thick fur coat and has got a simple pack slung about a shoulder, but that posture, that cocksure attitude is unmistakable at this distance. He's chatting up one of the elevator operators, telling her what by all appearances are a bunch of jokes amidst the constant clacking of pulleys and bleating of shaggy goats as they turn winches and unload carts of ore.
    
    [party.has etheryn
        |"Looks like he's having fun," Ryn says a little wistfully. "Must be nice to be as carefree as he is; would I be able to talk to my own people like that."
        
        Well, Garret's lack of worries stems in part from his lack of responsibility for very much in the world, and you don't think that's necessarily a very good thing. Ryn, on the other hand, has all kinds of expectations of her from everyone.
        
        "..."
    ]
    
    Hey, if he's done being friendly with the locals, how about getting a move on, eh?
    
    Garret doesn't immediately show any sign of having heard you, but quickly makes his excuses to the elf and starts heading in your direction, that same easygoing grin on his face as he gives you a nod. "Sorry about that, hope I didn't keep you waiting too long. I arrived a bit ago and didn't see you around, so I thought I'd get to know the locals. Haven't had that many chances to talk with their kind save for Ryn and that druidess, and the latter wasn't much of a conversationalist."
    
    [party.has etheryn
        |"No one's given you any trouble so far, have they?" Ryn asks.
        
        "Well, there was a bit of trouble at the gate, but I showed them the writ that you had your seneschal write up and it was all good."
        
        Ryn frowns. "I don't have a seneschal. Was it signed as such?"
        
        "Well, not as much, whoever Elthara is — that's the name on the writ the messenger handed to me."
        
        That gets a nervous and relieved laugh out of your elven companion. "Oh. Elthara's not my seneschal or anything, Garret. She's just the high priestess and my sometimes advisor, that's all."
        
        A shrug. "Don't know or care what her title is. Looks like a duck, smells like a duck, walks like a duck, is a duck. People here are pretty friendly and they take hawks here, but then again there's only one of me. You know the saying — one stranger's a novelty, a dozen's a worry."
        |Looks like he got into the city no trouble.
        
        "There was a bit of concern at the gates, and I don't blame them; folk wouldn't be doing their job otherwise. Not that it was a problem — the writ Ryn's seneschal sent got me through no problems."
        
        Ryn doesn't have a seneschal. Was it signed as such?
        
        Garret shrugs. "Whoever this Elthara woman is, then; that's the name on the writ."
        
        Oh, she's just Ryn's high priestess and sometimes advisor. And well... coming to think of the position Elthara's slid into following Alissa's deposal... yeah, saying that she's Ryn's de facto seneschal isn't too far off the mark.
        
        A shrug. "Don't know or care what her title is. Looks like a duck, smells like a duck, walks like a duck, is a duck."
    ]
    
    Either way, is he ready to head up into the rift?
    
    "Yeah."
    
    Has he thought of what he's going to say to his mother when he finally meets her?
    
    "No."
    
    That's a bit surprising.
    
    "Is it really? [pc.name], when we bring my mom back home, she'll have to live with me for the rest of her life. If I try and fake the kind of person I am and she takes that as my first impression, then she'll be mighty disappointed when we get back and she realizes that I wasn't the son she thought I was. Here and now, with something and someone so important, I think I'm just going to be honest, both with my mom and myself. That's the best way to go about it, and once I realized that I stopped worrying about this whole trip and just let it happen."
    
    That's a bit of a roundabout way of thinking about it, but it makes sense in a very Garret sort of way. All right, then — time to take him to Gweyr. You step onto the elevator, the ropes creak, and then you're hurtling upwards to the top of the glacier; the air is already chilly, but gains a distinct nip the higher you go. Garret is quiet all the way as [party.yall] lead him onward through the rift valley, his feet crunching in the snow as you make your way across the permafrost. He's a little underdressed for the occasion, but doesn't seem to be bothered by the cold any; even if he were, the strongest man in Savarra wouldn't be inclined to complain, would he?
    "

rows.original: At length, though, the both of you reach the comforting little cave that's Gweyr's home; you can only hope that you're not too late. That worry is eased when you see the flicker of fire on the rough-hewn wall, and the scent of sizzling fat rises out into the freezing air. Huh, she hasn't bothered to keep the cold out that well... Her eyes fixed on the cooking cut of seal on the spit, Gweyr raises her nose and sniffs the air morosely. "Come in, [pc.name]. Nice of you to head on out all the way just to visit an old woman... and who's this you've brought with you? Doesn't smell like one of your usual companions." "Well, ma'am, you're in luck! Today, the strongest man in all of Savarra graces your fine home! A very fine home it is indeed. Great personal touch, everything handcrafted." Still bundled up in his warm cloak and furred boots, Garret swaggers past you and right into the firelight. "I've heard a great deal about you from [pc.name], Mo — I mean, ma'am, mostly that you're tough as nails. Didn't expect you to have aged so well, either!" Gweyr blinks her ears perking up before looking suspiciously at Garret then at you, as if to say, what were you thinking, bringing this idiot into my home? "A sweet talker, aren't you, kid?" "Well, I'd like to think I'm not too bad at wrestling," Garret replies with that same easygoing swagger and grin, sitting down across the fire from his mother and stretching out. "That, and pretty decent at soothing words for pretty ears." [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona atugia azyrran quintillus kiyoko etheryn |"W-what is he doing?" Cait whispers, leaning in and trying not to draw too much notice from mother and son. "Is he actually trying to chat up his mother?" |Brint scrunches up his face and looks distinctly awkward at the conversation that's going on by the fire. "Is it just me, or... or is he actually trying to flirt with his mother?" This isn't something he thought would happen, is it? "I mean, I've known him for a while now, and... this isn't what I expected, [pc.name]. Someone else, maybe, but his mother of all people?" |Brienne scrunches up her face and looks distinctly awkward at the conversation that's going on by the fire. "Is it just me, or... or is he actually trying to flirt with his mother?" This isn't something she thought would happen, is it? "I mean, I've known him for a while now, and... this isn't what I expected, [pc.name]. Can't say I'm mightily impressed, but it might've worked on me if I'd had a half-dozen beers beforehand. I'll give him a seven out of ten just for being daring enough to try." |"Is... is he serious?" Atugia whispers, leaning in and trying not to draw too much notice from mother and son. "He knows that's his mother, doesn't he? It'd... it'd be like me trying to chat up Carmen or something. I don't know if I'd have the stomach for it." |Azyrran takes one look at the scene playing out before her eyes and shakes her head. "Well, he's brave enough to attempt it, I'll give him that. A bold move, indeed — let's see if it'll work out for him, shall we?" |"Oh. Huh." While this scene has been playing out, Quin's taken a careful step back, putting some distance between him and the dup by the firepit. The bunny-man looks thoughtful, scratching his chin, then shrugs. Penny for his thoughts? "Can't say she's my type, but I can see the play that he's trying to make here — and no, he's not really trying to pick up his mother. If what everyone says about Garret is true, that his temperament is distinctly similar to his mother's, then she should recognize as much in him." Quin frowns and thins his lips. "It's a bold play all right, I'll give him that. Let's see if it works out for him." |Kiyoko frowns at the sight by the firepit, looking distinctly puzzled. You're just about to ask your fox-wife what the matter is, but at length comprehension clearly dawns upon her expression, and the confusion clears up into a warm smile. "I see what he is attempting to do here. While it may be risky, if it works, it would work well, and his temperament is that of an oni — risk and danger do not deter him, be it from foolhardiness or otherwise." Two coppers for her thoughts, then? Kiyoko swishes her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails at you, batting you on the legs. "Well, I could tell you, Beloved, but it would be much more fun to let this play out and allow you to realize it for yourself." |"W-what is he doing?" Ryn whispers, leaning in and trying not to draw too much notice from mother and son. "Is he actually trying to chat up his mother?" That would appear to be the case, yes. "Oh." Ryn raises a hand to her forehead. "I... I don't think I've got anything to say to that." ] Several moments pass in silence as Gweyr turns the spit over and over, letting fat from the cooking cut of seal drip onto the fire; she's clearly less interested in dinner now that this newcomer's sauntered his way into her home. At length, she sniffs the air again, and sighs. "You're too honest for your own good, kid. I don't think you're lying, I do believe you meant every word of what you just said — and I'm not sure if I prefer this over you outright bullshitting me to my face. Don't you know that flattery only counts when it's not flattery?" "Well, it's a good thing that you believe in me, ma'am, and to be frankly, I'm honored that you do. So long as someone as fetching as you must've been in your youth believes in the strongest man walking the face of the earth, he's undefeatable." That manages to get a wry smile out of the old wolfess despite her previously dour and morose demeanor — or maybe she's just showing him her teeth. "Oh, as fetching as I must've been in my youth, you say? That means you're saying I'm not a looker now?" "Not in the way of youth and beauty, no, ma'am. You know that's not true, and I believe you just said something about flattery only counting when it's not flattery." Gweyr pulls the chunk of cooked seal off the fire and gives it a good, appreciative whiff. "Ha! That's what I might've said myself thirty years ago. I haven't even asked you your name, kid, but you remind me a lot of myself when I was your age; before I met my husband, I'd try to regale guys I thought were cute with this kind of braindead nonsense. In fact, you might even be the — you might even be the — " her words hang in the air as realization slowly dawns. Slowly, Gweyr looks between Garret and you, biting her muzzle with her snaggled teeth. "It isn't, is it? But how could it be anyone else? You certainly had the means to bring him here, [pc.name]." It's at this point that Garret drops the act, his forward demeanor changing to... well, it's still forward, but in a different way. Shuffling over to Gweyr's side of the fire, he gives his mother a great big hug — it's a little clumsy given all the thick furs they're both wearing, but it's nonetheless equally heartfelt. "Mom." Gweyr sets down the skewer of seal very carefully by the firepit, and then returns the hug with all her might — one that Garret's able to accept with ease and without being crushed to pieces by her broad arms. "Oh, my son. My dear son... I'm so sorry, and yet so happy. [pc.name]! Why the fuck didn't you say anything, you glorious [pc.mf |bastard |bitch ]?" You thought it would be more poignant if she connected the dots herself. Besides, watching Garret chatting and cheering up his own mother was [pc.isDK |funny |kind of heartwarming ]; you didn't want to interrupt a good thing going, did you? It was only a matter of time before Gweyr saw her younger self in how he was acting and made the connection, but you were still interested in seeing how long it'd take. Now that it's clear what Garret was attempting, you have admit it was a risky thing to do, but... well, poor odds have never been that much of a deterrent to mother or son. Gweyr chuckles dryly, although there's no humor in it, then turns back to Garret. "Strongest man in the world, eh? You might have a chance, given that I didn't manage to break you into several pieces despite trying with that hug. Let me get a good look at you, kid." Garret shies away a little, but Gweyr firmly takes him by the chin and inspects his jaw before moving over the rest of his face. You're not exactly sure what she's trying to find in him, but it takes a good while of poking and prodding with her callused fingers before she settles back with a satisfied sigh. "Ah... the last time I saw you, you couldn't have been three? Four? Gods, I'm so old, my memory's starting to go. So, why'd you come all the way out here? Not that I'm not glad I've finally gotten to see you before I die, but — " "That's exactly why I talked [pc.name] into bringing me to see you, Mom." Garret folds his arms and does his best to look as resolute as he can. "You're not going to rot out here, you're not going to just lay down here in this cave out in the middle of the ice and die. I don't care what you did twenty years ago, who was at fault, but while you may have hunted Tollus all you could, that doesn't mean you're done, or that you're useless now." "Twenty years ago. So you remember, then." Garret shakes his head. "Gwyn doesn't. I don't either, not very much. You told me something before you left, and I remember that it was important, but I don't recall what. No, [pc.name] here told me something of what happened that day, and then I squeezed the rest out of the old man and Sanders." "And do you think I was a monster?" "Oh, you were a monster, Mom. But you were the monster people needed. When people like Tollus come after everything you love with a knife, those civilized fuckers had better pray there's a monster looking out for them. I can't say I don't see where Sanders was coming from, but the only reason he's got the luxury to be civilized is because he's got a monster like you watching his back. Even if I'm your son, I don't know if I can say that you were perfectly in the right back then... but you don't deserve to just lay down and die. Not when so many people need you, not when I need you." That answer seems to satisfy Gweyr; the old wolfess grunts and nods, although you note she still won't look her son in the eye. "Come home with me, Mom. That's why I came all the way here — [pc.name] said I was the only one in the world who had the means and the will to do it." He's right. If there's anyone who could convince her to come home after all these years, it's Garret. Just because she can't fight the cult directly doesn't mean she's lost all purpose in life. There's still so much more she needs to do, so many people who need her whether they admit it or not. "..." "[pc.names] right, Mom. The old man's tried his best in bringing me up, but I honestly don't think he's got what it takes. Gwyn's done perfectly well under him, but I..." "I've heard about some of the things that you've gotten yourself into, yes. Not from your father, but even so." "... And it's not just that, either. After this happened to fall into my hands, I've done a bit of thinking about who I am. Who you are. Growing up, no one in town would talk about you — either because they arrived after you were exiled, or weren't about to tell me. And look." He reaches into his furs and draws out the heavy medallion. "I also managed to get my hands on this." The glint of gold catches on the firelight, the clink of chain echoes in the little cavern. Gweyr turns the medallion over and over in her hands, squeezing it as if to test how real it is, picking at the embossed insignia of the crossed swords with a claw. Her breathing's slow, deliberate and heavy, and at last, she looks up at Garret. "For years I marched under this banner at your grandfather's side, and after he got his skull stoved in I led my own by it. How did you get your hands on this, kid?" "It's a long story, Mom. But I know who we are. Who you are. Who I am." "And who are you?" "I'm just a tavernkeeper's son, that's all." "Not a wrong answer, and not a bad one either." "So, Mom... will you come home with me?" Gweyr looks away from Garret and into the fire. "I don't know. What would I do?" "Do what you didn't for the last twenty years. Raise Gwyn and me. I don't blame you for staying away all this while; thanks to [pc.name], I've seen some small part of what Master Tollus is capable of, and am glad that if nothing else, you bought us some time for us to act. But now that you're done with that, it's time for you to come home and finish the job you started by having us to begin with. Leave Tollus to people like [pc.name] and me, but your job's not done yet. The same people still need you, only in a different way." You raise an eyebrow at Garret. He's a lot more errant now than from when you found him cooped up in a cage, being used by a druidess as a doggy dildo... "Hey, I only did it so that she wouldn't hurt the loggers. The strongest man in the world wouldn't have stood for it for too long." And you remember a rather different turn of events from back then... Gweyr chuckles and shakes her head. "If I learned anything from my little tiff with Sanders, it's that people can be completely honest about the exact same events and tell very different stories. It's all about your perspective on things. I know something about how my daughter sees my departure from the family..." "I'm not taking no for an answer, Mom. Sure, if you go back and try to fix that bridge for the rest of your life, you might not succeed in getting through to Gwyn. But if you don't go back and try to begin with, then that 'might' turns into a 'will.' "Forget despair, Mom. I'm not talking about that. Everyone understands that despair is worse than useless. What I'm talking about is a refusal to hope, which is entirely different. And the problem with a refusal to hope is this: you won't be in a position to act if things happen to go your way. If there's anything I learned since [pc.name] let me out of that cage, it's that you've got to try, even though you know perfectly well how low the percentages are. Even if the chances of something breaking your way are low, the chances of making it when they do do so are very, very high." "Which is why you're here?" "I never had any doubt that I'd return to the old man and Gwyn with you, Mom." "Irrational self-confidence." Gweyr turns the old golden medallion over by the fire once more, then heaves a sigh before handing it back to Garret. "Here, kid, you keep this. If it were ever mine, it's yours now. I suppose I'm not getting any younger, and it would be nice to sleep in a proper bed again before I die."

Now that it's clear what Garret was attempting, you have admit it was a risky thing to do, but... well, poor odds have never been that much of a deterrent to mother or son. Gweyr chuckles dryly, although there's no humor in it, then turns back to Garret. "Strongest man in the world, eh? You might have a chance, given that I didn't manage to break you into several pieces despite trying with that hug. Let me get a good look at you, kid." Garret shies away a little, but Gweyr firmly takes him by the chin and inspects his jaw before moving over the rest of his face. You're not exactly sure what she's trying to find in him, but it takes a good while of poking and prodding with her callused fingers before she settles back with a satisfied sigh. "Ah... the last time I saw you, you couldn't have been three? Four? Gods, I'm so old, my memory's starting to go. So, why'd you come all the way out here? Not that I'm not glad I've finally gotten to see you before I die, but — " "That's exactly why I talked [pc.name] into bringing me to see you, Mom." Garret folds his arms and does his best to look as resolute as he can. "You're not going to rot out here, you're not going to just lay down here in this cave out in the middle of the ice and die. I don't care what you did twenty years ago, who was at fault, but while you may have hunted Tollus all you could, that doesn't mean you're done, or that you're useless now." "Twenty years ago. So you remember, then." Garret shakes his head. "Gwyn doesn't. I don't either, not very much. You told me something before you left, and I remember that it was important, but I don't recall what. No, [pc.name] here told me something of what happened that day, and then I squeezed the rest out of the old man and Sanders." "And do you think I was a monster?" "Oh, you were a monster, Mom. But you were the monster people needed. When people like Tollus come after everything you love with a knife, those civilized fuckers had better pray there's a monster looking out for them. I can't say I don't see where Sanders was coming from, but the only reason he's got the luxury to be civilized is because he's got a monster like you watching his back. Even if I'm your son, I don't know if I can say that you were perfectly in the right back then... but you don't deserve to just lay down and die. Not when so many people need you, not when I need you." That answer seems to satisfy Gweyr; the old wolfess grunts and nods, although you note she still won't look her son in the eye. "Come home with me, Mom. That's why I came all the way here — [pc.name] said I was the only one in the world who had the means and the will to do it." He's right. If there's anyone who could convince her to come home after all these years, it's Garret. Just because she can't fight the cult directly doesn't mean she's lost all purpose in life. There's still so much more she needs to do, so many people who need her whether they admit it or not. "..." "[pc.names] right, Mom. The old man's tried his best in bringing me up, but I honestly don't think he's got what it takes. Gwyn's done perfectly well under him, but I..." "I've heard about some of the things that you've gotten yourself into, yes. Not from your father, but even so." "... And it's not just that, either. After this happened to fall into my hands, I've done a bit of thinking about who I am. Who you are. Growing up, no one in town would talk about you — either because they arrived after you were exiled, or weren't about to tell me. And look." He reaches into his furs and draws out the heavy medallion. "I also managed to get my hands on this." The glint of gold catches on the firelight, the clink of chain echoes in the little cavern. Gweyr turns the medallion over and over in her hands, squeezing it as if to test how real it is, picking at the embossed insignia of the crossed swords with a claw. Her breathing's slow, deliberate and heavy, and at last, she looks up at Garret. "For years I marched under this banner at your grandfather's side, and after he got his skull stoved in I led my own by it. How did you get your hands on this, kid?" "It's a long story, Mom. But I know who we are. Who you are. Who I am." "And who are you?" "I'm just a tavernkeeper's son, that's all." "Not a wrong answer, and not a bad one either." "So, Mom... will you come home with me?" Gweyr looks away from Garret and into the fire. "I don't know. What would I do?" "Do what you didn't for the last twenty years. Raise Gwyn and me. I don't blame you for staying away all this while; thanks to [pc.name], I've seen some small part of what Master Tollus is capable of, and am glad that if nothing else, you bought us some time for us to act. But now that you're done with that, it's time for you to come home and finish the job you started by having us to begin with. Leave Tollus to people like [pc.name] and me, but your job's not done yet. The same people still need you, only in a different way." You raise an eyebrow at Garret. He's a lot more errant now than from when you found him cooped up in a cage, being used by a druidess as a doggy dildo... "Hey, I only did it so that she wouldn't hurt the loggers. The strongest man in the world wouldn't have stood for it for too long." And you remember a rather different turn of events from back then... Gweyr chuckles and shakes her head. "If I learned anything from my little tiff with Sanders, it's that people can be completely honest about the exact same events and tell very different stories. It's all about your perspective on things. I know something about how my daughter sees my departure from the family..." "I'm not taking no for an answer, Mom. Sure, if you go back and try to fix that bridge for the rest of your life, you might not succeed in getting through to Gwyn. But if you don't go back and try to begin with, then that 'might' turns into a 'will.' "Forget despair, Mom. I'm not talking about that. Everyone understands that despair is worse than useless. What I'm talking about is a refusal to hope, which is entirely different. And the problem with a refusal to hope is this: you won't be in a position to act if things happen to go your way. If there's anything I learned since [pc.name] let me out of that cage, it's that you've got to try, even though you know perfectly well how low the percentages are. Even if the chances of something breaking your way are low, the chances of making it when they do do so are very, very high." "Which is why you're here?" "I never had any doubt that I'd return to the old man and Gwyn with you, Mom." "Irrational self-confidence." Gweyr turns the old golden medallion over by the fire once more, then heaves a sigh before handing it back to Garret. "Here, kid, you keep this. If it were ever mine, it's yours now. I suppose I'm not getting any younger, and it would be nice to sleep in a proper bed again before I die." "

rows.original:
The next day dawns, ashes from the firepit still warm as harsh sunlight streams into the little cubbyhole from the merciless, cloudless sky above. Gweyr and Garret are already up by the time you wake, taking down the furs from the walls and kicking stones over the firepit.
            
            Need some help with that?
            
            Gweyr shakes her head. "Nah, I'll have Garret do it. He's already got plenty of character, but it won't hurt for him to build some more. Don't wait up for the both of us; I know that your time is precious and all, since you're now the one spearheading the effort to put paid to Tollus's ass. I don't have many things with me, but I've still got to make a trip around the rift, let my neighbors know I'm moving out so they won't think I've disappeared on them or anything. It's only polite, you know? That, and introduce my idiot son to them."
            
            That's honestly very kind of her... but at the same time, she's got to be proud of Garret to want to show him off about the rift before leaving.
            
            "He's... like what I used to be when I was his age. And after everything he said last night, I thought back to those days and all the things my father used to do for me before he got his head stoved in by a warhammer, and realized that I might as well start on all the years I missed out by doing the same for him. Knowing people is extremely important in this world, after all — the same way my father introduced me to his mercenary contacts, so am I introducing him to the jotuns, selkies and more. Never know when they might come in handy.
            
            "I missed two decades of my childrens' lives, [pc.name]; now I've got a daughter who hates me and a son who has his heart in the right place but is missing his head. Might as well start fixing things with a strong start. Anyway... as I said, go ahead and return to Hawkethorne without us, [pc.name]. After showing my son around, we're going to head off the glacier the long way."
            
            The long way?
            
            "The way that doesn't involve using the elves' elevator. Rather treacherous, so don't wait up for us. Garret may be my son, but if he's to be going around telling everyone who'll listen that he's the strongest man in the world, I've got to test his ass first."
            
            All right, then. You'll meet her back at the Frost Hound.
            
            "It shouldn't take too long, really. We'll be there before you know it. Might even get there ahead of you! Now then, if you don't mind, I've got to get Garret to pack away all my stuff. We won't be carrying down all of it — we can give some to the jotuns and selkies — but as scarce as things are in the rift, I'm not just going to leave good material to wear away."
rows.translation:
第二天清晨来临，火坑里的灰烬依然温暖，刺眼的阳光从无云的蓝天倾泻下来，照进这个小小的空间。当你醒来时，格温尔和Garret已经起床了，他们正在把墙上的毛皮取下来，然后把石头扔到火坑里。
            
            需要帮忙吗？

格温尔摇了摇头：“不用，让我让加勒特来做吧。他本来就有很多角色形象可以塑造了，再塑造一些也不会有什么坏处。别等我们俩了；我知道你的时间很宝贵，毕竟现在是你正在带头努力解决托卢斯这个麻烦。 我身上没带太多东西，但还是得去裂隙那边走一趟，告诉我的邻居们我要搬走了，这样他们就不会以为我突然消失了什么的。这也是出于礼貌，你知道吧？另外，还得把我的那个傻儿子介绍给他们认识。"
            
            说实话，她这样做真的很贴心……但同时，她也应该为加勒特感到骄傲，因为他想在离开之前向大家展示这个裂隙。

“他……就像我在他这个年纪时的样子。 在听了他昨晚说的那些话之后，我回想起那些日子，以及在我父亲被战锤击中头部之前，他为我做过的所有事情。我突然意识到，既然我已经错过了那么多年的时光，那么现在就应该开始为他做同样的事情，弥补那些失去的时光。 在这个世界上，结识各种各样的人确实非常重要——就像我父亲把我介绍给他的雇佣兵朋友们一样，现在我也正在把他介绍给那些 约顿巨人、海豹精 以及其他各种人。谁知道什么时候他们会派上用场呢。
            
            我错过了孩子们二十年的成长过程， [pc.name]现在，我有一个恨我的女儿，还有一个心地善良但做事欠考虑的儿子。既然如此，还不如从现在开始努力改善这些状况。总之……就像我之前说的，你们可以不用等我们，直接回到鹰棘镇去吧。 [pc.name]等我带儿子逛完周围的环境后，我们就打算绕道离开冰川。”

绕道？

“就是不使用精灵们准备的电梯那条路。那条路有点危险，所以你们不用等我们了。 加勒特虽然是我的儿子，但如果他到处跟别人吹嘘自己是世界上最强壮的人，那我总得先考验一下他的实力。

好吧，那我们在霜犬酒馆那里见吧。
            
            其实应该不会花太长时间，我们很快就会到那里的，甚至可能会比你先到！现在，如果你不介意的话，我得去让加勒特把我的东西都收拾好。我们不会把所有的东西都带下去——可以分一些给那些侏儒和人鱼——但在这个裂隙地带，物资本来就非常稀缺，我总不能把那些好用的衣物都留下不管吧。"

rows.original: No sooner have you stepped into Hawkethorne's town square do you feel it: a change in the air, a shift in the atmosphere [dayNight |that the other people on the streets sense as well. It spreads from the north gate to the Old Forest, and passers-by around you start speaking in hushed tones and pull their clothes about themselves protectively, as if a chill wind had passed through the town square |that lingers on the edge of your senses in the night air. Spreading forth from the north gate that leads to the Old Forest, it sweeps past you like a chill evening wind, and with much the same effect even if the air is still ]. And then, striding imperiously into the town square — or as imperiously as someone who's seen the things she's seen can be — is Gweyr, using the shaft of her bone spear as a walking stick. Garret's at her side, and with the two together it's little wonder that they didn't have any trouble at the gate. [dayNight |The militia wouldn't have stood a chance... not that she would have started anything, of course. Woman's too old for that |Seeing her loom out of the cover of night like that, even with the faint street lamps... it's enough to inspire a sudden and fervent rekindling of one's faith in the gods ]. No one actually pays particular notice to her — it's the kind of careful ignorance one affects when one most definitely doesn't want to know what's going on and wants no part of it. And yet even so, everyone gives Gweyr a wide berth as she strolls down the streets of Hawkethorne with Garret at her side, a small bubble of space about her as if a mystical force were pushing people away from her. That being said, you're perfectly fine. Gweyr acknowledges you with a nod as you step up to meet her and her son, and together the three of you approach the statue that's the square's centerpiece; River's there as always, and he's the first of the townsfolk you've seen to acknowledge her presence, pulling the hood of his poncho over his eyes and giving his lute a strum. "[dayNight |Hello |Evening ], Gweyr." "Well, if it isn't little River. You haven't aged a bit in twenty years. How do you do it?" "It's all about the attitude and posture, Gweyr. Smiling takes years off your countenance, you know. Standing up straight, another handful. That, and having white hair to begin with means no one knows I'm graying." "You're still singing for your supper?" "That I am," River replies, leaning back into the bench at the statue's feet. "Thanks to you, really. You saved me and the statue... whatever else anyone thinks, you did as much, and I owe you for that." "You didn't try to speak up for me back then... but I don't blame you for it. We'll catch up later, kitten, but my son has to bring me home, doesn't he?" "Let's go, Mom." They sweep past the statue and across the square, their path inevitably taking them past the chapel of Velun and straight into Sanders' waiting arms[var0 | — and with Liaden at his side, no less ]. The graying priest stands in the middle of their path, arms folded, not overtly threatening but nevertheless resolute. Gweyr stops a decent distance away, the two sizing each other up; several tense moments pass, then [var0 |Liaden tugs at her father's arm. "Dad. Don't do this. Let me handle her instead." "What I've tried so hard to do all these years, Liaden, what started all of this in the first place, was a young man's hope that he could avoid having to 'handle' people. And despite how things turned out, I still think it's a hope worth having." He pats Liaden on the hand. "And let's be serious. If you actually tried to handle her, she'd gut you like a fish. Pardon my bluntness, sweet pea, but I hope you understand I'm serious about this." "Dad!"[party.has azyrran | Noticing Azyrran in your party, Liaden shoots the hive knight an imploring glance, but to no avail. Bold as she might be, even Azyrran knows that this is a matter between the two... so long as it stays contained between Sanders and Gweyr, that is. ] "Don't worry, Liaden, it's going to be all right. This day was long in coming; just like you, what I've done in the past is catching up with me." He turns to the three of you. " |Sanders speaks." ][pc.name]. Garret. Gweyr. I've been expecting this moment ever since Garret stormed into my chapel and told me he was bringing you back." "And are you going to stop us, Riordan?" Riordan. It feels strange to have someone call Sanders by his first name... "That depends on what you intend." "Clear the path. I'm going home to my kids. I didn't have the time to think about it before, not when I was chasing Tollus all over the Marches, but now that I'm not it's time for me to make up for all the time I've lost — [pc.name] and my son were kind enough to remind me that my life wasn't quite over just yet." "And that's all you're going to do, Gweyr?" Gweyr doesn't reply immediately, instead looking [var0 |between Liaden and Sanders, a bitter smile creeping onto her muzzle. "I'd heard you had a crisis of faith and stopped being a Lumian, Riordan. Didn't expect you to have taken the other aspects of her creed so seriously. Quite the fetching girl you have there." Liaden scowls and moves to step between her father and Gweyr, but Sanders stops his daughter with an upraised hand. "I think we've all spent a lot of time thinking about that night in the intervening years." "Yes. You and I both, by the looks of things." "And have we come to any conclusions?" |up at the sky as if beseeching the gods for something, then at Garret, before returning her gaze to Sanders. "Yes." "Had an epiphany of sorts, then?" ] "On my part? Only that I'm getting old and I want to be with my kids before I die. That's all, Riordan. You and I may have been amongst those who first settled this village, but it won't be too long before it passes down to the likes of my son[var0| and your daughter]. Both you and I have fewer years left before we go and see the gods." Sanders takes a step forward, and you see Gweyr's entire demeanor change with but the slightest of movements, ready to spring if need be.[var0 | Liaden blanches, and pulls more insistently at her father's arm, but thankfully her concern is misplaced. ] The two of them eye each other, perhaps searching for the unfathomable, perhaps wondering who will make the first move, or allow for disengagement in a way that will allow both parties to save face. Another stare-down ensues, the two locked into an impasse until Gweyr grunts and gives way, breaking the stony, steely silence. "So once more, Riordan: are you going to stop me?" Sanders looks [var0 |over his shoulder at his daughter |askance ] and sighs. "Everyone who could be argued to have a legitimate grievance against you is either dead or departed from Hawkethorne, Gweyr. Garret and [pc.name] tell me you've been working hard to atone for what you did, so anything that remains is between your conscience and the gods. So long as you only do what you said you're going to do, Gweyr... I shan't stop you." "While I've thought about it many a time in the last twenty years, Riordan, I don't regret it. I'm too old to go about playing butcher, and you're in no shape to be gallivanting around, either. Now, if you're not going to do anything about me, kindly clear a path. I'm going home." Sanders hesitates. While he hides his anguish well, the deliberate slowness with which he half-turns and steps back onto the chapel's stone steps tells you all you need to know. Gweyr follows suit, the tension draining from her muscles, and sweeps past Sanders[var0 | and Liaden | ] to the last stretch leading up to the Frost Hound.
rows.translation: 你一走进鹰棘镇的镇广场，就能立刻感受到那种变化：空气中的氛围不同了，整个气氛也发生了改变。 [dayNight |街上的其他人们也能感受到这种气息。这种氛围从北门开始蔓延，一直传到旧森林，周围的路人都会开始小声交谈，还会不由自主地拉紧衣服，仿佛有一阵寒风吹过了城镇广场。 |那种气息在夜空中萦绕在你的感官边缘。它从通往旧森林的北门开始扩散，像一阵寒冷的晚风一样从你身边掠过，即使空气静止不动，这种感觉也依然存在。 ]然后，格薇尔以一种威严的姿态走进了城镇广场——或者说，以一个经历过那么多事情的人所能表现出的威严姿态走了进去。她将骨制长矛当作拐杖使用。加勒特跟在她身边，有了他们两个的配合，他们在城门处自然没有遇到任何麻烦。 [dayNight |那些民兵根本没有任何机会……当然，她也不会主动挑起事端。毕竟，她年纪已经太大，不适合再参与这种事了。 |看到她那样从夜色中悄然出现，即便只有微弱的街灯照明……这也足以让人突然重新燃起对神明的信仰。 ]实际上，没有人会特别注意她——这种漠不关心的态度，恰恰源于人们根本不想了解正在发生什么，也不想卷入其中。然而，每当格韦尔与加勒特并肩走在鹰棘镇的街道上时，所有人都会自觉地与她保持距离，仿佛有一股神秘的力量在将人们推开，在她周围形成了一片空旷的空间。 话虽如此，你完全没有问题。当你走上前与她和她的儿子见面时，格温尔向你点了点头表示认可。随后你们三人一起走向了位于广场中央的那座雕像；里弗像往常一样也在那里，他是你在镇上遇到的第一个注意到她的存在的人——他拉下了披风上的兜帽，轻轻拨弄着他的鲁特琴。 "[dayNight |你好 |傍晚 ]哎呀，原来是小河啊。二十年过去了，你一点都没变老啊，真是不可思议。” “关键在于态度和姿势啊，格温尔。你知道，微笑能让你的面容看起来年轻许多；而站得笔直也会让你看起来更有精神。 再加上我本来就有一头白发，所以没人能看出我的头发正在变白。” “你到现在还在为了一点食物而唱歌吗？” “确实是在啊，”里弗回答道，他靠在雕像足部下的长椅上，“真的要感谢你呢。 你救了我，也救了那座雕像……无论别人怎么想，你确实做了很多，因此我欠你一个人情。” “那时候你并没有试图为我出头……但我并不怪你。我们以后再慢慢聊吧，小猫咪，不过我的儿子现在必须带我回家，对吧？我们走吧，妈妈。” 他们掠过雕像，穿过广场，沿途必然会经过维伦小教堂，然后直接走进桑德斯等待他们的怀抱。[var0 | ——而且还有李亚登在他身边。 ]那位头发花白的牧师站在他们的道路中央，双臂交叉抱在胸前，虽然没有表现出明显的威胁，但态度却十分坚决。格韦尔在距离他一段适当距离的地方停了下来，两人互相打量着对方；几秒钟的紧张气氛之后…… [var0 |莉亚登拉住了父亲的胳膊。 “爸爸，别这样。让我来处理这件事吧。” rows.raw: " No sooner have you stepped into Hawkethorne's town square do you feel it: a change in the air, a shift in the atmosphere [dayNight |that the other people on the streets sense as well. It spreads from the north gate to the Old Forest, and passers-by around you start speaking in hushed tones and pull their clothes about themselves protectively, as if a chill wind had passed through the town square |that lingers on the edge of your senses in the night air. Spreading forth from the north gate that leads to the Old Forest, it sweeps past you like a chill evening wind, and with much the same effect even if the air is still ]. And then, striding imperiously into the town square — or as imperiously as someone who's seen the things she's seen can be — is Gweyr, using the shaft of her bone spear as a walking stick. Garret's at her side, and with the two together it's little wonder that they didn't have any trouble at the gate. [dayNight |The militia wouldn't have stood a chance... not that she would have started anything, of course. Woman's too old for that |Seeing her loom out of the cover of night like that, even with the faint street lamps... it's enough to inspire a sudden and fervent rekindling of one's faith in the gods ]. No one actually pays particular notice to her — it's the kind of careful ignorance one affects when one most definitely doesn't want to know what's going on and wants no part of it. And yet even so, everyone gives Gweyr a wide berth as she strolls down the streets of Hawkethorne with Garret at her side, a small bubble of space about her as if a mystical force were pushing people away from her. That being said, you're perfectly fine. Gweyr acknowledges you with a nod as you step up to meet her and her son, and together the three of you approach the statue that's the square's centerpiece; River's there as always, and he's the first of the townsfolk you've seen to acknowledge her presence, pulling the hood of his poncho over his eyes and giving his lute a strum. "[dayNight |Hello |Evening ], Gweyr." "Well, if it isn't little River. You haven't aged a bit in twenty years. How do you do it?" "It's all about the attitude and posture, Gweyr. Smiling takes years off your countenance, you know. Standing up straight, another handful. That, and having white hair to begin with means no one knows I'm graying." "You're still singing for your supper?" "That I am," River replies, leaning back into the bench at the statue's feet. "Thanks to you, really. You saved me and the statue... whatever else anyone thinks, you did as much, and I owe you for that." "You didn't try to speak up for me back then... but I don't blame you for it. We'll catch up later, kitten, but my son has to bring me home, doesn't he?" "Let's go, Mom." They sweep past the statue and across the square, their path inevitably taking them past the chapel of Velun and straight into Sanders' waiting arms[var0 | — and with Liaden at his side, no less ]. The graying priest stands in the middle of their path, arms folded, not overtly threatening but nevertheless resolute. Gweyr stops a decent distance away, the two sizing each other up; several tense moments pass, then [var0 |Liaden tugs at her father's arm. "Dad. Don't do this. Let me handle her instead." "What I've tried so hard to do all these years, Liaden, what started all of this in the first place, was a young man's hope that he could avoid having to 'handle' people. And despite how things turned out, I still think it's a hope worth having." He pats Liaden on the hand. "And let's be serious. If you actually tried to handle her, she'd gut you like a fish. Pardon my bluntness, sweet pea, but I hope you understand I'm serious about this." "Dad!"[party.has azyrran | Noticing Azyrran in your party, Liaden shoots the hive knight an imploring glance, but to no avail. Bold as she might be, even Azyrran knows that this is a matter between the two... so long as it stays contained between Sanders and Gweyr, that is. ] "Don't worry, Liaden, it's going to be all right. This day was long in coming; just like you, what I've done in the past is catching up with me." He turns to the three of you. " |Sanders speaks." ][pc.name]. Garret. Gweyr. I've been expecting this moment ever since Garret stormed into my chapel and told me he was bringing you back." "And are you going to stop us, Riordan?" Riordan. It feels strange to have someone call Sanders by his first name... "That depends on what you intend." "Clear the path. I'm going home to my kids. I didn't have the time to think about it before, not when I was chasing Tollus all over the Marches, but now that I'm not it's time for me to make up for all the time I've lost — [pc.name] and my son were kind enough to remind me that my life wasn't quite over just yet." "And that's all you're going to do, Gweyr?" Gweyr doesn't reply immediately, instead looking [var0 |between Liaden and Sanders, a bitter smile creeping onto her muzzle. "I'd heard you had a crisis of faith and stopped being a Lumian, Riordan. Didn't expect you to have taken the other aspects of her creed so seriously. Quite the fetching girl you have there." Liaden scowls and moves to step between her father and Gweyr, but Sanders stops his daughter with an upraised hand. "I think we've all spent a lot of time thinking about that night in the intervening years." "Yes. You and I both, by the looks of things." "And have we come to any conclusions?" |up at the sky as if beseeching the gods for something, then at Garret, before returning her gaze to Sanders. "Yes." "Had an epiphany of sorts, then?" ] "On my part? Only that I'm getting old and I want to be with my kids before I die. That's all, Riordan. You and I may have been amongst those who first settled this village, but it won't be too long before it passes down to the likes of my son[var0| and your daughter]. Both you and I have fewer years left before we go and see the gods." Sanders takes a step forward, and you see Gweyr's entire demeanor change with but the slightest of movements, ready to spring if need be.[var0 | Liaden blanches, and pulls more insistently at her father's arm, but thankfully her concern is misplaced. ] The two of them eye each other, perhaps searching for the unfathomable, perhaps wondering who will make the first move, or allow for disengagement in a way that will allow both parties to save face. Another stare-down ensues, the two locked into an impasse until Gweyr grunts and gives way, breaking the stony, steely silence. "So once more, Riordan: are you going to stop me?" Sanders looks [var0 |over his shoulder at his daughter |askance ] and sighs. "Everyone who could be argued to have a legitimate grievance against you is either dead or departed from Hawkethorne, Gweyr. Garret and [pc.name] tell me you've been working hard to atone for what you did, so anything that remains is between your conscience and the gods. So long as you only do what you said you're going to do, Gweyr... I shan't stop you." "While I've thought about it many a time in the last twenty years, Riordan, I don't regret it. I'm too old to go about playing butcher, and you're in no shape to be gallivanting around, either. Now, if you're not going to do anything about me, kindly clear a path. I'm going home." Sanders hesitates. While he hides his anguish well, the deliberate slowness with which he half-turns and steps back onto the chapel's stone steps tells you all you need to know. Gweyr follows suit, the tension draining from her muscles, and sweeps past Sanders[var0 | and Liaden | ] to the last stretch leading up to the Frost Hound. "

rows.original: It takes a little longer than expected — not surprising in retrospect, but certainly melancholic. Gweyr pauses for a moment to inspect the hanging wolfshead sign over the entrance, to thumb the grain of the doorway's timbers. The old wolfess takes a deep breath, squares her shoulders, and then rubs her temples. She's afraid. "Mom..." "I remember when these were new; I put them in place myself," Gweyr mutters thoughtfully. "Never thought I'd have reason to see them again. And now that I'm here, I find myself wondering just how I'm going to face your sister." "...She's half the reason why you're here, Mom." "I know, kid. Just give me a second or two to gather myself. Funny, isn't it? A woman who survived the dark places under the Heartlands as a mercenary, who lived her life in the cold — she's afraid of facing her own daughter. It shouldn't make sense, and yet it does." But at last, Gweyr gathers herself; Garret and you push open the door for her, and she steps in. [dayNight |There aren't that many patrons in the common room given that the evening crowd hasn't gathered yet, but that just means the old wolfess is more able to gather notice as a hush falls over the taproom. What spoils the mood even more, though, |The common room is in a reasonable state of carousel as is expected for the Frost Hound, and doesn't pause in the least as the old wolfess makes her entrance. No, what spoils the mood ] is the fact that instead of Garth behind the bar with his mugs, Gwyn's manning his post, a distinctive scowl on her face that leaves little doubt as to what she thinks of her mother's homecoming. [gwyn.isPregnant |As pregnant as she is, Gwyn's all too ready to sweep out from around the counter, waddling up to her mother and glaring daggers at her. It's sobering, the juxtaposition of all the anger packed into a pregnant woman, but in the end... it's not really surprising, is it? |Showing her teeth, Gwyn's all too ready to sweep out from around the counter, striding up to her mother and glaring daggers at her. It's sobering, seeing such naked hatred completely consume the usually docile Gwyn, but then... this outcome was never really in doubt, was it? ] "So that's what you look like. You dare to show your face here," Gwyn growls, trying her best to sound aggressive and not-so-surreptitiously choking back a sob in the process. "You dare! I was the one who stayed with Daddy all these years! I was the one who cooked his meals, darned his clothes, listened to him, while you — you — what have you done for him, anyway!" "I bought all of you time to have a future," Gweyr replies quietly. "I can't believe you're acting like some kind of martyr after throwing the three of us away like so much trash for years! I won't let you steal Da — " "Gwyneth, that's enough." Gwyn looks like she's going to scream, but her inner submissiveness, especially to her father, clashes with the rage roiling inside of her at the sound of Garth's voice. Moaning, the nursery matron raises her hands to her face and starts to weep. "And don't turn on the waterworks for me." Garth says as he closes the last of the steps down from the Hound's second floor. "Not in front of the customers, either. Go out back and we'll settle this later." Gwyn doesn't seem to hear her father, and after another bout of sniffling and sobbing Garret sighs and takes his sister out back, hooking his hands under her shoulders and gently but firmly leading her away from the scene. That leaves Garth, Gweyr and you — and everyone else in the common room, of course. "I leave our daughter to tend the bar while I clean the guest rooms, and this happens; you're still capable of making an entrance as ever. Welcome home, for what it's worth." "Our daughter..." "Like you, she was never one for lying." As Gweyr shakes her head and lets her shoulders slump, Garth turns to you. "Well then, [pc.name], you've brought my wife home, after all these years. I suppose I should thank you for that, even if I suspect I won't have peace under this roof for a little while." He can damn well put up with it, then. This isn't just about him, or Gweyr, or Sanders. You've been here in Hawkethorne for a while now, and heard the rumors going about town — as what passes for the village alderman, he shouldn't be surprised that tongues wag about him, and some of the things said are unkind. On the other hand, people saying that Gwyn's first litter of pups was fathered either by him or Garret — that's the kind of hearsay that truly gains legs when it's plausible to begin with. "Yes, I've heard that one, and many others. As much as it hurts, what's it got to do with bringing my wife back, [pc.name]?" What's it got to do is that the buck stops here. Yes, you've heard all sides of the tale as to what happened twenty years ago. No, you don't think anyone will ever truly be apportioned the blame, and it's one of those situations where frankly everyone had a hand in mucking it all up. But the consequences of their actions so long ago have bled not just into their lives from that day on, but the lives of those around them — Garret and Gwyn, for example — and maybe even Hawkethorne at large. Just like before, no one wants to admit the problem that's lying in plain sight, letting it fester, and fixing it starts with bringing Gweyr back so she can catch up on the twenty years she missed with her son and daughter. Is it going to be perfect and everything's going to be fine once she's back in the Hound? No, of course not. But at least everyone's going to have to confront the matter and start working on patching things up, for the sake of the next generation if nothing else. The sons shouldn't have to pay for the sins of the fathers, as the saying goes. "Nice speech there, [pc.name]. Now, Garth, what [pc.heShe] means is that we're going to go in the back with our children and do some catching up," Gweyr adds, catching her husband by the scruff of his neck. "And you've got some explaining to do, like [jaelyn.isMaid|why you've got a pale elf waitress here, and just why she's wearing my old maid outfit|the state you've let the sign fall into all these years when I wasn't around to bother you with it]." ...And that's it. With all of the family out back, the show's over, although you can hear raised voices coming from the backyard, muffled as they are. There's the temptation to do more, but you've already done plenty by convincing Gweyr to come home and Sanders to step aside. The rest is truly up to them to sort out, and judging by the ruckus caucus that's going on they're well on their way to doing just that. While you don't expect this family to sort out all its dysfunctions in a day or even a year, the important thing is that they've made a start on it. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona atugia azyrran quintillus kiyoko etheryn |"All's well that ends well, eh?" Cait gives you a weak grin and wipes her brow. "For a moment there — well, a couple of moments — I thought it was really touch and go. That bit with Sanders, and when Gwyn looked like she was fit to burst — I thought it was all going to break down there, and a fight would've been the least of it." Oh, it would've been the least of it all right, but sometimes you've got to rip off the scab to let the wound heal. "It just goes to remind me how thankful I should be to have had a mom and dad who cared for me with everything they had, even if the latter wasn't always around. He may have had to travel on business so often, but I never doubted that he'd be there for me and Mom if either of us ever needed him." |"All's well that ends well, eh?" Brint gives you a weak grin and wipes his brow with the back of his hand. "That could've gone a lot worse if Sanders or Gwyn had decided to press the issue and had gotten handsy." It was a risk you were willing to take not just for Gweyr, but her kids' sakes as well. Well worth it, otherwise you wouldn't have started this whole chain of events to begin with. "Yeah, I know it's got to be worth it, and yes, it did come close a couple of times. But..." he pauses and muses a moment, scratching his chin. "Y'know, I can't blame Gwyn, even if she took things a little further than I'd have done. If my dad just showed up at my doorstep one day, I'd have a handful of questions that'd need answering, too. "It's like that kind of stuff that Rags always liked to read to Hretha." Well, it's not quite a happy ending, if that's what bothers her. There's still a lot this family needs to work through, and the baggage of twenty years isn't going to be cleared up in a single night. "Y'know what I think would've been more interesting? If a fight had broken out, either with that old priest or the daughter. What? Don't look at me like that — I'm not saying that it'd have been any better, I'm just saying it would've been more interesting, that's all. You can't deny that." Interesting for Arona, maybe. Does she ever think about her parents, wherever they may be? Arona shrugs. "Look, let's just say that I'd want my kids to remember me in my prime. Strong, young, beating in someone's head. Not old and weathered like that woman... she might've even been worthy of looking up to, once. Now, she's just beaten and going to be living out the rest of her years, waiting for a straw death." You shake your head at that, noting that Arona neatly evaded the question about her parents and making a note to press her on it sometime. Oh no, no. If anything, Gweyr's true battle has only just begun. |"Looks like it all ended just peachy, didn't it?" Atugia says, watching Gweyr drag Garth off. "I was a little worried there — Carmen always didn't like it when people fought, least of all those she considered her own." Does she think that even knowing everything that Gweyr did, that the baroness would consider the wolfess one of her own? Tui thinks this over for a bit. "I'd say so. Maybe she made a mistake or two, but she did it in the defense of the town; if Carmen was going to find fault with her for that, then she'd be a hypocrite." Just what were the details of this thing that the baroness did anyway that were so bad to even surpass Gweyr's mass slaughter? "That's her story to tell, not mine. Sorry, but I don't have that right." Well, if she says so... |"What a happy family," Azyrran says with a sigh as she watches Gweyr drag Garth off out back. "There's a lot of mending that needs to be done there." She speaks the truth, yeah. Still, you think that all this was for the best, and that it went surprisingly well given that neither Sanders nor Gwyn actually came to blows with her. There's hope yet. Azyrran chuckles, a forced laugh, then looks a bit melancholic. "The girl, I can empathize with her. In the days that I couldn't return home to the hive, the thought that I might've lost my mother and sisters forever was always a weight on my heart. To imagine that it would've stretched on for twenty years... even knowing that it wasn't her fault, I'd have been sorely tested. But if I did believe that my mother had abandoned me, like the girl does... oh, I would've been furious." Like she said, there's a lot of mending that needs to be done there. The absence of her mother has undoubtedly damaged Gwyn, and to make things worse you're not entirely sure if it's Gweyr she actually hates, or more an image of her mother that she's built up over the years. More the latter, you'd imagine, but... "We'll see. We'll see. If nothing else, it'll spice up things around the tavern while I'm not out and about with you. That there is one screwed up family... and it's a big lesson as to how your actions affect people other than you. Like you said, there's a lot of mending that needs to be done there. It came close a couple of times with Sanders and Gwyn, but it's a good thing no one actually came to blows. Sets a good precedent for things going forward and all. "I sincerely hope the old woman will be able to mend things with her daughter," your fox-wife says. "Family is important, after all. Given that the daughter in question did not so much as remember her mother's face, I am heavily of the opinion that she does not truly resent her mother to begin with, but rather a caricature of her that the girl has built in her mind. That could make things harder... she has invested so much of her identity in resenting her mother." To stop hating Gweyr, Gwyn would have to examine herself and reassess who she is — something a lot of people don't have the introspection or emotional fortitude for. But with her family helping her, maybe she can finally come around to her mother being home. "It is a good thing our daughter is much better in the way of temperament, is it not?" Kiyoko chuckles. "Ah, I am sorry. Perhaps that hit a little too close to home. But it is good that your friend has his family reunited; I am sure that this is for the best." |"It's great to see Garth and his family finally reunited," Ryn says as she eyes Gweyr dragging her husband out to be with their kids in the back. "He's put up with me, he's put up with you... bringing his wife back home is a small price to pay for everything he's done for us." Heh. With the way things are probably going down now, he's the one paying the price, it seems like. "Well, he dragged things out for so long... I can understand his fear, that hope for tomorrow to be the same as today, because you know you've lived through today. But if I'd managed to swallow my fear and gone to seek help earlier, the Winter City mightn't have descended to such a sorry state." If she'd gone to seek help earlier, she might not have run into you to begin with. "You know what I mean, [pc.name]. Been where he's been, I can't say I'm fully sorry for anything Garth might get in the near future, because his situation is partly of his own making. I'm not going to deny the same of myself, either." ]

|由于晚间的顾客们还没有聚集过来，所以公共休息室里的顾客并不多。不过，这也意味着当酒馆里陷入一片寂静时，那位老女巫就更容易吸引人们的注意了。不过，真正破坏这种氛围的，却是…… |公共休息室的状态还算不错，这对于“霜猎犬”来说也是意料之中的；当那位老女狼走进来时，房间里的活动丝毫没有停顿。不过，真正破坏这种氛围的，却是…… ] 事实上，站在吧台后面的是格温，而不是加思——她的脸上带着明显的怒容，这让人毫不怀疑她对母亲归来的态度。 [gwyn.isPregnant |尽管已经怀孕，格温还是迫不及待地从柜台后面走出来，摇摇摆摆地走到母亲跟前，用充满怒火的目光盯着她。将如此多的愤怒聚集在一个孕妇身上，这一对比确实令人感到震撼……但归根结底……这也并不奇怪，不是吗？ |格温露出一副凶狠的表情，立刻从柜台后面冲了出来，大步走到母亲面前，用充满敌意的目光盯着她。看到平时温顺的格温被这种纯粹的仇恨所吞噬，确实让人感到震撼……不过……这样的结果，其实从一开始就没什么悬念吧？ ] 原来你是这样的样子啊…… 敢 你怎么敢在这里出现？”格温怒吼道，她竭力让自己的语气听起来充满威胁性，同时却也在暗自强忍着泪水。 “你…… 敢！ 这些年来一直陪在爸爸身边的人是我！是我为他做饭、洗他的衣服、听他倾诉，而你——你究竟为他做了什么？” “我买下了你们所有人未来的时间，”格温尔平静地回答。 “我做不到…… 相信 你把我们三个人当作垃圾一样扔掉，现在表现得就像什么殉道者一样…… 多年我绝不会让你抢走达——” “格温妮丝，够了。” 格温看起来像是要尖叫出来，但她内心深处的顺从意识，尤其是对父亲的顺从，与听到加思的声音时在她心中涌动的愤怒产生了冲突。 nursery matron呻吟着，双手部捂住脸，开始哭泣起来。 “别在我面前哭鼻子，”加思一边说，一边走下猎犬楼层的最后一级台阶，“也别在顾客面前哭。 到后面去，我们稍后再解决这个问题。” 格温似乎没有听到父亲的话，又是一阵抽泣和呜咽之后，加勒特叹了口气，伸手部搭在妹妹的肩上，轻轻但坚定地带着她离开了现场。 那就只剩下加斯、格温尔和你了——当然，还有客厅里的其他所有人。 “我让我们的女儿去照看酒吧，自己则去打扫客房，结果却发生了这种事；你们还是像以前一样，总能制造出一些轰动的效果。 欢迎回家，不管这话有多么微不足道。” “我们的女儿……” “和她你一样，她也从来不会说谎。”格温尔摇着头，肩膀也随之耷了下来，这时加思转向了你：“那么， [pc.name]这么多年过去了，你终于把我的妻子带回了家。我想我应该为此感谢你，尽管我怀疑在这段时间里，我们在这个家里恐怕无法安宁地生活。” 那么，他就只好忍着吧。 这不仅仅关乎他、格温尔或桑德斯。你在鹰棘镇已经待了一段时间了，也应该听说过那些流传在村子里的谣言。作为所谓的村长，他本就不该对人们谈论他感到惊讶，更何况其中一些说法实在刻薄不堪。 另一方面，那些声称格温的第一窝幼崽的父亲要么是它自己，要么是加勒特的人——这种传言，如果一开始就听起来有点可信的话，确实会越传越广。 “是的，我听说过这种说法，还有很多其他的传言也是如此。 尽管这很痛苦，但这和我让妻子回到我身边有什么关系呢？ [pc.name]关键在于，责任最终要由这里来承担。没错，你们已经听到了关于二十年前发生的事情的各方说法。但事实上，你们认为根本没有人会真正被追究责任，因为坦白说，在那场混乱中，每个人其实都扮演了一定的角色。 但是，他们很久以前所做出的那些选择所带来的后果，不仅从那天起影响了他们自己的生活，也波及到了周围的人——比如加勒特和格温，甚至可能影响到整个鹰棘镇家族。和以前一样，没有人愿意承认这个显而易见的问题，任由它持续恶化，而要解决这个问题，首先就必须让格韦尔回来，这样她才能弥补与儿子和女儿错过的二十年时光。 当她重新回到“猎犬小队”后，一切真的会变得完美无缺吗？当然不会。但至少，为了下一代，每个人都必须正视这个问题，并开始努力修复其中的矛盾与问题。 俗话说，儿子们不应该为父亲的过错买单。 “说得真好， [pc.name]现在，加斯，接下来该做什么呢？ [pc.heShe] 也就是说，我们要带着孩子们去后面，把落下的功课补上，”格韦尔一边说，一边抓住丈夫的脖子。“而你，也有些事情需要解释清楚，对吧？ 年轻力壮，却被人肆意践踏。她并不像那个女人那样历经沧桑……或许曾经，她甚至值得人们敬仰。如今，她只是被摧残了，接下来只能孤独地度过余生，等待着那个决定她命运的最后一根稻草。你对此摇了摇头，注意到阿罗娜巧妙地避开了关于她父母的问题，于是决定改日再追问她。哦不，不……如果说有什么不同的话，那么格韦尔的真正战斗才刚刚开始而已。
